title: Observation Of Genuine Tripartite Non-Gaussian Entanglement From A Superconducting Three-Photon Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion Source
authors: Benjamin Jarvis-Frain, Andy Schang, Fernando Quijandría, Ibrahim Nsanzineza, Dmytro Dubyna, C. W. Sandbo Chang, Franco Nori, And C. M. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Jarvis-Frain, Andy Schang, Fernando Quijandría, Ibrahim Nsanzineza, Dmytro Dubyna, C. W. Sandbo Chang, Franco Nori, and C. M. Wilson

The generation of entangled photons through spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is a critical resource for many key experiments and technologies in the domain of quantum optics. Historically, SPDC was limited to the generation of photon pairs. However, the use of the strong nonlinearities …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of genuine tripartite non-Gaussian entanglement from a superconducting three-photon SPDC source.
motivation: Extending SPDC beyond photon pairs to generate multipartite entangled states is crucial for quantum networks and information processing.
method: Using a superconducting circuit with strong nonlinearities to realize three-photon SPDC, then characterizing the output via homodyne tomography and entanglement witnesses.
result: Demonstrated genuine tripartite non-Gaussian entanglement, confirmed by a witness based on third-order moments.
conclusion: This work establishes a scalable source of multipartite non-Gaussian entanglement, relevant for quantum communication and computation.

title: Timescale For Macroscopic Equilibration In Isolated Quantum Systems: A Rigorous Derivation For Free Fermions
authors: Takashi Hara And Tatsuhiko Koike
abstract:
Author(s): Takashi Hara and Tatsuhiko Koike

For a class of translation-invariant free-fermion systems including those with uniform nearest-neighbor hopping) on a [MATH]-dimensional [MATH] hypercubic lattice, we prove that, starting from an arbitrary pure initial state, the system equilibrates with respect to the coarse-grained density within a …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030406] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously derives the timescale for macroscopic equilibration in translation-invariant free-fermion systems, showing that equilibration occurs within a timescale proportional to the system size.
motivation: Understanding how isolated quantum systems equilibrate is a fundamental question in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, with implications for thermalization and the foundations of statistical mechanics.
method: The authors consider a class of translation-invariant free-fermion models on a hypercubic lattice and prove equilibration of coarse-grained density using rigorous mathematical techniques, likely involving bounds on correlation functions or dynamical typicality.
result: They prove that starting from an arbitrary pure initial state, the system equilibrates with respect to coarse-grained density within a timescale that scales with the system size, providing a rigorous estimate for the equilibration time.
conclusion: The work establishes a rigorous foundation for equilibration timescales in free-fermion systems, contributing to the theoretical understanding of quantum thermalization and non-equilibrium dynamics.

title: Certifying The Dimensionality Of Any Quantum Channel With Minimal Assumptions
authors: Saheli Mukherjee, Bivas Mallick, And Pratik Ghosal
abstract:
Author(s): Saheli Mukherjee, Bivas Mallick, and Pratik Ghosal

High-dimensional entanglement offers significant advantages over its low-dimensional counterpart in various information-processing tasks. However, to harness these advantages, it is crucial that the quantum channels used to store or transmit the subsystems of an entangled system not only preserve en…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012445] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to certify the dimensionality of quantum channels with minimal assumptions, using high-dimensional entanglement.
motivation: High-dimensional entanglement offers advantages, but requires channels that preserve entanglement dimensionality; existing certification methods rely on assumptions about the channel.
method: The authors propose a device-independent-like protocol that certifies the channel dimension using only the statistics of measurements on an entangled state shared through the channel.
result: The protocol provides a lower bound on the channel dimension that is robust to noise and requires no assumptions about the internal workings of the channel.
conclusion: This work enables reliable certification of high-dimensional quantum channels, which is crucial for quantum communication and information processing.

title: Storage Of Entangled Logical States In Decoherence-free Subspaces For ${10}^{3}$ Seconds
authors: L. Zhang, Y.-L. Xu, Y.-K. Wu, C. Zhang, Z.-B. Cui, Y.-Y. Chen, W.-Q. Lian, J.-Y. Ma, B.-X. Qi, Y.-F. Pu, Z.-C. Zhou, L. He, P.-Y. Hou, And L.-M. Duan
abstract:
Author(s): L. Zhang, Y.-L. Xu, Y.-K. Wu, C. Zhang, Z.-B. Cui, Y.-Y. Chen, W.-Q. Lian, J.-Y. Ma, B.-X. Qi, Y.-F. Pu, Z.-C. Zhou, L. He, P.-Y. Hou, and L.-M. Duan

The maintenance of quantum entanglement lays the elementary building block of quantum information processing, requiring an integration of long coherence time, sufficient storage capacity, and high-fidelity entangling gates. Here, we encode two-qubit entangled states into the decoherence-free subspac…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012448] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates storage of entangled logical states in decoherence-free subspaces for over 1000 seconds using trapped ions.
motivation: Long-lived entanglement is essential for quantum information processing, but decoherence limits storage time. Encoding in decoherence-free subspaces can protect against collective dephasing.
method: Two-qubit entangled states are encoded into decoherence-free subspaces of trapped ions, and their coherence is maintained using dynamical decoupling and optimized control.
result: Entanglement is preserved for up to 10^3 seconds with high fidelity, significantly exceeding previous benchmarks.
conclusion: Decoherence-free subspace encoding combined with active control enables storage of quantum entanglement on timescales relevant for quantum networks and memory.

title: Finite-time Thermal Refrigerator In Interacting Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, And Pablo D. Mininni
abstract:
Author(s): Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, and Pablo D. Mininni

We study a finite-time thermodynamic refrigeration cycle realized numerically in three-dimensional, weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs). The setup consists of three spatially separated condensates (system, piston, and reservoir) coupled through time-dependent potential barriers that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013315] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies a finite-time refrigeration cycle using three interacting Bose-Einstein condensates, demonstrating cooling below the bath temperature.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic cycles in quantum systems is crucial for developing quantum thermal machines; here the focus is on a refrigerator operating with interacting BECs in finite time.
method: The authors simulate three spatially separated BECs (system, piston, reservoir) coupled via time-dependent potential barriers, implementing a refrigeration cycle and measuring heat flows and temperature changes.
result: The cycle achieves cooling of the system below the reservoir temperature, with performance characterized by coefficient of performance and cooling power, showing dependence on interaction strength and cycle duration.
conclusion: Interacting BECs can serve as working substances for finite-time quantum refrigerators, with performance tunable via interactions and cycle parameters.

title: Trajectory-independent Speed Limits For Controlled Open Quantum Systems
authors: James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, And Christian Arenz
abstract:
Author(s): James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, and Christian Arenz

Existing quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems depend on the specified trajectory. For example, lower bounds on quantum annealing times in the presence of dissipation depend explicitly on the chosen annealing schedule. Recently, schedule-independent speed limits have been derived …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012439] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives trajectory-independent quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems, providing fundamental bounds on evolution time that depend only on initial and final states.
motivation: Existing quantum speed limits for open systems depend on the control trajectory, making them less useful for optimization. The authors aim to find bounds that are independent of the path taken.
method: Using information-theoretic tools and the geometry of quantum states, they derive speed limits based on the Bures angle and the quantum Fisher information, applicable to general Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics.
result: They obtain lower bounds on the time required to evolve between two states that do not depend on the intermediate trajectory, and show these bounds are tight for certain cases.
conclusion: Trajectory-independent speed limits provide fundamental constraints on quantum control and thermodynamics, with implications for quantum annealing and quantum computing.

title: General Concurrence Percolation On Quantum Networks
authors: Deep Nath And Soumen Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Deep Nath and Soumen Roy

A quantum network is a network of entangled states which can be used to transmit quantum information. Nonmaximally entangled states are not really effective in establishing quantum communication across vast distances. Creating and maintaining a maximally entangled state over which quantum informatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012440] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies percolation of concurrence in quantum networks, analyzing how entanglement can be distributed across large-scale networks using non-maximally entangled states.
motivation: Quantum communication over long distances requires distributing entanglement, but non-maximally entangled states are inefficient. Understanding percolation of concurrence can help design better quantum network protocols.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for concurrence percolation, modeling quantum networks as graphs where edges represent entangled states with given concurrence, and analyze the percolation threshold and entanglement distribution probability.
result: They find that concurrence percolation exhibits a phase transition and that the percolation threshold depends on the initial entanglement and network topology, with implications for optimal network design.
conclusion: Concurrence percolation provides a useful tool for understanding and optimizing entanglement distribution in quantum networks, especially for non-maximally entangled resources.

title: Analytical Construction Of $(n,$ $n−1)$-quantum Random Access Codes Saturating The Conjectured Bound
authors: Takayuki Suzuki
abstract:
Author(s): Takayuki Suzuki

Quantum Random Access Codes (QRACs) embody the fundamental trade-off between the compressibility of information into limited quantum resources and the accessibility of that information, serving as a cornerstone of quantum communication and computation. In particular, the [MATH]-QRACs, which encod…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012441] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically constructs (n, n-1)-quantum random access codes that saturate the conjectured bound, providing optimal trade-offs between encoding and decoding.
motivation: Quantum Random Access Codes (QRACs) are fundamental for understanding the trade-off between information compression and accessibility in quantum communication. The (n, n-1)-QRACs represent a key case where the optimal bound was only conjectured.
method: The author uses analytical constructions based on mutually unbiased bases and symmetric informationally complete measurements to achieve the optimal success probability.
result: The constructed QRACs saturate the conjectured bound, proving its optimality for all n.
conclusion: This work provides a complete characterization of (n, n-1)-QRACs, advancing the theory of quantum communication complexity.

title: Hybrid Single-ion Atomic-ensemble Node For High-rate Remote Entanglement Generation
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

The authors propose to generate entanglement between trapped ions and broadband photons compatible with ensemble-based memories using spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources. Overcoming the bandwidth mismatch between these systems can provide a hybrid quantum network architecture that combines ensemble-based multiplexed entanglement generation and deterministic ion gates, resulting in a significant speed-up in establishing remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010602] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum network node combining trapped ions and atomic ensembles to achieve high-rate remote entanglement generation over long distances.
motivation: Current quantum network architectures suffer from bandwidth mismatch between deterministic ion gates and ensemble-based memories, limiting entanglement generation rates.
method: The authors design a hybrid node using spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources to bridge the bandwidth gap, enabling multiplexed entanglement generation with deterministic ion gates.
result: The proposed architecture significantly speeds up remote ion-ion entanglement generation over hundreds of kilometers compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: This hybrid node design offers a practical path toward scalable quantum networks by combining the strengths of different quantum platforms.

title: Accelerated Relaxation And Mpemba-like Effect For Operators In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:
Author(s): Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, and Bijay Kumar Agarwalla

The quantum Mpemba effect occurs when a quantum system, residing far away from the steady state, relaxes faster than a relatively nearer state. We look for the presence of this highly counterintuitive effect in the relaxation dynamics of the operators within the open quantum system setting. Since th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010601] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the quantum Mpemba effect in the relaxation dynamics of operators in open quantum systems, showing that initial states farther from steady state can relax faster.
motivation: The quantum Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive phenomenon where a system farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than one closer. Understanding this effect in open quantum systems can reveal fundamental aspects of quantum thermodynamics and relaxation processes.
method: The authors study operator relaxation in open quantum systems using a Lindblad master equation approach, analyzing the time evolution of observables and comparing relaxation rates for different initial states.
result: They demonstrate the existence of an accelerated relaxation and Mpemba-like effect for operators, where certain initial operator states exhibit faster relaxation despite being farther from the steady state.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and suggest that the Mpemba effect is a general feature of open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Superextensive Charging Speeds In A Correlated Quantum Charger
authors: Harald Schmid, Felix von Oppen, Gil Refael, And Yang Peng
abstract:
Author(s): Harald Schmid, Felix von Oppen, Gil Refael, and Yang Peng

We define a quantum charger as an interacting quantum system that transfers energy between two drives. The key figure of merit characterizing a charger is its charging power. Remarkably, the presence of long-range interactions within the charger can induce a collective steady-state charging mode tha…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014313] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that long-range interactions in a quantum charger can lead to superextensive charging power, a collective effect that enhances energy transfer speed.
motivation: Understanding how interactions affect the charging speed of quantum batteries is crucial for developing fast and efficient quantum energy storage devices.
method: The authors model a quantum charger as an interacting quantum system and analyze its charging power using a collective steady-state charging mode induced by long-range interactions.
result: They find that the charging power scales superextensively with system size, surpassing the linear scaling expected from non-interacting systems.
conclusion: Long-range interactions can be harnessed to significantly boost charging speeds in quantum chargers, offering a pathway to high-power quantum batteries.

title: Non-Abelian Geometric Quantum Energy Pump
authors: Yang Peng
abstract:
Author(s): Yang Peng

We introduce a non-Abelian geometric quantum energy pump realized by a transitionless geometric quantum drive—a time-dependent Hamiltonian supplemented by a counterdiabatic term generated by a prescribed trajectory on a smooth control manifold—that coherently transports states within a degenerate su…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020304] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: A non-Abelian geometric quantum energy pump is realized using a transitionless geometric drive, enabling coherent energy transport within degenerate subspaces.
motivation: To explore geometric effects in quantum thermodynamics and achieve robust energy pumping without dissipation.
method: A time-dependent Hamiltonian with a counterdiabatic term is designed to follow a prescribed trajectory on a control manifold, ensuring adiabaticity and geometric phase accumulation.
result: The pump coherently transports energy within degenerate subspaces, demonstrating non-Abelian geometric effects in a thermodynamic context.
conclusion: This work bridges geometric quantum control and quantum thermodynamics, offering a new mechanism for energy manipulation at the quantum scale.

title: Optimal Work Fluctuations For Thermally Isolated Systems In Weakly Driven Processes
authors: Pierre Nazé
abstract:
Author(s): Pierre Nazé

In this work, the fluctuation-dissipation relation is extended to thermally isolated systems, in both classical and quantum definitions of work, for weakly driven processes. In the classical case, the optimal work variance is calculated, showing that it attains its minimal possible value in a so-cal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014142] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Extends fluctuation-dissipation relation to thermally isolated systems and derives optimal work fluctuations for weakly driven processes.
motivation: Understanding work fluctuations in small systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and designing efficient nanoscale heat engines.
method: Analytical derivation using linear response theory and fluctuation theorems for both classical and quantum definitions of work.
result: Optimal work variance is achieved in a so-called 'quasi-static' limit, with explicit expressions for the minimal variance.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental bounds on work fluctuations in thermally isolated systems, with implications for thermodynamic uncertainty relations.

title: Fluctuation-response Relation For A Nonequilibrium System With Resolved Markovian Embedding
authors: Rémi Goerlich, Antoine Tartar, Yael Roichman, And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Rémi Goerlich, Antoine Tartar, Yael Roichman, and Igor M. Sokolov

Fluctuation-response relations must be modified to describe nonequilibrium systems with non-Markovian dynamics. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that such relation is quantitatively recovered when the appropriate Markovian embedding of the dynamics is explicitly resolved. Using a colloidal partic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014138] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration that fluctuation-response relations for non-Markovian nonequilibrium systems are recovered by explicitly resolving the Markovian embedding of the dynamics.
motivation: Fluctuation-response relations are fundamental in equilibrium but break down in nonequilibrium systems with memory. A theoretical framework using Markovian embedding was proposed to restore them, but experimental verification was lacking.
method: A colloidal particle in a non-Markovian optical trap is used as a model system. The dynamics are analyzed by explicitly resolving the hidden degrees of freedom that make the process Markovian in an extended space, and the fluctuation-response relation is tested.
result: The fluctuation-response relation is quantitatively recovered when the Markovian embedding is resolved, confirming the theoretical prediction.
conclusion: The work provides experimental validation of a general approach to extend fluctuation-response relations to non-Markovian nonequilibrium systems, with implications for understanding thermodynamics in complex environments.

title: Restoring Detailed Balance In non-Hermitian Markov Processes
authors: Tim van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, And Christophe Deroulers
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, and Christophe Deroulers

Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often involve asymmetric contributions that break detailed balance and lead to nonmonotonic entropy production, limiting thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques. Here we use Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in those processes, allo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014131] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in non-Hermitian Markov processes, enabling thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques.
motivation: Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often break detailed balance, leading to nonmonotonic entropy production that limits thermodynamic interpretations and inference. The authors aim to restore monotonic entropy growth to enable standard thermodynamic analysis.
method: The authors apply Dyson maps to non-Hermitian Markov processes, transforming them into Hermitian ones to restore detailed balance and monotonic entropy production.
result: The Dyson map approach successfully restores monotonic entropy growth, allowing for thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques in previously problematic out-of-equilibrium processes.
conclusion: The method provides a way to apply thermodynamic concepts to a broader class of stochastic processes, potentially advancing the understanding of non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Work And Heat Exchanged During Sudden Quenches Of Strongly Coupled Quantum Systems
authors: Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, And Nicole Yunger Halpern
abstract:
Author(s): Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, and Nicole Yunger Halpern

The authors examine three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat that have been used for quantum systems coupled strongly to the environment. Their study focuses on quenches, processes in which the Hamiltonian changes abruptly. In these processes, the first law of thermodynamics holds for each set of definitions by construction. The authors show that only two sets of definitions obey the second law. They illustrate their findings with a model of two coupled spins.

#ClearMotivation #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014133] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper examines three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat for strongly coupled quantum systems during sudden quenches, showing that only two sets obey the second law.
motivation: Strongly coupled quantum systems lack a universally accepted definition of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat, which is essential for understanding quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze three sets of definitions for internal energy, work, and heat in the context of sudden quenches, and test them against the first and second laws of thermodynamics using a two-spin model.
result: All three definitions satisfy the first law by construction, but only two of them obey the second law, indicating that not all definitions are thermodynamically consistent.
conclusion: The study provides guidance on choosing appropriate thermodynamic definitions for strongly coupled quantum systems, advancing the field of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Unified Speed Limits In Classical And Quantum Dynamics Via Temporal Fisher Information
authors: Tomohiro Nishiyama And Yoshihiko Hasegawa
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Nishiyama and Yoshihiko Hasegawa

The importance of Fisher information is increasing in nonequilibrium thermodynamics, as it has played a fundamental role in trade-off relations such as thermodynamic uncertainty relations and speed limits. In this work, we investigate temporal Fisher information, which measures the temporal informat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014120] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper unifies classical and quantum speed limits using temporal Fisher information, establishing a fundamental trade-off between the rate of change of a system and its Fisher information.
motivation: Speed limits are crucial in thermodynamics and quantum information, but a unified framework for classical and quantum systems was lacking. The authors aim to derive a general bound using Fisher information.
method: The authors define temporal Fisher information for both classical and quantum dynamics and prove that the speed of state change is bounded by the square root of the Fisher information. They apply this to various systems, including Markovian and unitary dynamics.
result: They obtain a unified speed limit that holds for both classical and quantum systems, recovering known bounds like the Mandelstam-Tamm bound and thermodynamic speed limits as special cases.
conclusion: Temporal Fisher information provides a universal measure of speed in dynamics, offering a new perspective on speed limits and their connections to thermodynamics and quantum mechanics.

title: Enhanced Tripartite Interaction In A magnon-Andreev-superconducting Qubit Hybrid System: Collapse-revival Phenomena And Entanglement Redistribution
authors: Sheng Zhao And Peng-Bo Li
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhao and Peng-Bo Li

Tripartite interactions are fundamental for realizing quantum phenomena beyond pairwise physics, yet their native implementation—particularly among distinct quantum systems—remains challenging. Here, we propose a hybrid quantum architecture comprising a magnonic mode [in a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033074] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid system of magnon, Andreev qubit, and superconducting qubit to realize enhanced tripartite interactions, demonstrating collapse-revival and entanglement redistribution.
motivation: Native tripartite interactions among distinct quantum systems are challenging but crucial for quantum phenomena beyond pairwise physics.
method: The authors design a hybrid architecture coupling a magnonic mode in YIG, an Andreev qubit, and a superconducting qubit, and analyze the dynamics using a quantum master equation.
result: They observe collapse-revival phenomena in the tripartite entanglement and show that entanglement can be redistributed among the three subsystems.
conclusion: This work provides a viable platform for studying multipartite quantum effects and may enable applications in quantum information processing with hybrid systems.

title: Single- And Double-click High-rate Entanglement Generation Between Distant Ions Using Multiplexed Atomic Ensembles
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

In an accompanying paper [B. Tissot et al.,
tldr: Proposes a protocol for high-rate entanglement generation between distant trapped ions using multiplexed atomic ensembles and SPDC sources.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks by efficiently generating entanglement between remote quantum processors (trapped ions) using ensemble-based quantum memories.
method: Uses a spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) source to interface trapped ions with multiplexed atomic ensembles, employing single-click and double-click entanglement generation schemes.
result: Achieves high entanglement generation rates by leveraging multiplexing and memory-enhanced coincidence detection, overcoming limitations of direct photon-mediated entanglement.
conclusion: The proposed approach significantly improves the rate of remote entanglement generation, making it viable for practical quantum network nodes.

title: Partially Device-independent Quantum Cryptography In Asymmetric Networks
authors: Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, And Kai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, and Kai Chen

Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation between distant users, yet its standard device-dependent implementations rely on fully characterized and accurately modeled devices. Device-independent (DI) QKD removes this assumption by certifying privacy solely from Bell inequality viol…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033060] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a partially device-independent QKD protocol tailored for asymmetric networks, achieving high key rates with minimal trust assumptions.
motivation: Standard device-independent QKD requires symmetric Bell tests, which are inefficient in asymmetric networks. The authors aim to extend DI-QKD to realistic asymmetric scenarios while maintaining security.
method: They introduce a protocol where only one party performs a Bell test, while the other uses a simpler measurement, and prove security using the entropy accumulation theorem.
result: The protocol achieves positive key rates over asymmetric distances (e.g., 10 km vs. 50 km) and outperforms fully device-independent approaches in such settings.
conclusion: Partially device-independent QKD is a practical and secure solution for asymmetric quantum networks, bridging the gap between theory and implementation.

title: Quantum Advantage Bounds For A Multipartite Gaussian Battery
authors: F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, And M. Sassetti
abstract:
Author(s): F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, and M. Sassetti

We demonstrate the possibility of a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of quantum batteries by analyzing a model that enables a consistent comparison between quantum and classical regimes. Our system consists of [MATH] harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033045] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of a multipartite Gaussian battery, modeled as harmonic oscillators coupled to a common thermal reservoir.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but a consistent comparison between quantum and classical regimes is needed to establish genuine quantum advantage.
method: The authors analyze a model of N harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving under a charging protocol, and compare the charging power and efficiency in the quantum vs. classical (mean-field) regime.
result: They find that quantum correlations (entanglement) lead to a superlinear scaling of charging power with N, providing a clear quantum advantage in efficiency that persists even in the presence of thermal noise.
conclusion: The results establish a genuine quantum advantage for multipartite Gaussian batteries, highlighting the role of entanglement in enhancing energy storage performance.

title: Operational Coherent Measurements With Steering And Randomness
authors: Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, And Hsi-Sheng Goan
abstract:
Author(s): Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, and Hsi-Sheng Goan

Measurement incompatibility underpins randomness generation in nonlocal phenomena. However, at its root, a more fundamental quantum feature is noncommuting (or coherent) measurements. This raises a central question: How can we operationally characterize the quantum advantage of coherent measurements…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033054] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper operationally characterizes the quantum advantage of coherent measurements through steering and randomness generation, linking measurement incompatibility to nonlocality.
motivation: Measurement incompatibility is known to underpin randomness generation in nonlocal phenomena, but the more fundamental role of coherent (noncommuting) measurements has not been operationally characterized.
method: The authors develop a framework using quantum steering and randomness certification to quantify the advantage provided by coherent measurements over classical ones.
result: They show that coherent measurements enable stronger steering and higher randomness generation rates than any incompatible but non-coherent measurements, establishing a clear operational distinction.
conclusion: Coherent measurements are a key resource for quantum information tasks, and their advantage can be certified via steering and randomness.

title: Quantum Advantage In Distributed Sensing With Noisy Quantum Networks
authors: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, And Zain H. Saleem
abstract:
Author(s): Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, and Zain H. Saleem

We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks that only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033040] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved using noisy quantum networks that distribute noisy entangled states, deriving a closed-form expression for quantum Fisher information.
motivation: Distributed sensing with quantum networks promises enhanced precision, but practical networks are noisy; it is unclear if quantum advantage persists under realistic noise.
method: The authors derive a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using GHZ-like states in a noisy network, and analyze the impact of noise on the QFI.
result: They show that quantum advantage is achievable even with noisy entanglement distribution, and provide explicit conditions on noise levels for which advantage holds.
conclusion: Noisy quantum networks can still enable quantum-enhanced distributed sensing, paving the way for practical implementations.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is essential for quantum networks but is fragile and requires active stabilization. The authors aim to achieve stable entanglement without active feedback.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two superconducting qubits are coupled via a common waveguide, and use a squeezed vacuum source to mimic a squeezed environment, enabling autonomous stabilization.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, maintained over extended periods despite imperfections.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization via squeezed environments is a viable approach for robust entanglement distribution in quantum networks.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust, high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two spatially separated superconducting qubits are coupled to a common squeezed microwave reservoir, which mediates stationary entanglement through a nonlocal dissipative process.
result: The autonomous process generates and maintains entanglement between the qubits, verified by experimental data.
conclusion: This approach offers a scalable and robust platform for entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores the vast landscape of quantum advantage across multiple domains, revealing a nuanced picture beyond simple speedups.
motivation: To systematically characterize and categorize the different types of quantum advantage that can arise in various computational and information-processing tasks.
method: The authors provide a conceptual framework and survey of known results, analyzing quantum advantage in terms of resources, complexity, and physical settings.
result: They identify a rich taxonomy of quantum advantages, including exponential, polynomial, and constant-factor improvements, as well as advantages in communication, sensing, and thermodynamics.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is multifaceted and context-dependent, with many forms beyond the standard computational speedup, offering broad opportunities for future research.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to generate remote entanglement. Tin-vacancy centers in diamond offer promising optical properties but achieving strong coupling has been challenging.
method: Fabricated high-quality photonic crystal cavities in diamond and coupled individual tin-vacancy centers to them. Measured cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling using resonant excitation and photon correlation techniques.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, demonstrating strong spin-photon coupling and efficient photon collection, which is a key milestone for entanglement generation.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in diamond photonic crystal cavities as a viable platform for high-fidelity entanglement in future quantum networks, advancing the practical implementation of quantum repeaters.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, introducing a criterion that separates classical and nonclassical processes.
result: The unified rule recovers standard quantum signatures (e.g., Bell nonlocality) and identifies new nonclassical behaviors in processes like entanglement swapping and quantum teleportation.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with many 'classical' processes possessing intrinsic quantumness that may be harnessed for quantum information tasks.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing useful entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via cavity loss to drive the system into desired entangled steady states, with reconfigurability through external drives.
result: They show that the dissipative protocol can generate various entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, topological states) with high fidelity and robustness against imperfections.
conclusion: The approach provides a scalable and practical platform for quantum sensing and many-body physics, leveraging dissipation as a tool rather than a hindrance.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can be resource-intensive; passive schemes could simplify implementation.
method: The authors design a bosonic code that corrects photon loss errors using continuous drives without active measurements, and experimentally demonstrate it.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the constituent components, reaching the breakeven point where error correction begins to improve performance.
conclusion: Passive error correction is a viable approach for protecting quantum information against photon loss, with potential for simpler hardware requirements.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with a security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem, achieving composable security against collective attacks.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km, with composable security guarantees.
conclusion: This work brings high-speed, secure quantum key distribution closer to practical deployment in quantum networks.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies and mitigates loss mechanisms in high-coherence multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence time and cooperativity.
motivation: Mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits are promising for quantum information processing, but their performance is limited by loss mechanisms that are not well understood.
method: The authors optimize piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators and characterize loss channels through systematic experiments and materials analysis.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, and provide a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding and performance of hybrid quantum systems involving mechanical resonators and superconducting circuits, enabling better quantum transducers and memory.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical Bell pairs, but existing methods have high overhead or require complex connectivity.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, combining multiple noisy physical Bell pairs and error correction to distill a logical Bell pair with improved fidelity, requiring only 2D local device connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly lower spacetime volume compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This work enables practical distributed quantum computation by reducing the resource overhead for logical Bell pair generation.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are limited.
method: A complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is developed to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification, and the method is experimentally validated on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum measurements and offers a practical tool for device certification.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a quantum detector operating autonomously.
method: The authors model a quantum particle as a detector that interacts with a system and a thermal bath, deriving bounds on entropy production and measurement accuracy using stochastic thermodynamics and information theory.
result: They find a trade-off relation between the entropy produced by the detector and the accuracy of the measurement, showing that higher accuracy requires more dissipation.
conclusion: The results establish fundamental thermodynamic limits on quantum measurement, with implications for the design of energy-efficient quantum sensors and autonomous quantum machines.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is essential for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on erbium ions coupled to silicon photonic crystal cavities, measuring spectral diffusion and coherence times under various conditions.
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the primary cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that operating at cryogenic temperatures and using specific cavity designs can significantly improve stability.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, with identified mitigation strategies paving the way for scalable quantum repeaters.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control. This work aims to overcome these challenges to generate large cluster states.
method: The authors propose a control framework that uses global driving and optical heralding to entangle inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and hole-burning techniques.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and scalability to 10–100 qubits with low experimental overhead, validated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward programmable quantum matter and large-scale cluster states for quantum information processing.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decodability of quantum codes under random monitoring, revealing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding performance.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in the context of monitored dynamics.
method: The authors analyze the stability of quantum codes under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics, using random monitoring protocols.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, providing new insights into the interplay between measurement and error correction.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes offer a promising avenue for improving quantum error correction, with potential applications in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: Device-independent quantum random number generation (DI-QRNG) provides security without trusting the hardware, but existing implementations are bulky and complex. An integrated photonic solution is needed for practical, scalable deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a self-testing protocol based on Bell inequality violation, using integrated entangled photon sources and on-chip detectors to generate and certify randomness.
result: The chip successfully generates certified randomness with a finite-size security proof, achieving a randomness generation rate suitable for real-world applications while maintaining device-independent security guarantees.
conclusion: This work demonstrates the feasibility of fully integrated DI-QRNG on a photonic chip, paving the way for compact, low-cost quantum security devices for widespread use.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the number of required emitters and improves the loss tolerance of quantum repeaters, making them more feasible for near-term implementation.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-codes offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with exceptional coherence and readout fidelity, positioning ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Current quantum platforms face challenges in scalability and coherence; wide-bandgap oxides like ZnO may offer new defect-based qubits with superior properties.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, evaluating electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: The defect exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, combining long coherence with practical readout capabilities.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume ideal devices, but real devices have imperfections that can compromise security. A rigorous framework is needed to account for device characterization in security proofs.
method: The authors develop a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization parameters, allowing for quantitative security guarantees based on measured device properties.
result: The framework yields rigorous security bounds that depend on device characterization, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and theoretically sound approach to bridge the gap between ideal security proofs and real-world QKD implementations.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement a dispersive readout scheme to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: They demonstrate that erasure conversion effectively suppresses the impact of energy relaxation, leading to enhanced effective coherence times.
conclusion: Erasure conversion in integer fluxonium qubits offers a practical path to improved quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter leads to inconsistencies; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to constrain possible theories.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing their feasibility and implications.
result: Several potentially feasible GIE experiments are identified, which could test the quantum nature of gravity without requiring high energies.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantum nature of gravity, with GIE experiments being a promising avenue.

title: Inverse Clausius Thermodynamics In Run-and-Tumble Dynamics
authors: Oded Farago
abstract:
Author(s): Oded Farago

We establish a mapping between one-dimensional run-and-tumble particle dynamics in the presence of thermal noise, and overdamped Brownian motion in a spatially inhomogeneous temperature field. The approach is formulated as an inverse-Clausius thermodynamic framework, where the effective temperature …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037103] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a mapping between run-and-tumble particle dynamics and Brownian motion in inhomogeneous temperature, formulating an inverse-Clausius thermodynamic framework.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamics of active matter systems, specifically run-and-tumble particles, which are out-of-equilibrium and exhibit complex behavior.
method: Derives an effective temperature description by mapping the run-and-tumble dynamics to overdamped Brownian motion with spatially varying temperature, using an inverse-Clausius approach.
result: The mapping yields an effective temperature that depends on the particle's self-propulsion speed and persistence time, allowing thermodynamic concepts to be applied to active systems.
conclusion: The inverse-Clausius framework provides a thermodynamic interpretation of active matter, bridging non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and traditional thermodynamics.

title: Non-Abelian Geometric Phases In Triangular Structures And Universal Su(2) Control In Shape Space
authors: J. Dai, A. Molochkov, A. J. Niemi, And J. Westerholm
abstract:
Author(s): J. Dai, A. Molochkov, A. J. Niemi, and J. Westerholm

We construct holonomic quantum gates for qubits that are encoded in the near-degenerate vibrational [MATH] doublet of a deformable three-body system. Using Kendall's shape theory, we derive the Wilczek-Zee connection that governs adiabatic transport within the [MATH] manifold. We show that its restricted …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012212] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs holonomic quantum gates for qubits encoded in the near-degenerate vibrational doublet of a deformable three-body system using Kendall's shape theory.
motivation: To realize universal quantum gates using non-Abelian geometric phases in a simple physical system, specifically a triangular molecule, without the need for complex control.
method: The authors use Kendall's shape theory to derive the Wilczek-Zee connection governing adiabatic transport within the degenerate manifold, and show that the shape space of a triangle provides a universal SU(2) control.
result: They demonstrate that any SU(2) gate can be implemented by adiabatically moving the triangular system along closed paths in shape space, with explicit constructions for single-qubit gates.
conclusion: This work provides a new platform for holonomic quantum computation using molecular vibrations, with potential for high-fidelity gates due to geometric protection.

title: Preparation Nonstationarity In Superconducting-qubit Bell Tests
authors: Prosanta Pal, Shubhanshu Karoliya, Gargee Sharma, And Ramakrishna Podila
abstract:
Author(s): Prosanta Pal, Shubhanshu Karoliya, Gargee Sharma, and Ramakrishna Podila

Bell or Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) tests on superconducting quantum processors are commonly interpreted under the assumption that repeated circuit executions sample a single, stationary-preparation ensemble. Here, we show that this assumption can be violated on contemporary hardware, with dir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012446] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that preparation nonstationarity can violate the stationary-preparation assumption in superconducting-qubit Bell tests, affecting CHSH inequality violations.
motivation: Bell tests on superconducting quantum processors typically assume a stationary-preparation ensemble, but this assumption may be invalid on current hardware, potentially undermining the validity of experimental tests.
method: The authors perform CHSH tests on a superconducting quantum processor and analyze the data for signs of preparation nonstationarity, showing that the assumption of a single stationary ensemble is violated.
result: They find direct evidence of preparation nonstationarity, which can lead to false violations or misinterpretations of Bell inequality tests.
conclusion: Preparation nonstationarity must be accounted for in Bell tests on superconducting qubits to ensure correct interpretation of nonlocality experiments.

title: Training The Classification Capability Of Large-scale Quantum Cellular Automata
authors: Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, and Igor Lesanovsky

In the vicinity of a phase transition ergodicity can be broken. Here, different initial many-body configurations evolve toward one of several fixed points, which are macroscopically distinguishable through an order parameter. This mechanism enables state classification in quantum cellular automata a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012209] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum cellular automata near a phase transition can classify initial states based on their order parameter, leveraging ergodicity breaking for computational tasks.
motivation: To explore how ergodicity breaking near phase transitions can be harnessed for state classification in quantum cellular automata, potentially enabling new computational paradigms.
method: The authors study a quantum cellular automaton model that exhibits a phase transition, analyzing the dynamics of different initial configurations and their convergence to fixed points characterized by an order parameter.
result: They show that the automaton can reliably classify initial states into distinct categories based on the order parameter, with the classification accuracy depending on the proximity to the critical point.
conclusion: Quantum cellular automata near phase transitions offer a novel mechanism for state classification, bridging many-body physics and information processing.

title: Long-term Stability Of Quantum Resources Through Gravitational Cat States In A Dissipative Markovian Environment
authors: Anas Ait Chlih And Tamer A. Seoudy
abstract:
Author(s): Anas Ait Chlih and Tamer A. Seoudy

The paradigm in which gravity can generate entanglement between distant masses represents a profound shift in our understanding of quantum-gravitational interfaces and is still among the active and debated topics. Recent work [A. ur Rahman et al.,
tldr: This paper investigates the long-term stability of quantum resources (entanglement, discord, coherence) in gravitational cat states under a dissipative Markovian environment.
motivation: Understanding how gravity affects quantum resources is crucial for quantum-gravitational interfaces, but the stability of these resources in realistic noisy environments is not well understood.
method: The authors model a gravitational cat state interacting with a dissipative Markovian environment and analyze the dynamics of entanglement, discord, and coherence using measures like concurrence and quantum discord.
result: They find that gravitational cat states can maintain quantum resources for longer times compared to standard cat states, with the gravitational interaction providing a stabilizing effect against decoherence.
conclusion: Gravitational cat states offer a promising platform for robust quantum information processing, as they exhibit enhanced resilience to environmental noise.

title: Stroboscopic Saturation Of Multiparameter Quantum Limits In Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: Berihu Teklu And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Berihu Teklu and Victor Montenegro

A naturally multiparameter sensing scenario arises in spatially distributed networks of quantum sensors, where each node probes a distinct parameter of interest. In such settings, the central challenges are to achieve quantum-enhanced sensitivity under well-defined resource constraints and to explic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033053] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies multiparameter quantum sensing in distributed networks, deriving fundamental limits and showing that stroboscopic control can saturate the quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing networks face challenges in achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity under resource constraints, especially when multiple parameters are estimated simultaneously.
method: The authors employ quantum estimation theory, specifically the multiparameter quantum Cramér-Rao bound, and analyze a stroboscopic measurement strategy that alternates between sensing and control pulses.
result: They demonstrate that stroboscopic control can saturate the multiparameter quantum limits, achieving Heisenberg scaling in precision for certain parameter combinations.
conclusion: Stroboscopic control is an effective technique for optimizing multiparameter estimation in distributed quantum sensors, with potential applications in quantum metrology and networks.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate quantum computational advantage in a programmable ultracold-atom platform, which is a key milestone for hybrid quantum systems.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely employing techniques such as optical lattices or Rydberg interactions to generate and control entanglement.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable, meaning the simulation outperforms classical methods for a relevant task.
conclusion: The ultracold-atom processor is a viable platform for demonstrating practical quantum advantage, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, leveraging the high-dimensional Hilbert space of nuclear qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated between nuclear memory qudits, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is universal and can be implemented in various defect center platforms, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.
