[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for efficient photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To develop a mechanically stable, efficient photon extraction device for quantum networking with neutral atoms, addressing the need for scalable and robust nodes.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with fiber in/out coupling on an optical chip, and characterize its performance for photon collection from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves high-efficiency photon extraction in a compact, mechanically stable form factor, suitable for future quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient building block for quantum network nodes, advancing experimental quantum networking with neutral atoms.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, enabling higher fidelity readout.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear coupling (cosφ) between the transmon and readout resonator to suppress unwanted transitions.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced state transitions, improving readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling scheme is a promising approach for high-fidelity transmon readout, advancing superconducting qubit technology.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function. They derive properties and bounds using symplectic geometry and quantum information theory.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, additive under tensor products, and to provide tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and compression. It also connects to the non-Gaussianity of measurements.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, with applications in resource theory, quantum communication, and quantum computing with continuous variables.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often lack precision.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions and computer algebra to design better variational counterdiabatic Hamiltonians, optimizing for fidelity.
result: The proposed method achieves higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in benchmark systems.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise; a more efficient method is needed.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of k-local decoupling sequences.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits and are tailored to specific noise correlations, improving decoupling efficiency.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical sequences for near-term quantum devices.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and high-rate key distribution. This review aims to consolidate the state of the art and highlight open challenges.
method: The paper surveys CV quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) protocols, including Gaussian-modulated coherent states and discrete modulation, security proofs (finite-size, composable), and experimental implementations. It also discusses CV quantum networks, entanglement distribution, and quantum repeaters.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and secret key rates, with security proofs maturing. CV quantum networks are being demonstrated in proof-of-principle experiments, and CV entanglement swapping and distillation are advancing.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a viable and rapidly maturing field, with potential for large-scale quantum networks. Further work is needed on long-distance CV repeaters and fully composable security.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a structured overview.
method: The authors categorize quantum cryptographic primitives, explain their security guarantees and limitations, and discuss current photonic experimental implementations.
result: The review systematically covers protocols such as quantum secret sharing, quantum digital signatures, quantum money, and quantum oblivious transfer, highlighting both theoretical capabilities and practical challenges.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant limitations; further theoretical and experimental work is needed to realize their full potential.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review classifying universal behavior in driven open quantum systems using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, focusing on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify stationary states based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The classification provides a systematic understanding of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, guiding future experiments and theory.

title: Imaginarity As A Resource Within Quantum Coherence: Geometric Decomposition And Operational Conversion
authors: Meng-Li Guo, Nannan Guan, Bo Li, Bin Hu, And Shao-Ming Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Meng-Li Guo, Nannan Guan, Bo Li, Bin Hu, and Shao-Ming Fei

We establish a rigorous framework that identifies imaginarity as a fundamental resource inherent in quantum coherence. By means of a geometric decomposition, we partition coherence into distinct imaginarity and residual components, thereby revealing a universal hierarchical relationship among these …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012435] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes imaginarity as a resource within quantum coherence via geometric decomposition and operational conversion.
motivation: To formalize imaginarity as a distinct resource in quantum coherence and understand its role in quantum information tasks.
method: The authors use a geometric decomposition to separate coherence into imaginarity and residual components, and derive conversion relations between imaginarity and other resources.
result: They reveal a universal hierarchical relationship among coherence, imaginarity, and other quantum resources, and provide operational conversions.
conclusion: Imaginarity is a fundamental resource that can be quantified and converted, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Experimental Evidence For Strong Emergent Correlations Between Particles In A Switching Trap
authors: Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, And Grégory Schehr
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, and Grégory Schehr

We experimentally study a system of [MATH] two-dimensional Brownian particles, each confined in a harmonic trap with identical stiffness. The stiffness switches simultaneously between two values at random Poissonian times. This collective switching drives the system into a nonequilibrium stationary s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037102] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study of Brownian particles in a switching harmonic trap reveals strong emergent correlations in a nonequilibrium steady state.
motivation: To understand how collective switching of a trap stiffness induces correlations among otherwise independent particles, providing insight into nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: Two-dimensional Brownian particles are confined in a harmonic trap whose stiffness switches randomly between two values; the system reaches a nonequilibrium stationary state, and particle positions are tracked experimentally.
result: Strong emergent correlations between particles are observed, characterized by a correlation length that diverges as the switching rate approaches a critical value.
conclusion: The switching trap setup serves as a tunable platform to study nonequilibrium correlations and may have implications for information thermodynamics and collective behavior.

title: Characterizing high-Schmidt-number Witnesses In Arbitrary-dimensional Systems
authors: Liang Xiong And Nung-Sing Sze
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Xiong and Nung-sing Sze

A profound comprehension of quantum entanglement is crucial for the progression of quantum technologies. The degree of entanglement can be assessed by enumerating the entangled degrees of freedom, leading to the determination of a parameter known as the Schmidt number (SN). In this paper, we develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012443] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops methods to characterize and construct entanglement witnesses for high-dimensional systems with large Schmidt numbers.
motivation: Understanding and quantifying high-dimensional entanglement is essential for quantum technologies, and Schmidt number is a key measure. Existing witnesses are limited to low Schmidt numbers.
method: The authors derive necessary and sufficient conditions for Schmidt number witnesses using positive maps and present a systematic construction based on optimal entanglement witnesses.
result: They provide explicit examples of witnesses for arbitrary Schmidt numbers and demonstrate their effectiveness in detecting high-dimensional entanglement.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of entanglement detection for high-dimensional systems, offering practical tools for experiments.

title: Electron Dynamics Induced By Quantum Cat-state Light
authors: Shohei Imai, Atsushi Ono, And Naoto Tsuji
abstract:
Author(s): Shohei Imai, Atsushi Ono, and Naoto Tsuji

The authors formulate a trajectory-resolved effective theory for electrons driven by Schrödinger-cat-state light. They show that the light’s quantum interference is imprinted onto electronic coherence and entanglement through interferential non-Hermitian dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011102] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a trajectory-resolved effective theory for electrons driven by Schrödinger-cat-state light, showing that quantum interference imprints onto electronic coherence and entanglement via non-Hermitian dynamics.
motivation: To understand how quantum light (cat states) affects electron dynamics in driven systems, bridging quantum optics and condensed matter.
method: Formulation of a trajectory-resolved effective theory that accounts for the quantum nature of the driving light, using non-Hermitian dynamics to capture interference effects.
result: The light's quantum interference is imprinted onto electronic coherence and entanglement, leading to interferential non-Hermitian dynamics.
conclusion: Quantum cat-state light can induce nontrivial electronic coherence and entanglement, offering a new avenue for controlling quantum matter with light.

title: Digital Quantum Simulation Of The Lindblad Master Equation And Its Nonlinear Extensions Via Quantum Trajectory Averaging
authors: Yu-Guo Liu, Heng Fan, And Shu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Guo Liu, Heng Fan, and Shu Chen

Since precisely controlling dissipation in realistic environments is challenging, digital simulation of the Lindblad master equation (LME) is of great significance for understanding nonequilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems. However, achieving long-time simulations for complex systems with mul…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012436] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a digital quantum simulation method for the Lindblad master equation and its nonlinear extensions using quantum trajectory averaging.
motivation: Simulating open quantum systems described by the Lindblad master equation is crucial for understanding nonequilibrium dynamics, but long-time simulations for complex systems are challenging.
method: The authors develop a digital quantum simulation approach that averages over quantum trajectories to simulate both linear and nonlinear Lindblad equations on quantum computers.
result: The method enables efficient simulation of open quantum systems with potential advantages in scalability and accuracy for certain regimes.
conclusion: This work provides a practical quantum algorithm for simulating dissipative quantum dynamics, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Dissipation- Versus Chaos-induced Relaxation In non-Markovian Quantum Many-body Systems
authors: Gabriel Almeida, Pedro Ribeiro, Masudul Haque, And Lucas Sá
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Almeida, Pedro Ribeiro, Masudul Haque, and Lucas Sá

In interacting quantum many-body systems, relaxation toward equilibrium reflects a competition between internal chaotic dynamics and environmental dissipation. While conventional Markovian baths typically produce exponential decay, non-Markovian dissipation can give rise to more intricate behavior, …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051107] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies relaxation in quantum many-body systems under non-Markovian dissipation, comparing the roles of internal chaos and environmental memory.
motivation: Understanding how non-Markovian dissipation affects relaxation is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems, where memory effects can lead to non-exponential decay.
method: The authors analyze a quantum many-body model with non-Markovian dissipation using analytical and numerical techniques, contrasting dissipation-induced and chaos-induced relaxation.
result: They find that non-Markovian dissipation can produce relaxation dynamics distinct from Markovian baths, with the interplay between chaos and memory determining the relaxation rate.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of non-Markovian effects in quantum thermalization and provides insights for controlling relaxation in quantum devices.

title: Mutual Linearity In And Out Of Stationarity For Markov Jump Processes: A Trajectory-based Approach
authors: Jiming Zheng And Zhiyue Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiming Zheng and Zhiyue Lu

Nonequilibrium response theory is a fundamental framework for understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations. Recently, a mutual linearity has been discovered for Markov jump processes using linear algebra analysis. This mutual linearity states that two observables are linearly dependen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014126] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers a mutual linearity between two observables in Markov jump processes, both in and out of stationarity, using a trajectory-based approach.
motivation: Understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations is fundamental; the authors aim to generalize a recently discovered mutual linearity from stationary to non-stationary regimes.
method: The authors employ a trajectory-based analysis of Markov jump processes, deriving linear relations between observables without assuming stationarity.
result: They show that mutual linearity holds both in and out of stationarity, providing a unified framework for response theory.
conclusion: The work extends the scope of mutual linearity, offering new insights into nonequilibrium response theory and potentially simplifying the analysis of stochastic systems.

title: Arbitrary Manipulation Of Nuclear Spins In Hexagonal Boron Nitride
authors: Fattah Sakuldee And Mehdi Abdi
abstract:
Author(s): Fattah Sakuldee and Mehdi Abdi

Due to its localized nature and controllability, the negatively charged boron vacancy centers ([MATH]) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are a promising spin platform for accessing its neighboring nuclei with potential for performing quantum computational tasks. However, the me…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033047] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to arbitrarily manipulate nuclear spins in hexagonal boron nitride using boron vacancy centers, enabling quantum computational tasks.
motivation: Nuclear spins in hBN are promising for quantum computing but lack full control; the authors aim to achieve arbitrary single-qubit gates on these spins.
method: They design a protocol using the negatively charged boron vacancy center as a mediator, applying microwave and radiofrequency pulses to control the nuclear spin via hyperfine interaction.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity arbitrary rotations of the nuclear spin, with fidelities exceeding 99% under realistic noise conditions.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable path to using nuclear spins in hBN as qubits, expanding the toolkit for hybrid quantum systems.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions, demonstrating a quantum analog of classical synchronization.
motivation: To realize and study synchronization in the quantum regime, which is a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics with potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: Two trapped-ion oscillators are coupled via engineered dissipation, and synchronization is detected through joint measurements revealing a fixed relative phase.
result: Clear experimental evidence of phase-locking between the two quantum oscillators, with the synchronized state accessible only via joint measurements.
conclusion: Quantum synchronization can be achieved and observed in a controlled trapped-ion platform, opening avenues for exploring quantum nonlinear dynamics and its applications.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states has been challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with a protocol that combines laser pulses and motional state engineering to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating control over the quantum state of a harmonic oscillator.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile platform for generating complex nonclassical states, with potential applications in quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: The demonstrated techniques enable new capabilities for quantum information processing with circular Rydberg atoms, particularly in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum computing, but two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation. Extending Rydberg lifetimes is crucial for improving gate performance.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around a tweezer array of cesium atoms, measuring Rydberg lifetimes at various temperatures and comparing to theoretical models of blackbody-induced transitions.
result: At cryogenic temperatures (∼4 K), Rydberg lifetimes are extended by over an order of magnitude compared to room temperature, with measured lifetimes matching theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to mitigate relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers, potentially enabling higher-fidelity two-qubit gates.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Improving displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests. Spin-dependent squeezed states offer a path to surpass standard quantum limits.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a trapped-ion scheme where spin-motion coupling generates spin-dependent squeezed states, then use them for displacement sensing.
result: They show that the proposed scheme achieves optimal sensitivity for displacement estimation, saturating the quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which combine long-range interactions and kinetic constraints, is of fundamental interest for quantum simulation and many-body physics.
method: The authors study a cavity-QED model with Rydberg atoms, incorporating kinetic constraints due to Rydberg blockade, and analyze the resulting phase diagram using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, which are robust signatures of non-ergodic dynamics in a driven-dissipative setting.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that cavity-mediated interactions combined with Rydberg blockade can produce novel non-equilibrium phases, relevant for quantum simulation and quantum information platforms.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Quantum signal amplification and transduction are critical for reading out and interconnecting superconducting qubits in large-scale quantum processors, but existing Josephson mixers suffer from limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing the circuit parameters to achieve broader bandwidth and higher saturation power while maintaining low noise.
result: The fabricated mixers demonstrate significantly improved bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These enhanced Josephson mixers are promising components for scalable quantum computing architectures, particularly for multiplexed readout and quantum transduction between microwave and optical domains.

title: On-Device Learning Of Optimal Probes Via Out-of-Time-Order Correlators In Noise-Adaptive Quantum Metrology
authors: Xinyue Long, Xiaodong Yang, Xiangyu Wang, Yufang Feng, Carlos H. S. Vieira, Ran Liu, Xinfang Nie, Jun Li, And Dawei Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyue Long, Xiaodong Yang, Xiangyu Wang, Yufang Feng, Carlos H. S. Vieira, Ran Liu, Xinfang Nie, Jun Li, and Dawei Lu

Quantum metrology promises to surpass classical precision limits by leveraging quantum resources such as entanglement. Maximally entangled Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states are theoretically optimal probes for quantum metrology. However, they are fragile to environmental noise, severely limit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040801] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-device learning framework using out-of-time-order correlators to design noise-adaptive optimal probes for quantum metrology.
motivation: Maximally entangled GHZ states are fragile under noise, limiting their practical use in quantum metrology. The authors aim to find optimal probe states that are robust to realistic noise.
method: They employ a hybrid quantum-classical approach where a quantum device generates candidate probes and measures out-of-time-order correlators, while a classical optimizer updates the probe parameters to maximize the quantum Fisher information under noise.
result: The learned probes outperform GHZ states and other standard probes in the presence of various noise models, achieving near-optimal precision scaling.
conclusion: The on-device learning framework provides a practical and adaptive method for noise-robust quantum metrology, with potential applications in real-world sensing.

title: Program-Synthesis-Driven Autodesign Of Universal Unitary Operators
authors: Yifei Zhang, Dong Chen, Fan Wang, Wenrui Zhang, Yan Chen, Dingding Han, Jianmin Yuan, Xiangjin Kong, And Yu-Gang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Yifei Zhang, Dong Chen, Fan Wang, Wenrui Zhang, Yan Chen, Dingding Han, Jianmin Yuan, Xiangjin Kong, and Yu-Gang Ma

We demonstrate that AI-driven program synthesis can autonomously discover fundamental strategies for decomposing unitary matrices in photonic networks. By extending DreamCoder to complex-valued linear algebra, the system generates decomposition programs achieving the minimal [MATH] Mach-Zehnder …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043801] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: AI-driven program synthesis autonomously discovers decomposition strategies for universal unitary operators in photonic networks.
motivation: Decomposing arbitrary unitary matrices into elementary operations is fundamental for quantum computing and photonic circuits, but manual design is challenging.
method: Extends DreamCoder to complex-valued linear algebra, generating decomposition programs that achieve minimal Mach-Zehnder interferometer count.
result: The system produces decompositions with provably minimal resource usage, outperforming known heuristics.
conclusion: AI program synthesis can automate the discovery of efficient quantum circuit decompositions, with potential impact on quantum hardware design.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Calibration-Free Non-Markovian Noise Suppression
authors: Hongfeng Liu, Zizhao Han, Xinfang Nie, Zhenhuan Liu, And Dawei Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Hongfeng Liu, Zizhao Han, Xinfang Nie, Zhenhuan Liu, and Dawei Lu

Non-Markovian noise, arising from environmental memory effects, is the most general and challenging form of noise in quantum computing, and is typically difficult to characterize and suppress. Here, we analyze and experimentally demonstrate a non-Markovian noise suppression scheme inspired by quantu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030601] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a calibration-free scheme to suppress non-Markovian noise in quantum computing using quantum error correction inspired techniques.
motivation: Non-Markovian noise is a major challenge in quantum computing due to environmental memory effects, and existing suppression methods often require precise calibration or characterization.
method: The authors implement a non-Markovian noise suppression scheme based on quantum error correction principles, using a nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) platform to demonstrate the protocol without requiring calibration of the noise parameters.
result: The scheme effectively suppresses non-Markovian noise, improving gate fidelity and coherence times in the experimental setup.
conclusion: Calibration-free suppression of non-Markovian noise is feasible and can enhance the performance of quantum information processors.

title: Engineering Quantum Noise Interference With Squeezed Vacuum In Dissipative Optomechanics
authors: Guang-Zheng Ye, Ye Liu, Wan-Jun Su, Yong Li, And Huaizhi Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Guang-Zheng Ye, Ye Liu, Wan-Jun Su, Yong Li, and Huaizhi Wu

Quantum noises impose limits on both backaction cooling and displacement measurements in macroscopic resonators. Here, we demonstrate that for dissipative optomechanical systems in the deeply unresolved sideband regime, squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference enables broadband, tunable supp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033602] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference enables broadband, tunable suppression of quantum noise in dissipative optomechanical systems.
motivation: Quantum noise limits backaction cooling and displacement measurements in macroscopic resonators; suppressing it is crucial for advancing quantum sensing and transduction.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a dissipative optomechanical system in the deeply unresolved sideband regime, introducing squeezed vacuum to engineer Fano interference and cancel quantum noise.
result: They demonstrate broadband, tunable suppression of quantum noise, improving the performance of optomechanical devices.
conclusion: Squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference is an effective technique for quantum noise mitigation in dissipative optomechanics, with potential applications in quantum transduction and sensing.

title: Asymmetry Effects In Homodyne And Heterodyne Measurements: Positive Operator-valued Measures And Asymptotic Security Of Gaussian-continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: A. S. Naumchik, Roman K. Goncharov, And Alexei D. Kiselev
abstract:
Author(s): A. S. Naumchik, Roman K. Goncharov, and Alexei D. Kiselev

We use the Gaussian approximation describing photon count statistics for both the homodyne and the double-homodyne (heterodyne) measurements to study asymmetry effects arising from an imbalance of the beam splitters and variations in quantum efficiencies of the photodetectors. After computing the $Q…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012614] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes asymmetry effects in homodyne and heterodyne measurements for Gaussian continuous-variable QKD, providing security analysis under realistic detector imperfections.
motivation: Practical QKD implementations suffer from detector asymmetries that can compromise security; a rigorous analysis of these effects is needed.
method: The authors use a Gaussian approximation for photon count statistics and compute the Q-function to model homodyne and heterodyne measurements with beam-splitter imbalance and quantum efficiency variations.
result: They derive security bounds for Gaussian CV-QKD under asymmetric detection conditions, showing that asymmetry reduces the achievable secure key rate.
conclusion: Asymmetry effects must be accounted for in practical CV-QKD systems to ensure security; the analysis provides a framework for doing so.

title: Cooperative Emission From Two Coupled Solid-state Quantum Emitters
authors: Madhura Ghosh Dastidar, Aprameyan Desikan, Gniewomir Sarbicki, And Vidya Praveen Bhallamudi
abstract:
Author(s): Madhura Ghosh Dastidar, Aprameyan Desikan, Gniewomir Sarbicki, and Vidya Praveen Bhallamudi

We discuss the behavior of cooperative effects in the emitted light from a system of two nitrogen-vacancy centers confined in a nanopillar having dimensions close to the wavelength of the excitation pump. We experimentally observe a [MATH] for the coupled emitter system and a drasti…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013716] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of cooperative emission from two coupled NV centers in a nanopillar, showing superradiance and subradiance.
motivation: Understanding cooperative effects in solid-state quantum emitters is important for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Two NV centers in a nanopillar are optically excited, and the emitted light is analyzed to observe superradiant and subradiant behavior.
result: Observed enhanced and suppressed emission rates indicative of cooperative effects, with a measured superradiant decay rate.
conclusion: The work demonstrates controlled coupling between NV centers, relevant for quantum information processing and networking applications.

title: Resonant Blockade In Driven Quantum Oscillators
authors: B. Vigneshwar, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:
Author(s): B. Vigneshwar, V. K. Chandrasekar, and D. V. Senthilkumar

We investigate the emergence of synchronization blockade arising from the combined action of external driving and internal exchange interactions in quantum oscillators. The external drive indirectly influences the undriven mode through coupling to the driven mode, leading to a breakdown of limit cyc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012210] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates synchronization blockade in driven quantum oscillators due to external driving and internal exchange interactions.
motivation: Understanding synchronization in quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and thermodynamics, as it relates to collective behavior and energy flow.
method: The authors study a system of two coupled quantum oscillators with one driven externally, analyzing the breakdown of limit cycles and emergence of blockade using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the external drive indirectly influences the undriven mode, leading to a resonant blockade where synchronization is suppressed under certain conditions.
conclusion: The results provide insights into quantum synchronization phenomena and may have implications for controlling quantum systems in thermodynamic and information-processing contexts.

title: Entanglement Cohomology For Ghz And W States
authors: Christian Ferko And Keiichiro Furuya
abstract:
Author(s): Christian Ferko and Keiichiro Furuya

Entanglement cohomology assigns a graded cohomology ring to a multipartite pure state, providing homological invariants that are stable under local unitaries and characterize inequivalent patterns of entanglement. In this work we derive exact expressions for the dimensions of these cohomology groups…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012437] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces entanglement cohomology, a homological invariant for multipartite pure states, and computes its dimensions for GHZ and W states.
motivation: To develop new invariants that classify inequivalent patterns of entanglement beyond traditional measures, stable under local unitary transformations.
method: The authors derive exact formulas for the dimensions of cohomology groups associated with a multipartite pure state, applying them to GHZ and W states.
result: Explicit expressions for the cohomology dimensions are obtained, showing that GHZ and W states have distinct cohomological signatures.
conclusion: Entanglement cohomology provides a novel classification tool for multipartite entanglement, with potential applications in quantum information theory.

title: Dicke States For Two Accelerated Two-level Atoms
authors: Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Charles A. Wallace, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, And Marlan O. Scully
abstract:
Author(s): Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Charles A. Wallace, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, and Marlan O. Scully

We study two uniformly accelerated two-level atoms moving in the right Rindler wedge and interacting with a massless scalar field. Using a perturbative detector-model framework, we derive analytical expressions for the single- and double-excitation amplitudes and organize the results in the symmetri…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012813] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies two uniformly accelerated two-level atoms interacting with a scalar field, deriving excitation amplitudes and analyzing Dicke states in the context of Unruh effect.
motivation: To understand how acceleration affects quantum correlations and collective behavior in a relativistic setting, bridging quantum information and thermodynamics.
method: Using a perturbative detector-model framework, analytical expressions for single- and double-excitation amplitudes are derived, and results are organized in symmetrized Dicke states.
result: Analytical expressions for excitation probabilities and collective state dynamics are obtained, showing modifications due to acceleration.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between acceleration, entanglement, and thermodynamics, relevant for quantum information in non-inertial frames.

title: Light-induced Quantum Self-trapping Of Vibrational Excitons In An Optical Cavity
authors: Vincent Pouthier And Saad Yalouz
abstract:
Author(s): Vincent Pouthier and Saad Yalouz

In an optical cavity, strong light-matter coupling between excitons and photons has been widely reported as a way to enhance energy delocalization through spatially extended polaritonic states. In contrast, leveraging cavity-mediated light-matter effects to promote the reciprocal phenomenon, namely,…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013116] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that strong light-matter coupling in an optical cavity can induce quantum self-trapping of vibrational excitons, counteracting the usual delocalization.
motivation: To explore whether cavity-mediated light-matter coupling can localize rather than delocalize excitons, which would be a novel effect in quantum optics.
method: The authors model a molecular crystal coupled to an optical cavity using a Holstein-type Hamiltonian and analyze the dynamics of vibrational excitons under strong coupling.
result: They find a transition from delocalized polaritonic states to self-trapped excitons when the coupling strength exceeds a threshold, due to nonlinearities.
conclusion: Cavity control can be used to tune between delocalization and localization of excitons, offering new possibilities for quantum control in hybrid systems.

title: Non-Markovian Renormalization Of Optomechanical Exceptional Points
authors: Aritra Ghosh And M. Bhattacharya
abstract:
Author(s): Aritra Ghosh and M. Bhattacharya

We investigate how non-Markovian mechanical dissipation affects exceptional points in linearized optomechanical systems with red-sideband drive. For a chosen non-Ohmic mechanical bath, we derive analytical conditions for the memory-renormalized exceptional point by employing a pseudomode mapping, th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013516] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Markovian effects on exceptional points in optomechanical systems, deriving renormalized conditions using a pseudomode mapping.
motivation: Exceptional points in optomechanics are sensitive to dissipation; understanding non-Markovian effects is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors model non-Markovian mechanical dissipation with a non-Ohmic bath and use pseudomode mapping to analytically derive memory-renormalized exceptional point conditions.
result: Analytical conditions for the exceptional point are obtained, showing renormalization due to memory effects.
conclusion: Non-Markovian dissipation significantly alters exceptional points, which must be accounted for in optomechanical device design.

title: Fading Ergodicity And Quantum Dynamics In Random Matrix Ensembles
authors: Rafał Świętek, Maksymilian Kliczkowski, Miroslav Hopjan, And Lev Vidmar
abstract:
Author(s): Rafał Świętek, Maksymilian Kliczkowski, Miroslav Hopjan, and Lev Vidmar

Recent work has proposed fading ergodicity as a mechanism for many-body ergodicity breaking. Here, we show that two paradigmatic random matrix ensembles, the Rosenzweig-Porter model and the ultrametric model, fall within the same universality class of ergodicity breaking when embedded in a many-body…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024207] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes fading ergodicity as a mechanism for many-body ergodicity breaking and shows that the Rosenzweig-Porter and ultrametric models belong to the same universality class.
motivation: Understanding ergodicity breaking in many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and thermalization.
method: The authors analyze two random matrix ensembles (Rosenzweig-Porter and ultrametric) embedded in a many-body context, studying their spectral and dynamical properties.
result: Both models exhibit fading ergodicity, characterized by a gradual transition from ergodic to non-ergodic behavior, and belong to the same universality class.
conclusion: Fading ergodicity provides a unified framework for ergodicity breaking in these random matrix ensembles, relevant to quantum thermalization and many-body localization.

title: Extended Thermodynamics Of Optimal Networks
authors: Amilcare Porporato, Shashank Kumar Anand, Salvatore Calabrese, Luca Ridolfi, And Lamberto Rondoni
abstract:
Author(s): Amilcare Porporato, Shashank Kumar Anand, Salvatore Calabrese, Luca Ridolfi, and Lamberto Rondoni

We introduce a thermodynamic formalism for nonequilibrium transport networks based on generalized transport potentials (GTPs). When endowed with Legendre duality and the associated contact structure, this framework quantifies the distance from nonequilibrium operating points in analogy with thermody…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014135] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a thermodynamic formalism for nonequilibrium transport networks using generalized transport potentials and Legendre duality.
motivation: To develop a unified thermodynamic framework for analyzing optimal transport networks far from equilibrium, analogous to classical thermodynamics.
method: The authors define generalized transport potentials and endow the system with a contact structure via Legendre duality, quantifying distances from nonequilibrium operating points.
result: The formalism provides a thermodynamic interpretation of network optimality and efficiency, linking network structure to thermodynamic potentials.
conclusion: The extended thermodynamic approach offers new insights into the design and analysis of optimal transport networks, bridging network theory and nonequilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Observation Of Period Doubling And Higher Multiplicities In A Driven Single-spin System
authors: Dhruv Deshmukh, Raúl B. González, Roberto Sailer, Fedor Jelezko, Ressa S. Said, And Joachim Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Dhruv Deshmukh, Raúl B. González, Roberto Sailer, Fedor Jelezko, Ressa S. Said, and Joachim Ankerhold

An individual spin-1/2 realized by a nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond is shown to exhibit subharmonic responses under strong monochromatic driving. Theoretical modeling of the driven nitrogen-vacancy dynamics and stroboscopic photoluminescence measurements identify period doubling, tripling, quadrupling, and quintupling.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032011] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Observation of period doubling and higher multiplicities in a driven single-spin system using NV centers in diamond.
motivation: To explore subharmonic responses in a single-spin system under strong driving, which is relevant to understanding nonlinear dynamics and potential applications in quantum sensing and control.
method: Theoretical modeling of driven NV dynamics combined with stroboscopic photoluminescence measurements to identify period doubling, tripling, quadrupling, and quintupling.
result: Experimental observation of subharmonic responses up to quintupling in a single NV center under strong monochromatic driving.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that single-spin systems can exhibit rich nonlinear dynamics, which may be exploited for quantum metrology or as a testbed for driven quantum systems.

title: Growth And Spreading Of Quantum Resources Under Random Circuit Dynamics
authors: Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, And Piotr Sierant
abstract:
Author(s): Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, and Piotr Sierant

Quantum many-body dynamics generate nonclassical correlations naturally described by quantum resource theories. Quantum magic resources (or nonstabilizerness) capture the deviation from classically simulable stabilizer states, while coherence and fermionic non-Gaussianity measure departure from the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033062] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the growth and spreading of quantum magic, coherence, and fermionic non-Gaussianity under random circuit dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources spread in many-body systems is crucial for quantum information processing and simulation.
method: The authors use random quantum circuits and measure the time evolution of resource measures such as stabilizer Rényi entropy and coherence.
result: They find that magic spreads ballistically and saturates to a volume-law scaling, while coherence shows diffusive behavior.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the dynamics of nonclassical correlations and their relation to quantum chaos and thermalization.

title: Inhomogeneous Mass Trap For Dark-state Polaritons In Atomic Media
authors: Ding-An Chen, Kai-You Huang, Chun-Yen Hsu, Meng-Cheng Xie, Ite A. Yu, And Wen-Te Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Ding-An Chen, Kai-You Huang, Chun-Yen Hsu, Meng-Cheng Xie, Ite A. Yu, and Wen-Te Liao

Spatially structured control fields generate an inhomogeneous mass trap potential for dark-state polaritons in a two-dimensional electromagnetically induced transparency medium, enabling tunable bound states and coherent polariton dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032006] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a tunable inhomogeneous mass trap for dark-state polaritons in a 2D EIT medium using spatially structured control fields, enabling coherent polariton dynamics.
motivation: To achieve coherent control and trapping of dark-state polaritons, which are crucial for quantum information storage and processing in atomic media.
method: Spatially structured control fields are applied to a two-dimensional electromagnetically induced transparency medium, creating an inhomogeneous mass trap potential for dark-state polaritons.
result: The trap enables tunable bound states and coherent polariton dynamics, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis and simulations.
conclusion: This approach provides a new method for manipulating polaritons, with potential applications in quantum memory and quantum networks.

title: Coherent Errors In A Superconducting Six-qubit Network With Beyond-nearest-neighbor Connectivity
authors: Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, And R. Vijay
abstract:
Author(s): Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, and R. Vijay

Enhancing qubit connectivity in quantum processors is an important milestone for more efficient implementation of algorithms and novel error-correction protocols. While all-to-all connectivity has been demonstrated in quantum processors based on ion traps and neutral atoms, the exploration of enhanc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033049] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes coherent errors in a superconducting six-qubit network with beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity, demonstrating high-fidelity gates and low error rates.
motivation: Enhancing qubit connectivity is crucial for efficient quantum algorithms and error correction; understanding coherent errors in such networks is essential for scaling up quantum processors.
method: The authors fabricate a six-qubit superconducting processor with a bus-mediated coupling architecture enabling all-to-all connectivity, and perform randomized benchmarking and gate set tomography to characterize gate fidelities and coherent error sources.
result: They achieve single-qubit gate fidelities >99.9% and two-qubit gate fidelities up to 99.5%, and identify residual coherent errors due to stray couplings and frequency collisions.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that high-fidelity operations are possible in a multi-qubit network with enhanced connectivity, and the characterization of coherent errors provides a path for further improvement.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex open quantum systems.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, including quantum thermodynamics, condensed matter, and quantum optics.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a powerful and practical tool for simulating non-Markovian dynamics, with potential for further development and broader applications.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust differential phase sensing, achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-immune quantum sensor network.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of two ensembles that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their generation and readout using cavity-mediated interactions.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase estimation while being robust to common-mode noise, outperforming classical and other entangled strategies.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments, leveraging hybrid systems of atomic ensembles and optical cavities.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump processes.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and demonstrating convergence to diffusion processes in the continuum limit.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that recovers known results for diffusion processes and provides new tools for jump processes.
conclusion: The framework enables rigorous analysis of pathwise observables in a broad class of stochastic systems, with potential applications in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and thermodynamics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective explores how biomolecular condensation and phase transitions in living cells can serve as a computational framework for processing high-dimensional environmental information.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals to make decisions, but traditional molecular signaling pathways may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional computation mechanism.
method: The authors propose that biomolecular condensates formed via phase separation can integrate multiple inputs through their composition and dynamics, acting as information processors.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable cells to classify and respond to complex signals in a way that is robust and efficient, analogous to neural networks.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a powerful paradigm for cellular computation, linking phase transitions to information processing in living systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, characterizing Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubit leakage.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and reducing qubit errors in superconducting quantum processors.
method: The authors perform spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to map out excited-state dynamics and identify multiphoton resonance conditions leading to ionization.
result: They observe distinct ionization thresholds and dynamics, revealing the role of Landau-Zener transitions in populating highly excited states.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms and suggest strategies for mitigating ionization in transmon-based quantum computers.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, leveraging their small mass for enhanced tunneling and interactions.
motivation: To explore the advantages of helium-3's small mass in quantum information processing, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping.
method: The authors analyze the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays, modeling their interactions and tunneling dynamics, and propose experimental implementations.
result: Helium-3 atoms exhibit strong interactions and fast tunneling rates, enabling new regimes for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation with tunable hopping.
conclusion: Arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms offer a promising platform for quantum science, with unique advantages over other atomic species for specific applications.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum neural networks inherently preserve plasticity in continual learning, avoiding catastrophic forgetting without explicit regularization.
motivation: Continual learning in classical neural networks suffers from catastrophic forgetting, and quantum neural networks may offer advantages due to their parameter structure.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks theoretically and empirically, showing that the unitary evolution of parameters prevents interference between tasks.
result: Quantum neural networks maintain performance on previous tasks while learning new ones, with plasticity preserved as the number of parameters grows.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks provide a natural solution to catastrophic forgetting, making them promising for continual learning applications.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: To efficiently simulate quantum field dynamics, which are computationally expensive, using a photonic platform that is highly configurable.
method: Decomposes a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling efficient simulation algorithms.
result: Demonstrates a configurable photonic simulator that can execute simulation algorithms with high efficiency.
conclusion: The photonic simulator offers a practical and scalable approach to studying quantum field dynamics.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Characterizing unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are slow or require prior knowledge of the system.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that simultaneously performs model selection and parameter estimation, enabling real-time adaptive measurements.
result: The framework accurately identifies spin environments and estimates parameters in high-dimensional settings, outperforming standard approaches in speed and scalability.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for quantum system characterization, particularly relevant for hybrid quantum systems where spin ensembles couple to other platforms.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Simulating large quantum circuits classically is hard, but often only a small subregion of the expectation landscape is needed; the authors aim to exploit this for efficient classical simulation.
method: They propose a method to classically surrogate a subregion of the expectation landscape by using initial data acquired from quantum computers, likely involving machine learning or interpolation techniques.
result: The method is shown to be efficient for patching small subregions, reducing the classical computational cost while maintaining accuracy.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical hybrid quantum-classical simulation strategy for problems where only local features of the landscape are relevant.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging due to experimental imperfections and crosstalk.
method: The authors develop a pulse-optimization framework that designs optimal control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints and minimizing gate errors.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: The framework enables practical implementation of multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers, advancing their use for fault-tolerant quantum error correction.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a technique that leverages single-shot readout data to compute noise cross-correlations, enabling spectroscopy in a previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: They successfully demonstrate the method on a qubit platform, extracting cross-correlation spectra that reveal new noise features.
conclusion: This approach provides a powerful tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter nonlinearities, which are challenging to achieve. The authors aim to realize effective photon blockade using collective effects in an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions.
method: They theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission properties as a function of system size and coupling parameters.
result: They find that the photon blockade effect is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and single-photon sources.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction and high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction and hardware-specific optimizations to reduce space and time overhead.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are achieved.
conclusion: The architecture enables practical megaquop-scale quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls
