By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and extrapolate dynamics.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators that operate in frequency space to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables, leveraging the periodic structure.
result: The method accurately learns Floquet Hamiltonians and predicts observable dynamics and operator growth beyond the training time window.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to many scientific and engineering problems, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, variable-time amplitude amplification, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods.
result: It catalogs the evolution of quantum linear system solvers, highlighting improvements in query complexity, precision, and applicability.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of diverse methods is needed.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate techniques for different physical contexts.
conclusion: The unified framework facilitates cross-fertilization between fields and aids in developing new simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qudits can simplify quantum circuits by reducing gate counts and enabling more efficient decompositions of multiqubit gates like the Toffoli gate.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits offer advantages in reducing circuit depth and resource requirements for certain quantum algorithms, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for near-term quantum computing, though challenges remain in qudit control and error correction.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques have matured to reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, though challenges remain for systems with higher-order perturbations or surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of solid-state spin qubits for quantum information processing.

title: Precision Limit Under Weak Coupling With An Ancillary Qubit
authors: Peng Chen And Jun Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Peng Chen and Jun Jing

We propose a measurement-based quantum metrology protocol in a composite model, where the probe system (a spin ensemble) is coupled to an ancillary two-level system (qubit) with a general Heisenberg XXZ interaction. With optimized probe-ancilla coupling strengths and duration of joint evolution, the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012449] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: A measurement-based quantum metrology protocol using a spin ensemble coupled to an ancillary qubit achieves precision beyond the standard quantum limit.
motivation: To improve precision in quantum metrology by exploiting weak coupling and ancillary systems.
method: The probe (spin ensemble) interacts with an ancillary qubit via Heisenberg XXZ coupling; optimized coupling strengths and evolution times are used to enhance measurement precision.
result: The protocol achieves sub-shot-noise scaling and surpasses the standard quantum limit under optimized conditions.
conclusion: Weak coupling with an ancillary qubit can enhance metrological precision, offering a practical approach for quantum sensing.

title: Recursive Analytical Technique For The Quantum Analysis Of A Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Parameter Reduction
authors: Richard A. Brewster, Gerald Baumgartner, Anne Marie Richards, And Yanne K. Chembo
abstract:
Author(s): Richard A. Brewster, Gerald Baumgartner, Anne Marie Richards, and Yanne K. Chembo

An analytic technique for the investigation of the combined impacts of multiple photon pairs and a non-negligible joint spectral density on the measurement of a Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) parameter is introduced. We demonstrate this technique for an asymmetric Gaussian-normal joint spectral d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033075] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytic technique to study the combined effects of multiple photon pairs and non-negligible joint spectral density on CHSH parameter measurement.
motivation: Accurate measurement of the CHSH parameter is crucial for Bell tests and device-independent protocols, but realistic imperfections like multiple photon pairs and spectral correlations degrade the observed violation.
method: The authors introduce a recursive analytic technique that accounts for multiple photon pairs and a non-negligible joint spectral density, demonstrated for an asymmetric Gaussian-normal joint spectral density.
result: The technique provides a tractable way to compute the CHSH parameter under realistic experimental conditions, showing how these imperfections reduce the violation.
conclusion: This analytic framework helps in designing experiments and interpreting CHSH measurements in the presence of practical limitations, aiding the development of device-independent quantum information protocols.

title: Double-bracket Quantum Algorithms For High-fidelity Ground-state Preparation
authors: Matteo Robbiati, Edoardo Pedicillo, Andrea Pasquale, Xiaoyue Li, Oriel Kiss, Andrew Wright, Renato M. S. Farias, Khanh Uyen Giang, Jeongrak Son, Johannes Knörzer, Siong Thye Goh, Jun Yong Khoo, Nelly H. Y. Ng, Zoë Holmes, Stefano Carrazza, And Marek Gluza
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Robbiati, Edoardo Pedicillo, Andrea Pasquale, Xiaoyue Li, Oriel Kiss, Andrew Wright, Renato M. S. Farias, Khanh Uyen Giang, Jeongrak Son, Johannes Knörzer, Siong Thye Goh, Jun Yong Khoo, Nelly H. Y. Ng, Zoë Holmes, Stefano Carrazza, and Marek Gluza

Ground-state preparation is a central application for quantum computers but remains challenging in practice. In this work, we quantitatively investigate the performance and gate counts of double-bracket quantum algorithms (DBQAs) for ground-state preparation. We propose a practical strategy in which…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033078] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes and benchmarks double-bracket quantum algorithms for high-fidelity ground-state preparation, focusing on gate counts and practical performance.
motivation: Ground-state preparation is crucial for quantum computing applications but remains challenging; the authors aim to develop efficient algorithms with practical gate counts.
method: The authors introduce double-bracket quantum algorithms (DBQAs) and evaluate their performance through numerical simulations, analyzing gate counts and fidelity.
result: DBQAs achieve high-fidelity ground-state preparation with moderate gate counts, outperforming some existing methods in certain regimes.
conclusion: Double-bracket quantum algorithms offer a promising approach for practical ground-state preparation on near-term quantum devices.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary evolution into a unitary on a larger system, realized via a tight-binding lattice with nearest-neighbor couplings.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and circuit depth, overcoming traditional connectivity bottlenecks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with implications for quantum algorithms and open quantum systems.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function gradient under generic noise models, relating it to the expressivity of the circuit measured by the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity, and provide estimates for the concentration of the loss function in noisy circuits.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to design noise-resilient variational circuits and optimize training, bridging quantum information theory and practical algorithm design.

title: Synchronized Aharonov-Bohm Motifs Via Engineered Dissipation
authors: Christopher W. Wächtler And Gloria Platero
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher W. Wächtler and Gloria Platero

The interplay between external gauge fields and lattice geometry can induce extreme localization dynamics through complete destructive interference. We show that combining this flux-induced localization with engineered dissipation leads to robust spin synchronization in rotationally symmetric spin g…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030405] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that combining flux-induced localization with engineered dissipation leads to robust spin synchronization in rotationally symmetric spin systems.
motivation: To understand how external gauge fields and dissipation can be harnessed to achieve robust synchronization in quantum systems, which is relevant for quantum information processing.
method: The authors study a rotationally symmetric spin system under an artificial gauge field (Aharonov-Bohm effect) and introduce engineered dissipation to stabilize synchronized spin dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that the interplay of flux-induced localization and dissipation produces robust spin synchronization, protected against certain perturbations.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation can be used to create synchronized Aharonov-Bohm motifs, offering a new approach to control quantum dynamics.

title: Variational Preparation Of Quantum Many-body Scars With Shallow Circuits
authors: Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, And Giuliano Benenti
abstract:
Author(s): Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, and Giuliano Benenti

We present and benchmark a type of variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) which we denote [MATH]-VQE. It is designed to target midspectrum eigenstates and prepare quantum many-body scar states. The approach leverages the fact that noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices are limited in their ability to …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012613] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) variant to prepare quantum many-body scar states using shallow circuits.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars are non-thermal eigenstates that evade thermalization, and preparing them on near-term quantum devices is challenging due to circuit depth limitations.
method: The authors introduce a modified VQE (called M-VQE) that targets mid-spectrum eigenstates by optimizing a cost function that penalizes states far from the target energy window, using shallow circuits.
result: Numerical simulations show that M-VQE can successfully prepare scar states in the PXP model and other systems with high fidelity using only a few layers of gates.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical method for studying quantum many-body scars on NISQ devices, though it is limited to small system sizes and specific models.

title: Efficient Three-dimensional sub-Doppler Cooling Of $^{40}\mathrm{Ca}^{+}$ In A Penning Trap
authors: Brian J. Mcmahon And Brian C. Sawyer
abstract:
Author(s): Brian J. McMahon and Brian C. Sawyer

The authors demonstrate three-dimensional sub-Doppler cooling of a single
[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013119] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates three-dimensional sub-Doppler cooling of a single Ca+ ion in a Penning trap using a two-photon dark resonance and parametric drive.
motivation: Sub-Doppler cooling in Penning traps is challenging due to the magnetic field; this work aims to achieve efficient cooling across all motional modes using only axially propagating lasers.
method: Exploits a two-photon dark resonance for cooling and applies a parametric drive to the trap electrodes to exchange motional occupations between axial and radial modes.
result: Achieves sub-Doppler temperatures in all three dimensions, demonstrating effective cooling of a single ion in a Penning trap.
conclusion: The technique provides a practical method for cooling trapped ions in Penning traps, which is relevant for quantum information processing with trapped ions.

title: Boundary Time Crystals Beyond Mean-field Theory: A Stroboscopic Rotating-wave Approximation
authors: Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, And Xiaoguang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, and Xiaoguang Wang

Boundary time crystals are a class of exotic dissipative quantum phases that spontaneously break continuous time-translation symmetry in the thermodynamic limit of open quantum systems. In finite-size systems, the long-time evolution of boundary time crystals exhibits decaying oscillations that cann…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012211] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies boundary time crystals in open quantum systems using a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation beyond mean-field theory.
motivation: Boundary time crystals are exotic dissipative quantum phases that break time-translation symmetry, but their finite-size behavior and beyond-mean-field corrections are not well understood.
method: The authors develop a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation to treat the dissipative dynamics of boundary time crystals, going beyond the mean-field approximation.
result: They find that the long-time evolution exhibits decaying oscillations that can be captured by their approximation, and they characterize the phase transition and finite-size scaling.
conclusion: The work provides a more accurate theoretical description of boundary time crystals, relevant for understanding non-equilibrium quantum phases.

title: Random-matrix Perspective On Probabilistic Error Cancellation
authors: Leonhard Moske, Pedro Ribeiro, Tomaž Prosen, Sergiy Denysov, Karol Życzkowski, And David J. Luitz
abstract:
Author(s): Leonhard Moske, Pedro Ribeiro, Tomaž Prosen, Sergiy Denysov, Karol Życzkowski, and David J. Luitz

Probabilistic error cancellation is an attempt to reverse the effect of dissipative noise channels on quantum computers by applying unphysical channels after the execution of a quantum algorithm on noisy hardware. We investigate on general grounds the properties of such unphysical quantum channels b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012442] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses random matrix theory to analyze the properties of unphysical channels in probabilistic error cancellation for quantum computing.
motivation: Probabilistic error cancellation aims to reverse dissipative noise on quantum computers, but the unphysical channels involved are not well understood. The authors seek a general framework to characterize these channels.
method: The authors employ random matrix theory to model the unphysical channels and derive statistical properties such as the distribution of eigenvalues and the average gate fidelity.
result: They find that the unphysical channels are typically non-CP (completely positive) and have a high probability of being non-physical, with the average gate fidelity decaying exponentially with the number of qubits.
conclusion: Probabilistic error cancellation becomes impractical for large systems due to the exponential overhead and non-physical nature of the required channels, suggesting the need for alternative error mitigation strategies.

title: Linear-optical Schemes To Postselect High-dimensional Dicke States
authors: Daniel Bhatti, William J. Munro, And Seungbeom Chin
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Bhatti, William J. Munro, and Seungbeom Chin

Multipartite entanglement is an essential quantum resource for various distributed quantum applications. One promising method for preparing multipartite entanglement is to interfere independent photons at linear-optical interference setups. While heralding the successful interference and thereby the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013714] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes linear-optical schemes to postselect high-dimensional Dicke states for multipartite entanglement.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement is essential for distributed quantum applications, and Dicke states are a useful class of entangled states. The authors aim to provide practical linear-optical methods to generate these states.
method: The schemes use linear-optical interference setups with postselection to herald the successful preparation of high-dimensional Dicke states.
result: The proposed schemes can generate high-dimensional Dicke states with certain success probabilities, and the authors analyze the resource requirements.
conclusion: The work offers a feasible approach to preparing high-dimensional Dicke states using linear optics, which may benefit quantum information processing tasks.

title: Spontaneous Breaking Of Time Translation Symmetry Via Spatially Inhomogeneous Many-body Interactions
authors: Tingmei Li, Pai Zhou, Yu-Hui Chen, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Tingmei Li, Pai Zhou, Yu-Hui Chen, and Xiangdong Zhang

Time crystals, with their intrinsic long-range temporal order and self-sustained oscillations, provide a unique platform for quantum applications that leverages long-lived coherence. We investigate the emergence of time-crystalline order in a continuously driven, dissipative atomic lattice featuring…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012612] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the emergence of time-crystalline order in a driven dissipative atomic lattice with spatially inhomogeneous interactions.
motivation: Time crystals exhibit long-range temporal order and self-sustained oscillations, offering a platform for quantum applications leveraging long-lived coherence.
method: The authors study a continuously driven, dissipative atomic lattice model with spatially inhomogeneous many-body interactions, analyzing the conditions for spontaneous breaking of time translation symmetry.
result: They demonstrate that spatially inhomogeneous interactions can stabilize time-crystalline order in a dissipative setting.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the robustness of time crystals in open systems, relevant for quantum technologies but not directly advancing core information thermodynamics.

title: Stability Of Quantum Chaos Against Weak Nonunitarity
authors: Yi-Cheng Wang, Ehud Altman, And Samuel J. Garratt
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Cheng Wang, Ehud Altman, and Samuel J. Garratt

We study the quantum dynamics generated by the repeated action of a nonunitary evolution operator on a system of qubits. Breaking unitarity can lead to the purification of mixed initial states, which corresponds to the loss of sensitivity to initial conditions, and hence the absence of a key signatu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014314] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of quantum chaos against weak nonunitarity, showing that the spectral form factor remains stable while out-of-time-order correlators decay.
motivation: Understanding how nonunitarity affects quantum chaos is important for open quantum systems and quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of a qubit system under repeated nonunitary evolution, computing the spectral form factor and out-of-time-order correlators.
result: The spectral form factor is robust to weak nonunitarity, but out-of-time-order correlators decay, indicating loss of sensitivity to initial conditions.
conclusion: Quantum chaos signatures can be partially stable against nonunitarity, with implications for thermalization and information scrambling in open systems.

title: Discrete Time Crystal Order In Spin Chains Enabled By Floquet Flat Bands
authors: Mahbub Rahaman And Analabha Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Mahbub Rahaman and Analabha Roy

We propose a novel protocol to realize discrete time-crystal (DTC) order in clean, periodically driven spin-[MATH] chains. In each drive cycle, a global spin flip is followed by a two-tone flat-band segment. This flat-band segment engineers a fully degenerate Floquet quasienergy spectrum, suppresses …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034311] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a protocol to realize discrete time-crystal order in clean spin chains using Floquet flat bands.
motivation: Discrete time crystals are a novel non-equilibrium phase of matter, and realizing them in clean systems without disorder is a significant challenge.
method: The protocol uses a periodic drive consisting of a global spin flip followed by a two-tone flat-band segment that engineers a fully degenerate Floquet quasienergy spectrum, suppressing heating.
result: The flat-band segment stabilizes the DTC order, leading to persistent subharmonic oscillations robust against perturbations.
conclusion: This work provides a new mechanism for realizing DTC order in clean systems, advancing the understanding of non-equilibrium quantum phases.

title: Phase Transition From Localization To Chaos In A Classical Many-body System
authors: Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, and Tomaž Prosen

We report a dynamical phase transition in the information spreading within a classical 2D deterministic interacting many-body system. Specifically, the transition is observed in a recently introduced momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on the square lattice [Kasim and Prosen,…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014140] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a dynamical phase transition from localization to chaos in a classical many-body system, studied via information spreading in a cellular automaton.
motivation: Understanding the transition from localized to chaotic behavior in many-body systems is a fundamental problem in statistical mechanics and thermodynamics.
method: The authors study a momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on a square lattice, analyzing information spreading as a diagnostic.
result: They observe a dynamical phase transition characterized by a change in the propagation of information.
conclusion: The work provides insights into classical many-body dynamics and may have implications for understanding thermalization and chaos.

title: Caloric Phenomena And Stirling-cycle Performance In Heisenberg-Kitaev Magnon Systems
authors: Bastian Castorene, Martin Hve Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, And Patricio Vargas
abstract:
Author(s): Bastian Castorene, Martin HvE Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, and Patricio Vargas

We investigate the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg–Kitaev magnonic medium with Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interactions. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show the DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, yielding even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency. In contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014132] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Stirling-cycle performance in a Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions, focusing on caloric phenomena and efficiency.
motivation: To understand how DM interactions affect the thermodynamic performance of a quantum magnetic medium in a Stirling cycle.
method: Linear spin-wave theory is used to compute the magnon spectrum and caloric responses, and the Stirling cycle efficiency is derived.
result: DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, leading to even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency.
conclusion: The Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions can serve as a working medium for Stirling cycles with symmetric efficiency.

title: Generic Signatures Of non-Markovian Dynamics In The Presence Of A Magnetic Field
authors: Mousumi Biswas, Joydip Das, And Bidhan Chandra Bag
abstract:
Author(s): Mousumi Biswas, Joydip Das, and Bidhan Chandra Bag

In this paper, we have presented the three-dimensional dynamics in the velocity space of a Brownian particle coupled to a non-Markovian thermal bath in the presence of a magnetic field (MF), as well as external deterministic and stochastic force fields. The directions of the MF and the deterministic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014121] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Markovian dynamics of a Brownian particle in a magnetic field, focusing on velocity-space signatures.
motivation: To understand how non-Markovian effects manifest in the presence of a magnetic field, which is relevant for open quantum systems and stochastic thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a Brownian particle coupled to a non-Markovian thermal bath under external deterministic and stochastic forces, analyzing three-dimensional velocity dynamics.
result: They identify generic signatures of non-Markovian dynamics, such as modifications to velocity correlations and relaxation times due to the magnetic field.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-Markovian effects in magnetic fields, which may inform thermodynamic and information-processing applications.

title: Computational Complexity And Simulability Of non-Hermitian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Brian Barch And Daniel Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Brian Barch and Daniel Lidar

Non-Hermitian (NH) quantum systems demonstrate striking differences from their Hermitian counterparts, leading to claims of NH advantage in areas ranging from metrology to entanglement generation. We show that in the context of quantum computation, any such NH advantage is unlikely to be scalable as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033083] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Hermitian quantum dynamics do not provide a scalable advantage for quantum computation due to complexity-theoretic limitations.
motivation: Non-Hermitian quantum systems have been claimed to offer advantages in metrology and entanglement generation, but their potential for scalable quantum computation was unclear.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of simulating non-Hermitian dynamics and prove that they are not more powerful than standard Hermitian quantum computation under reasonable assumptions.
result: They demonstrate that any non-Hermitian advantage is unlikely to be scalable, as the simulation of such dynamics is bounded by the same complexity class as Hermitian quantum circuits.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian quantum dynamics do not offer a scalable computational advantage, aligning with the broader understanding of quantum computational complexity.

title: General Model And Modulation Strategies For Sagnac-based Encoders
authors: Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto de Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, And Giuseppe Vallone
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto De Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, and Giuseppe Vallone

In recent decades, there has been an increasing demand for faster modulation schemes. Electro-optic modulators are essential components in modern photonic systems, enabling high-speed control of light for applications ranging from telecommunications to quantum communication. Conventional inline and …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033069] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general model and modulation strategies for Sagnac-based encoders used in quantum communication.
motivation: Faster modulation schemes are needed for quantum communication, and Sagnac-based encoders offer advantages but lack a unified theoretical model.
method: The authors develop a general theoretical model for Sagnac-based encoders and analyze various modulation strategies, including phase and intensity modulation.
result: They identify optimal modulation strategies that maximize encoding speed and fidelity, and validate their model with experimental demonstrations.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for designing high-speed Sagnac-based encoders, which can improve the performance of quantum key distribution systems.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for optimizing the generation of non-Gaussian quantum states, significantly increasing success rates.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing, but their generation is inefficient. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization framework.
method: They define control parameters beyond the stellar rank and develop a method to optimize the generation process using these parameters.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success rate of generating non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This work offers a scalable approach to generating non-Gaussian states, which is important for quantum information applications.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, but the paper focuses on complexity classification rather than direct information-theoretic results.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using quantum computational complexity theory.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity classes for matrix functions, highlighting potential quantum advantage in certain regimes.
conclusion: The work offers insights into quantum advantage but is more aligned with quantum complexity theory than the core information-theoretic focus of the researcher.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but existing methods struggle with large multiqubit unitaries. The authors aim to extend the reach of stabilizer-based simulation by leveraging symmetries.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for larger systems, building on the Gottesman-Knill theorem and Clifford circuit simulation.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry reduction significantly improves the efficiency of classical simulation for Clifford-dominated circuits, enabling simulation of circuits beyond previous limits.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, with potential applications in quantum circuit verification and benchmarking.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, focusing on critical quantum sensing.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.
method: The tutorial reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis and metrological bounds near critical points.
result: It provides a pedagogical overview of how criticality can enhance sensitivity, with examples from various many-body systems.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for quantum-enhanced metrology, but practical implementations remain challenging.

title: Expander Quantum Low Density Parity Check Codes Against Long-range Correlated Errors In Memory
authors: Yash Deepak Kashtikar, Pranay Mathur, Sudharsan Senthil, And Avhishek Chatterjee
abstract:
Author(s): Yash Deepak Kashtikar, Pranay Mathur, Sudharsan Senthil, and Avhishek Chatterjee

Fault tolerance using constant space overhead against long-range correlated errors is an important practical question. In the pioneering works of Terhal and Burkhard [ 6, 97 (2006)], and Aharonov, Kitaev, and Pres…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012444] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fault tolerance of quantum LDPC codes against long-range correlated errors in quantum memory.
motivation: Practical quantum memory requires fault tolerance with constant space overhead even under realistic correlated noise, which is less understood than independent errors.
method: The authors analyze the performance of expander quantum LDPC codes under long-range correlated error models using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They derive thresholds and logical error rates for these codes under correlated noise, showing that expander codes can tolerate certain correlations.
conclusion: Expander quantum LDPC codes are promising for fault-tolerant quantum memory with constant overhead against long-range correlated errors.

title: Composite-dimensional Topological Codes With Boundaries And Defects
authors: Mohamad Mousa, Amit Jamadagni, And Eugene Dumitrescu
abstract:
Author(s): Mohamad Mousa, Amit Jamadagni, and Eugene Dumitrescu

We introduce new algorithms and provide example constructions of stabilizer models for the gapped boundaries, domain walls, and [MATH] defects of Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles. Using the physically intuitive concept of condensation, our algorithm explicitly describes how…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012438] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces algorithms and constructions for stabilizer models of gapped boundaries, domain walls, and defects in Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles, focusing on topological codes.
motivation: Topological codes are important for fault-tolerant quantum computation, and understanding their boundaries and defects is crucial for implementing logical operations and error correction.
method: The authors use the concept of condensation to algorithmically describe gapped boundaries, domain walls, and defects in composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles, providing explicit stabilizer models.
result: New algorithms and example constructions are presented for stabilizer models of these topological features in Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of topological codes by providing systematic methods to handle boundaries and defects, which are essential for practical quantum error correction.

title: Fermion Doubling In Dirac Quantum Walks
authors: Chaitanya Gupta And Anthony J. Short
abstract:
Author(s): Chaitanya Gupta and Anthony J. Short

We consider discrete spacetime models known as quantum walks, which can be used to simulate Dirac particles. In particular, we look at fermion doubling in these models, in which high-momentum states yield additional low-energy solutions which behave like Dirac particles. The presence of doublers car…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012208] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fermion doubling in Dirac quantum walks, a discrete spacetime model for simulating Dirac particles.
motivation: Fermion doubling is a known issue in lattice field theories where extra low-energy solutions appear; understanding it in quantum walks is important for quantum simulation.
method: The authors analyze the dispersion relation of Dirac quantum walks on a lattice and identify conditions under which doublers appear.
result: They show that fermion doubling occurs in a wide class of quantum walks and characterize the number and properties of doublers.
conclusion: Fermion doubling is a generic feature of Dirac quantum walks, which may limit their use for simulating relativistic quantum physics without additional modifications.

title: Access-limited Equilibration And Observable-dependent Relaxation In Lattice-gas Systems
authors: Marvin A. Albao
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin A. Albao

We investigate equilibration dynamics in a lattice-gas model with spatially restricted coupling to a particle reservoir. Using kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, we isolate the role of reservoir-access geometry by comparing spatially uniform exchange with exchange confined to a limited access region w…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014124] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibration dynamics in a lattice-gas model with spatially restricted coupling to a particle reservoir using kinetic Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand how the geometry of reservoir access affects equilibration and relaxation in many-body systems.
method: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations comparing spatially uniform exchange with exchange confined to a limited access region.
result: The access-limited geometry leads to observable-dependent relaxation and slower equilibration.
conclusion: Spatial constraints on reservoir coupling significantly influence non-equilibrium dynamics, with implications for understanding relaxation in confined systems.

title: Critical States Preparation In Light-matter Systems With Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jia-Wen Yu, Yiming Yu, Ke-Xiong Yan, Jun-Hao Lin, Jie Song, Ye-Hong Chen, And Yan Xia
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-Wen Yu, Yiming Yu, Ke-Xiong Yan, Jun-Hao Lin, Jie Song, Ye-Hong Chen, and Yan Xia

The fast and efficient preparation of quantum critical states is a challenging yet crucial task for various quantum technologies. This difficulty is most particularly for systems near a quantum phase transition, where the closure of the energy gap fundamentally limits the timescale of adiabatic proc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033063] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep reinforcement learning to prepare quantum critical states in light-matter systems, focusing on fast state preparation near quantum phase transitions.
motivation: Preparing quantum critical states is challenging due to the closing energy gap near phase transitions, which limits adiabatic timescales. The authors aim to overcome this using reinforcement learning.
method: They employ a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to design control pulses that drive a light-matter system into a critical state, optimizing for speed and fidelity.
result: The reinforcement learning approach achieves faster preparation of critical states compared to traditional adiabatic methods, with high fidelity.
conclusion: Deep reinforcement learning offers an efficient alternative for preparing quantum critical states, which may benefit quantum technologies relying on such states.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in two dimensions is challenging due to the difficulty of performing non-Clifford gates without braiding. The authors aim to overcome this by leveraging non-Abelian phases.
method: The method involves temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform complex logic gates, then returning to the original phase.
result: The approach enables universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D without the need for braiding or complicated procedures.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation using 2D architectures.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is a key challenge; this work aims to address it using parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
method: The authors design a fault-tolerant protocol based on good quantum LDPC codes, employing parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation to reduce overhead.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, demonstrating improved efficiency for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes enable more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation, potentially advancing practical quantum computing.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing protocols have high overhead. This work aims to reduce overhead by leveraging nonlocal connectivity.
method: The authors propose a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states through transversal gates and lattice surgery.
result: The protocol achieves significantly lower spacetime overhead compared to standard distillation methods, particularly for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a practical path to reduce resource requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a cold Rydberg gas platform.
motivation: Non-Hermitian topology is a new frontier in quantum physics, and cold Rydberg gases offer a tunable dissipative many-body system to explore it.
method: The authors use a cold Rydberg gas as a dissipative many-body platform and map out non-Hermitian spectral topology by measuring winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, confirming non-Hermitian topological behavior.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that cold Rydberg gases are a viable platform for studying non-Hermitian topology, opening new avenues for topological physics in dissipative systems.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code using twisted color circuits and a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing requires efficient implementation of non-Clifford gates on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings, which is challenging for color codes.
method: The authors design twisted color circuits that enable non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, and use a just-in-time decoder to achieve fault tolerance.
result: A family of scalable circuits is presented that can perform universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings.
conclusion: The proposed circuits provide a practical path toward fault-tolerant universal quantum computing on planar color code architectures.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear criteria to assess the protection and feasibility of Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to define Majorana bound states in interacting systems and compute measures of robustness and locality.
result: They provide quantitative criteria to distinguish topological Majorana modes from trivial Andreev bound states, and assess their suitability for braiding.
conclusion: The work offers practical tools to evaluate Majorana-based qubit platforms, but the focus is on topological qubit hardware rather than quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Physics From The Hubbard Model: A Floquet-Engineering Approach
authors: Charles Creffield, Fernando Sols, Marco Schirò, And Nathan Goldman
abstract:
Author(s): Charles Creffield, Fernando Sols, Marco Schirò, and Nathan Goldman

Ultracold atoms in an optical lattice could emulate a prominent model of quantum matter linked to black holes and high-temperature superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046302] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a Floquet-engineering approach to realize the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model in ultracold atoms in an optical lattice, linking to black holes and high-temperature superconductors.
motivation: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model is a prominent model of quantum matter with connections to black holes and high-temperature superconductors, but its experimental realization is challenging. The authors aim to emulate it using ultracold atoms in an optical lattice via Floquet engineering.
method: The authors design a Floquet-engineering scheme to generate the necessary interactions in a Hubbard model with ultracold atoms, using periodic driving to simulate the SYK model's random all-to-all interactions.
result: They show that the Floquet-engineered system reproduces key features of the SYK model, such as maximal chaos and a non-Fermi liquid state, as evidenced by out-of-time-order correlators and spectral functions.
conclusion: This work provides a feasible experimental platform to study SYK physics, offering insights into quantum chaos and holography, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Signatures Of Superfluidity And Shear Rigidity In Different Phases Of A Dipolar Bose-Einstein Condensate
authors: Soumyadeep Halder, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Axel Pelster, And B. Prasanna Venkatesh

We show that a sudden change in the polarization direction of the magnetic dipole moments of the atoms in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) can serve as a useful dynamical probe to sense its superfluid and solid-like properties. We find that for small angular deviation of the polarization dir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013314] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a sudden change in polarization direction of magnetic dipoles in a dipolar BEC to probe superfluid and solid-like properties.
motivation: To develop a dynamical probe that can sense superfluidity and shear rigidity in different phases of a dipolar BEC.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the response of a dipolar BEC to a sudden small angular deviation of the polarization direction, studying the resulting dynamics.
result: They find that the dynamical response exhibits signatures that distinguish between superfluid and solid-like phases.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a useful tool for characterizing phases in dipolar BECs.

V. …

tldr: This paper studies subexponential relaxation of density waves in a facilitated classical lattice gas due to nonlinear long-time tails.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in interacting many-body systems is a fundamental problem in statistical mechanics, with implications for transport and thermalization.

conclusion: Nonlinear effects can qualitatively change relaxation dynamics in classical lattice gases, highlighting the importance of beyond-linear theories for transport.

title: Signatures Of Infinite Randomness In Transport Properties Of Strongly Disordered Spin Chains

We study the spin transport properties of some disordered spin chains with a special focus on the distribution of the frequency-dependent spin conductivity. In the cases of interest here, the systems are governed by an effectively infinite disorder at low energies. A hallmark of this behavior is the…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014206] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin transport in strongly disordered spin chains, focusing on the distribution of frequency-dependent spin conductivity and signatures of infinite randomness.
motivation: Understanding transport in disordered quantum systems is important for many-body physics, but the paper's focus on spin conductivity in disordered chains is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze spin transport properties using theoretical and numerical methods, examining the distribution of spin conductivity in the presence of strong disorder.
result: They find signatures of infinite randomness in the transport properties, characterized by broad distributions of conductivity.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of disordered quantum systems but does not address information-theoretic or thermodynamic aspects relevant to the user's research directions.

title: Fault-tolerant Quantum Circuits On Connectivity-constrained Hardware With swap Gates
authors: Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, And Hui Khoon Ng
abstract:
Author(s): Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, and Hui Khoon Ng

In near-term quantum computing devices, connectivity between qubits remain limited by architectural constraints. A computational circuit with given connectivity requirements necessary for multiqubit gates has to be embedded within physical hardware with fixed connectivity. Long-distance gates have t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033081] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to compile quantum circuits onto connectivity-constrained hardware using SWAP gates, optimizing for fault-tolerant implementations.
motivation: Near-term quantum devices have limited qubit connectivity, requiring SWAP gates to enable multi-qubit gates between non-adjacent qubits. Efficient compilation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors develop a heuristic algorithm that maps logical qubits to physical qubits and inserts SWAP gates to satisfy connectivity constraints, while minimizing the overhead for fault-tolerant error correction.
result: The algorithm reduces the number of SWAP gates compared to existing methods, leading to lower error rates and improved circuit fidelity on realistic noise models.
conclusion: The proposed compilation technique enhances the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computation on current and near-term hardware with limited connectivity.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly to implement. The paper aims to find a more efficient method to reduce T-count.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that exploits commuting structures in quantum circuits, allowing multiple Pauli rotations to be combined or reordered to reduce T-count.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces the T-count compared to existing methods, as demonstrated on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: The multiproduct commutation relation provides a new tool for optimizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits, potentially lowering the resource overhead for quantum computation.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong electronic correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel quantum phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory, time-resolved spectroscopy, and pump-probe techniques.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and nonthermal orders such as superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich playground for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Transient Localization From Fractionalization: Vanishingly Small Energy Transport In Gapless Quantum Magnets
authors: Shi Feng, Penghao Zhu, Johannes Knolle, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Shi Feng, Penghao Zhu, Johannes Knolle, and Michael Knap

Disorder-free localization is usually associated with dynamics far from equilibrium. Here, the authors uncover a new mechanism in the low-energy sector of clean, gapless quantum magnets: transient localization from mass-imbalanced fractionalization. Studying the dynamical response in the gapless phase of a translation-invariant Kitaev ladder model, they show that fractionalization creates a coherent superposition of quasistatic flux-disorder configurations in the ground state, preserving translation symmetry while strongly suppressing correlation spreading and energy transport.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034423] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers a new mechanism of transient localization from fractionalization in clean, gapless quantum magnets, leading to vanishingly small energy transport.
motivation: Understanding energy transport in low-dimensional quantum magnets is important for fundamental physics and potential applications, but disorder-free localization typically requires far-from-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors study a translation-invariant Kitaev ladder model in its gapless phase, analyzing the dynamical response and showing that fractionalization creates a coherent superposition of quasistatic flux-disorder configurations.
result: They find that despite preserving translation symmetry, the fractionalization strongly suppresses correlation spreading and energy transport, leading to transient localization.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for localization in clean systems, which may have implications for understanding thermalization and transport in quantum materials.

title: Relaxation Toward An Ideal Chern Band Through Coupling To A Markovian Bath
authors: Bruno Mera And Tomoki Ozawa
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Mera and Tomoki Ozawa

We propose a microscopic, weak-coupling mechanism by which generic Chern bands asymptotically relax toward ideal bands. We consider coupling interacting electrons to a Caldeira-Leggett-like Ohmic bosonic bath. Using the Born-Markov approximation, we analytically show that, upon taking the leading or…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046601] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for Chern bands to relax toward ideal bands via coupling to a Markovian bath, using a Caldeira-Leggett model and Born-Markov approximation.
motivation: Ideal Chern bands are important for fractional Chern insulators, but realistic systems often deviate from ideal conditions; the authors aim to show that coupling to a bath can drive relaxation toward ideal bands.
method: They consider interacting electrons in a Chern band coupled to an Ohmic bosonic bath, derive a master equation using the Born-Markov approximation, and analyze the steady state.
result: Under weak coupling and leading order, the system relaxes to a state that approximates an ideal Chern band, with corrections that can be controlled.
conclusion: The proposed mechanism provides a practical route to realize ideal Chern bands in experiments, potentially enabling fractional Chern insulator physics.

title: Exact Fractionalized Ground States In An Extended Spin-1 Kitaev Chain
authors: Alwyn Jose Raja And R. Ganesh
abstract:
Author(s): Alwyn Jose Raja and R. Ganesh

Inspired by the Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki (AKLT) model, we present exact solutions for a spin-1 chain with Kitaev-like couplings. We consider an expanded Kitaev model with bilinear and biquadratic terms. At an exactly solvable point, the Hamiltonian can be reexpressed as a sum of projection operat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046701] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: Exact fractionalized ground states in an extended spin-1 Kitaev chain with AKLT-like interactions.
motivation: To find exact solutions for spin-1 chains with Kitaev-like couplings, inspired by the AKLT model.
method: Constructs an extended Kitaev model with bilinear and biquadratic terms, reexpressing the Hamiltonian as a sum of projection operators at an exactly solvable point.
result: Obtains exact fractionalized ground states and characterizes their properties.
conclusion: The model provides a new exactly solvable spin chain with fractionalized excitations, relevant to condensed matter physics.

title: Symmetry-adapted Energy Estimation On Quantum Devices
authors: Kosuke Nogaki, Steffen Backes, Tomonori Shirakawa, Seiji Yunoki, And Ryotaro Arita
abstract:
Author(s): Kosuke Nogaki, Steffen Backes, Tomonori Shirakawa, Seiji Yunoki, and Ryotaro Arita

We present a symmetry-adapted extension of quantum selected configuration interaction and sample-based quantum diagonalization that rigorously embeds space-group symmetry into the many-body subspace sampled by quantum hardware. The method is benchmarked on the two-leg ladder Hubbard model using both…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065124] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a symmetry-adapted quantum algorithm for estimating ground state energies of lattice models on quantum devices.
motivation: Quantum computing for quantum chemistry and condensed matter requires efficient methods to compute ground state energies, but current approaches suffer from high resource costs.
method: The authors extend quantum selected configuration interaction and sample-based quantum diagonalization by embedding space-group symmetry into the many-body subspace sampled by quantum hardware.
result: Benchmarks on the two-leg ladder Hubbard model demonstrate improved accuracy and reduced computational cost compared to standard methods.
conclusion: Symmetry-adapted techniques can enhance the performance of quantum algorithms for strongly correlated systems, making them more practical for near-term quantum devices.

title: Higher-order Topological Superconductivity And Electrically Tunable Majorana Corner Modes In Monolayer $\mathrm{Mn}X{\mathrm{Pb}}_{2}\text{−}\mathrm{Pb}$ ($X=\mathrm{Se}$, Te) Heterostructure
authors: Yongting Shi, Qing Wang, Zhen-Guo Fu, Ping Zhang, And Ning Hao

Here we propose a symmetry-enforced higher-order topological superconductivity based on …

tldr: Proposes a heterostructure hosting higher-order topological superconductivity with electrically tunable Majorana corner modes.
motivation: To realize scalable and controllable Majorana networks without vortices or magnetic flux for topological quantum computing.
method: First-principles calculations and symmetry analysis of a monolayer MnXPb2-Pb heterostructure to predict higher-order topological superconductivity.
result: Predicts Majorana corner modes that can be electrically tuned via gate voltage.
conclusion: The proposed heterostructure provides a platform for Majorana-based quantum computing with electrical control.

title: Insertion Space In Repulsive Active Matter
authors: Luke K. Davis And Karel Proesmans
abstract:
Author(s): Luke K. Davis and Karel Proesmans

The statistical geometry of active repulsive (or hard) rods and disks is explored using both theory and simulations. It is found that increasing the persistence of the active particle motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area: the averaged space available to place another particle without overlaps. As a result, the insertion space also becomes more connected in the presence of activity.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032007] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the statistical geometry of active repulsive rods and disks, finding that activity increases insertion volume and connectivity.
motivation: To understand how active motion affects the geometry of available space in repulsive particle systems, which is relevant to active matter physics.
method: Combines theoretical analysis with simulations of active repulsive rods and disks, measuring insertion volume and surface area as functions of persistence.
result: Increasing persistence of active motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area, making the insertion space more connected.
conclusion: Activity significantly alters the statistical geometry of repulsive active matter, with implications for packing and transport in such systems.

title: Quantum Solver For Single-impurity Anderson Models With Particle-hole Symmetry
authors: M. Karabin, T. Sohail, D. Bykov, E. A. Coello Pérez, S. Ghosh, M. Gopalakrishnan Meena, S. Kim, A. Shehata, I.-S. Suh, H. Terletska, And M. Eisenbach
abstract:

motivation: Solving the Anderson impurity model is classically intractable for large bath sizes, limiting DMFT simulations of strongly correlated materials.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit that exploits particle-hole symmetry to reduce qubit requirements and implement a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) to find the ground state of the impurity model.
result: Numerical simulations show that the quantum solver can accurately reproduce the impurity spectral function and self-energy for small systems, with potential scaling advantages.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a proof-of-principle quantum approach for DMFT, but practical advantages require fault-tolerant quantum hardware.

result: The algorithm achieves provable exponential speedup over classical methods for certain input classes.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum dynamics, with connections to quantum computation.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to experimental recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible behaviors and demonstrate that abstract theoretical principles can have predictive power in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a quantitative bridge between neural data and theoretical models, advancing our understanding of brain function.

motivation: Understanding strongly correlated SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models is important for ultracold atom experiments, but theoretical knowledge at finite doping is limited.
method: The authors investigate the strong-coupling limit of the SU(3) symmetric Fermi-Hubbard model using numerical techniques.
result: They find magnetic correlations and possibly novel phases in the doped triangular lattice.
conclusion: The work provides insights into SU(3) magnetism but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: They identify a quantum critical point associated with a structural phase transition and discuss its implications for superconductivity.

title: Scaling Of Relaxation And Entropy In Buckled Colloidal Monolayers
authors: Yongming Zhang, Qingyu Qu, Qian-Yuan Tang, And Xiaoguang Ma

By extracting spin configurations directly from a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, entropy scaling laws for liquids and glasses are extended to the domain of spin systems, revealing a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.
