tldr: This paper studies entropy scaling laws in a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, finding a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.
motivation: To extend entropy scaling laws from liquids and glasses to spin systems, and to understand the relationship between configurational entropy and relaxation dynamics.
method: Extracting spin configurations directly from a colloidal monolayer that mimics a 2D Ising lattice, and analyzing the configurational entropy and relaxation times.
result: A universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time is observed.
conclusion: The entropy scaling laws for liquids and glasses can be extended to spin systems, providing insight into the role of entropy in relaxation processes.

title: Imprints Of Asymptotic Freedom On Confining Strings
authors: Jan Albert And Alexandre Homrich
abstract:
Author(s): Jan Albert and Alexandre Homrich

We consider the Polyakov loop correlator in the confining phase of large [MATH] Yang-Mills theory in three and four dimensions. It can be computed by summing over the exchange of closed flux tubes winding around the thermal cycle. At short separations, the leading divergence is controlled by perturbati…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041601] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Polyakov loop correlator in large N Yang-Mills theory, focusing on the imprint of asymptotic freedom on confining strings.
motivation: To understand how asymptotic freedom affects the short-distance behavior of confining strings in non-Abelian gauge theories.
method: The authors compute the Polyakov loop correlator in the confining phase using a sum over closed flux tubes, incorporating perturbative and non-perturbative effects.
result: They find that the leading divergence at short separations is controlled by perturbative asymptotic freedom, leaving an imprint on the string tension and spectrum.
conclusion: The work provides a connection between perturbative asymptotic freedom and non-perturbative confining string properties, but is primarily a high-energy physics result without direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Heavy-Fermion Phase Diagram In Magic-Angle Twisted Trilayer Graphene
authors: Le Zhang, Wenqiang Zhou, Xinjie Fang, Zhen Zhan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yi-Feng Yang, And Shuigang Xu

conclusion: Twisted trilayer graphene provides a platform for studying heavy-fermion physics.

title: Simulating Fermionic Fractional Chern Insulators With Infinite Projected Entangled-Pair States
authors: Hao Chen, Titus Neupert, And Juraj Hasik
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Chen, Titus Neupert, and Juraj Hasik

Infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPSs) provide a powerful variational framework for two-dimensional quantum matter and have been widely used to capture bosonic topological order, including chiral spin liquids. Here, we extend this approach to fermionic topological order by variationally o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046502] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) to simulate fermionic fractional Chern insulators, extending bosonic topological order methods to fermionic systems.
motivation: Fractional Chern insulators are of interest for topological quantum computation, but simulating fermionic versions is challenging. The authors aim to develop a variational method for fermionic topological order.
method: They extend the iPEPS framework to fermionic systems by incorporating fermionic tensor networks and optimizing the ansatz for the ground state of a fermionic fractional Chern insulator model.
result: The iPEPS approach successfully captures the topological properties of fermionic fractional Chern insulators, including ground-state degeneracy and anyonic excitations.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that iPEPS is a viable tool for studying fermionic topological phases, opening the door to further investigations of strongly correlated fermionic systems.

title: Bridging Constrained Random-Phase Approximation And Linear Response Theory For Computing Hubbard Parameters
authors: Alberto Carta, Iurii Timrov, Sophie Beck, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Carta, Iurii Timrov, Sophie Beck, and Claude Ederer

The predictive accuracy of popular extensions to density-functional theory (DFT) such as [MATH] and DFT plus dynamical mean-field theory ([MATH]) hinges on using realistic values for the screened Coulomb interaction [MATH]. Here, we present a systematic comparison of the…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046503] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares methods for computing Hubbard U parameters in DFT+U and DFT+DMFT, focusing on constrained random-phase approximation and linear response theory.
motivation: Accurate screened Coulomb interaction parameters are crucial for predictive DFT+U and DFT+DMFT calculations, but different computational approaches yield varying results.
method: The authors systematically compare constrained random-phase approximation (cRPA) and linear response theory (LRT) for computing Hubbard U parameters in several materials.

conclusion: The work provides guidance for choosing and computing Hubbard U parameters, improving the accuracy of correlated electronic structure methods.

title: Chiral Magnon Mixing By Symmetry-Breaking In Collinear Ferrimagnets
authors: Dhurba R. Jaishi, Tyler J. Slade, S. X. M. Riberolles, Bing Li, Tianxiong Han, D. M. Pajerowski, D. L. Abernathy, Barry Winn, Melissa Graves-Brook, B. G. Ueland, And R. J. Mcqueeney

Magnons in ferromagnets possess spin angular momentum defined by right-handed precession of the moment around the magnetization direction. In antiferromagnets with no net magnetization, left- and right-handed magnons are degenerate in the absence of an applied field. Ferrimagnets possess uncompensat…

tldr: This paper studies chiral magnon mixing due to symmetry-breaking in collinear ferrimagnets using neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the spin dynamics and magnon properties in ferrimagnets, which are important for spintronics but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Neutron scattering experiments and theoretical modeling of magnon dispersions in ferrimagnetic materials.
result: Observation of chiral magnon mixing and splitting due to symmetry-breaking effects.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into magnon behavior in ferrimagnets but have no clear connection to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Anomalous Reflection Phase Of Slot Plasmons In An $\mathrm{AlGaN}/\mathrm{GaN}$ Plasmonic Crystal
authors: A. R. Khisameeva, D. A. Khudaiberdiev, I. M. Moiseenko, P. A. Gusikhin, A. S. Astrakhantseva, A. Shuvaev, A. Pimenov, D. A. Svintsov, I. V. Kukushkin, And V. M. Muravev
abstract:
Author(s): A. R. Khisameeva, D. A. Khudaiberdiev, I. M. Moiseenko, P. A. Gusikhin, A. S. Astrakhantseva, A. Shuvaev, A. Pimenov, D. A. Svintsov, I. V. Kukushkin, and V. M. Muravev

We experimentally investigate the terahertz spectrum of plasma excitations in a plasmonic crystal based on AlGaN/GaN two-dimensional electron system (2DES). While screened plasmon modes with linear dispersion are readily observed in such structures, unscreened modes localized in the slots between th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046901] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies terahertz plasma excitations in an AlGaN/GaN plasmonic crystal, focusing on anomalous reflection phase of slot plasmons.
motivation: To understand the properties of plasma excitations in two-dimensional electron systems, particularly unscreened slot plasmon modes, which are relevant for terahertz device applications.
method: Terahertz spectroscopy measurements on a plasmonic crystal based on AlGaN/GaN heterostructure, analyzing reflection phase and dispersion of slot plasmons.
result: Observation of anomalous reflection phase behavior of slot plasmons, indicating strong confinement and unique dispersion characteristics.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into plasmonic modes in semiconductor heterostructures, with potential implications for terahertz photonics.

title: Interference And Short-Range Correlation In Fermionic Hubbard Gases
authors: Yan-Song Zhu, Hou-Ji Shao, Yu-Xuan Wang, De-Zhi Zhu, Hao-Nan Sun, Si-Yuan Chen, Chi Zhang, Xing-Can Yao, Yu-Ao Chen, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Song Zhu, Hou-Ji Shao, Yu-Xuan Wang, De-Zhi Zhu, Hao-Nan Sun, Si-Yuan Chen, Chi Zhang, Xing-Can Yao, Yu-Ao Chen, and Jian-Wei Pan

The interference patterns of ultracold atoms, observed after ballistic expansion from optical lattices, encode essential information about strongly correlated lattice systems, including phase coherence and nonlocal correlations. While the interference of lattice bosons has been extensively investiga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033401] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interference patterns and short-range correlations in fermionic Hubbard gases after ballistic expansion from optical lattices.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated lattice systems, particularly fermionic ones, is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors experimentally observe interference patterns of ultracold fermionic atoms released from optical lattices and analyze the visibility and correlation functions.
result: They extract information about phase coherence and nonlocal correlations in the fermionic Hubbard model.
conclusion: The work provides insights into fermionic lattice systems but does not advance quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Chirality Cannot Be Ferroic In Phase Transitions Leading To Enantiomorphic Space-Group Pairs
authors: F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. Mccabe, A. H. Romero, And E. Bousquet
abstract:
Author(s): F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. McCabe, A. H. Romero, and E. Bousquet

With growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. In the work described, we demonstrate, by means of a formal group-theoretical proof and a systematic group-subgroup analysis, that achiral-to-chiral …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036103] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that chirality cannot be a ferroic order parameter in structural phase transitions leading to enantiomorphic space-group pairs.
motivation: There is growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, and it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. The authors aim to clarify this possibility.
method: The authors use formal group-theoretical proof and systematic group-subgroup analysis to examine achiral-to-chiral phase transitions.
result: They demonstrate that chirality cannot be ferroic in such transitions, contradicting the suggestion that chirality could be a ferroic order parameter.
conclusion: Chirality is not a ferroic property in the context of structural phase transitions leading to enantiomorphic space-group pairs, settling the debate.

title: Antiferromagnetism And Stripe Channel Order In The $\mathrm{SU}(N)$-Symmetric Two-Channel Kondo Lattice Model
authors: Elyasaf Y. Cohen, Fakher F. Assaad, And Snir Gazit
abstract:
Author(s): Elyasaf Y. Cohen, Fakher F. Assaad, and Snir Gazit

We carry out large-scale, sign-problem-free determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the square lattice [MATH]-symmetric two-channel Kondo lattice model at half-filling. We map out the zero-temperature phase diagram for [MATH], 4, 6, and 8, as a function of the Kondo coupling strength…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036504] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the phase diagram of an SU(N)-symmetric two-channel Kondo lattice model using quantum Monte Carlo simulations, focusing on antiferromagnetism and stripe channel order.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated electron systems and exotic phases in Kondo lattice models is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Large-scale, sign-problem-free determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations are performed on a square lattice for various N and Kondo coupling strengths.
result: The zero-temperature phase diagram is mapped out, revealing antiferromagnetic and stripe channel ordered phases.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the competition between Kondo screening and magnetic ordering in multi-channel Kondo lattices.

title: Spin-Triplet Paired Wigner Crystal Stabilized By Quantum Geometry
authors: Dmitry Zverevich, Alex Levchenko, And Ilya Esterlis

We have used variational states to analyze the effects of band geometry on the two-dimensional Wigner crystal with one and two electrons per unit cell. At sufficiently low electron densities, we find that increasing Berry curvature drives a transition into a crystalline state composed of spin-triple…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036506] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a spin-triplet paired Wigner crystal stabilized by quantum geometry in a two-dimensional electron system.
motivation: To understand the effects of band geometry and Berry curvature on the Wigner crystal phase in low-density electron systems.
method: Variational wavefunction analysis for Wigner crystals with one and two electrons per unit cell, incorporating band geometry effects.
result: Increasing Berry curvature drives a transition to a crystalline state composed of spin-triplet pairs.
conclusion: Quantum geometry can stabilize novel paired crystalline phases in two-dimensional electron systems.

title: Harnessing Spin-Texture Dynamics For Low-Noise, High-Sensitivity Magnetic Sensors
authors: Kang Wang, Teng Xu, Meng Shi, Xinxiang Sun, Yizhou Liu, Huali Yang, Run-Wei Li, And Haifeng Du
abstract:
Author(s): Kang Wang, Teng Xu, Meng Shi, Xinxiang Sun, Yizhou Liu, Huali Yang, Run-Wei Li, and Haifeng Du

The development of low-noise, high-sensitivity magnetic sensors is essential for applications such as automotive systems, biomedical imaging, and magnetic microscopy. However, sensor performance has long been impeded by a fundamental constraint that noise and sensitivity increase concomitantly, whic…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036705] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to break the noise-sensitivity trade-off in magnetic sensors by exploiting spin-texture dynamics.
motivation: Magnetic sensors are limited by a fundamental trade-off between noise and sensitivity; the authors aim to overcome this constraint.
method: They utilize spin-texture dynamics, likely involving skyrmions or domain walls, to achieve simultaneous low noise and high sensitivity.
result: The proposed sensor demonstrates improved performance, breaking the conventional trade-off.
conclusion: Spin-texture dynamics offer a promising route for next-generation magnetic sensors.

title: Entangled Two-photon Absorption In Cesium Atoms And The Limitations Of The Far-off-resonance Approximation
authors: Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, And Mayerlin Nuñez Portela
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, and Mayerlin Nuñez Portela

The discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in the process of entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) are not fully understood. Atomic systems are a promising alternative for investigating this process without the systematic effects present in molecules. We present a theoretical st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013120] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms, focusing on limitations of the far-off-resonance approximation.
motivation: Discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in entangled two-photon absorption are not fully understood; atomic systems offer a cleaner testbed than molecules.
method: A theoretical study of entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms, analyzing the far-off-resonance approximation and its limitations.
result: The far-off-resonance approximation is found to be inadequate for describing entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms under certain conditions.
conclusion: Atomic systems can help resolve discrepancies in entangled two-photon absorption, but improved theoretical models beyond the far-off-resonance approximation are needed.

title: Control Of Ion-photoelectron Entanglement In Rabi Oscillations By Time-delayed Pulses
authors: Yutong Deng, Xu Zhang, Jia Tan, Mingrui He, Peixiang Lu, And Yueming Zhou
abstract:

tldr: This paper studies ion-photoelectron entanglement in Rabi oscillations driven by time-delayed laser pulses in helium photoionization.
motivation: To understand and control entanglement dynamics in photoionization processes, which is fundamental for quantum control and attosecond science.
method: Numerical solution of the two-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation for helium driven by a pair of time-delayed laser pulses.
result: Photoelectron spectra exhibit Grobe–Eberly doublet structures, indicating entanglement between the ion and photoelectron.
conclusion: Time-delayed pulses can control the degree of ion-photoelectron entanglement, offering a tool for quantum state engineering in photoionization.

title: Spin-orbit-coupling-induced Geometric Squeezing In Rotating Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Fei Zhu, Chunxia Guo, Rui Zhang, Lianghui Huang, Ren Zhang, And Li Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Zhu, Chunxia Guo, Rui Zhang, Lianghui Huang, Ren Zhang, and Li Chen

Squeezed states play a key role in diverse frontiers of quantum physics. Geometrically squeezed states, squeezed states in the orbital phase space of rotating Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs), have been conventionally generated by anisotropic-trapping potentials. In this work, we propose a different…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013316] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes generating geometric squeezed states in rotating Bose-Einstein condensates via spin-orbit coupling instead of anisotropic trapping.
motivation: Geometric squeezing in rotating BECs is conventionally achieved with anisotropic traps; this work explores an alternative mechanism using spin-orbit coupling.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a rotating BEC with spin-orbit coupling, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and calculating the squeezing parameter in the orbital phase space.
result: Spin-orbit coupling can induce geometric squeezing comparable to or exceeding that from anisotropic traps, with tunable parameters.
conclusion: Spin-orbit coupling offers a new route to generate squeezed states in rotating BECs, potentially useful for quantum sensing.

title: Optical Repumping And Controlled Population Transfer In A Two-color Magneto-optical Trap
authors: Shubha Deutschle, Lőrinc Sárkány, Milán János Negyedi, József Fortágh, Andreas Günther, And Philippe Wilhelm Courteille

We study a repumping transition for [MATH] atoms trapped in a blue magneto-optical trap. We show that, while the repumping efficiency is about three orders of magnitude smaller than for traditional schemes, it is sufficient for recycling all atoms, provided the repumping laser beams are …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013715] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an optical repumping scheme for atoms in a two-color magneto-optical trap, focusing on experimental efficiency and population transfer.
motivation: To explore alternative repumping transitions for magneto-optical traps that may offer advantages in certain atomic species or experimental configurations.
method: Experimental study of a repumping transition in a blue magneto-optical trap, measuring repumping efficiency and comparing with traditional schemes.
result: The repumping efficiency is about three orders of magnitude smaller than traditional schemes, but still sufficient for recycling all atoms with appropriate laser beam parameters.
conclusion: The proposed repumping scheme is viable for atom trapping, though less efficient, and may be useful in specific contexts where traditional repumping is not feasible.

title: Observation Of Nonlinear Spin Dynamics In Dual-cell Atomic Gases
authors: Xiaofan Wang, Haitao Lu, Hengyan Wang, Zhihuang Luo, And Wenqiang Zheng

tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of nonlinear spin dynamics in dual-cell atomic gases, focusing on spin masers and time crystals.
motivation: Nonlinear spin systems exhibit rich dynamical phenomena with applications in precision measurement and time crystals, but experimental realizations are challenging.
method: The authors use a dual-cell atomic gas setup to observe nonlinear spin dynamics, likely involving optical pumping and spin-exchange collisions.
result: They observe nonlinear dynamical phases predicted by recent theory, demonstrating controlled spin dynamics in a dual-cell configuration.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence for nonlinear spin dynamics, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Non-Abelian Topological Charges Determined By Euler Class
authors: Yu Huang, Jiayun Ning, Keran Hu, Linsheng Bao, Aoqian Shi, Shilong Li, And Jianjun Liu

Here we present a practical and intuitive approach for determining the non-Abelian topological charge of a defect based on its associated two-ba…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013515] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to determine non-Abelian topological charges using the Euler class in multi-band systems.
motivation: Non-Abelian defects in multi-band systems are important for topological phases, but determining their topological charges is challenging.
method: The authors propose a practical approach based on the Euler class of two-band subsystems to compute the non-Abelian topological charge.
result: They demonstrate the method on specific models and show that the Euler class correctly captures the non-Abelian charge.
conclusion: The Euler class provides an intuitive and practical way to determine non-Abelian topological charges in multi-band systems.

title: Enantiosensitive Exceptional Points In Open Chiral Systems
authors: Nicola Mayer, Alexander Löhr, Nimrod Moiseyev, Misha Ivanov, And Olga Smirnova
abstract:
Author(s): Nicola Mayer, Alexander Löhr, Nimrod Moiseyev, Misha Ivanov, and Olga Smirnova

Exceptional points (EPs) are remarkable spectral degeneracies in a non-Hermitian system's parameter space, where both eigenvalues and eigenstates coalesce. tldr: This paper shows that exceptional points in non-Hermitian molecular chiral systems are enantiomer-specific, enabling enantiosensitive discrimination.
motivation: To exploit exceptional points for distinguishing molecular enantiomers, which is important for chiral chemistry and physics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian describing a chiral molecule coupled to a cavity, demonstrating that the positions of exceptional points depend on molecular handedness.
result: Exceptional points occur at different parameter values for left- and right-handed enantiomers, providing a new mechanism for chiral discrimination.
conclusion: Exceptional points in open chiral systems offer a sensitive tool for enantiodetection, with potential applications in analytical chemistry and fundamental physics.

title: Mobility-edge-embedded Hofstadter Butterfly From A Tilt-induced Quasiperiodic Potential
authors: Sanghoon Lee And Kyoung-Min Kim
abstract:

The Hofstadter butterfly (HB) and mobility edges (MEs) are hallmark phenomena of quasiperiodic systems, yet their interplay remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate their coexistence within a tilt-induced quasiperiodic potential on a square lattice, giving rise to a “mobility-edge-embedded Hofstadter b…

tldr: This paper studies the coexistence of Hofstadter butterfly and mobility edges in a tilt-induced quasiperiodic potential on a square lattice.
motivation: The interplay between Hofstadter butterfly and mobility edges in quasiperiodic systems has remained elusive, motivating this study.
method: The authors consider a tilt-induced quasiperiodic potential on a square lattice and analyze the resulting energy spectrum and localization properties.
result: They demonstrate the coexistence of Hofstadter butterfly and mobility edges, leading to a 'mobility-edge-embedded Hofstadter butterfly'.
conclusion: The work reveals a new phenomenon in quasiperiodic systems, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Localization And Flat Bands In Bond-inflated Lattices
authors: Richard Berkovits
abstract:
Author(s): Richard Berkovits

We study localization and flat-band formation in lattices generated by repeated bond inflation of square, honeycomb, and triangular parent lattices. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 014208] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization and flat-band formation in bond-inflated lattices, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how bond inflation in lattices leads to flat bands and localization, which are of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors generate lattices by repeatedly replacing each bond with a finite tight-binding chain and analyze the resulting band structures and localization properties.
result: They identify several classes of flat bands, including chain-induced flat bands at specific eigenenergies, and observe localization phenomena in these inflated lattices.
conclusion: Bond inflation provides a systematic way to engineer flat bands and localization in lattice systems, with potential applications in strongly correlated physics.

title: Magnetic Field Induced Magnon Portfolio In The Van Der Waals Magnet CrOCl
authors: T. Riccardi, F. Le Mardélé, L. A. Veyrat de Lachenal, A. Pawbake, I. Plutnarova, Z. Sofer, G. Jacquet, F. Petot, A. Saúl, B. Grémaud, A. L. Barra, M. Orlita, J. Coraux, C. Faugeras, And B. A. Piot
abstract:

Magnonic excitations are investigated in the CrOCl van der Waals (vdW) antiferromagnet with absorption experiments in a broad continuous energy range. In an external magnetic field, the dispersions of magnon branches characteristic of different magnetic orders are subsequently observed, revealing a strong biaxial anisotropy, hysteretic magnon spectra, as well as the formation of spatially separated magnetic phases. Theexperiments here show that competing exchange interactions broaden the options to generate different kinds of magnonic excitations within the same vdW material.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024419] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnon excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrOCl under magnetic fields, revealing biaxial anisotropy and hysteretic magnon spectra.
motivation: To understand magnonic excitations in van der Waals antiferromagnets and explore how competing exchange interactions can generate diverse magnon modes.
method: Absorption experiments in a broad continuous energy range under external magnetic fields, combined with analysis of magnon dispersions.
result: Observation of multiple magnon branches corresponding to different magnetic orders, strong biaxial anisotropy, hysteretic magnon spectra, and spatially separated magnetic phases.
conclusion: Competing exchange interactions in CrOCl broaden the options for generating different magnonic excitations within the same van der Waals material.

title: Machine Learning Protocol To Identify Pairing Symmetries Via Quasiparticle Interference Imaging In Ising Superconductors

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024511] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to identify pairing symmetries in Ising superconductors from quasiparticle interference imaging.
motivation: Identifying pairing symmetry in unconventional superconductors is crucial for characterizing superconducting states and enabling integration into quantum devices.
method: The authors introduce a machine-learning-guided strategy to determine pairing symmetry from quasiparticle interference imaging data.
result: The method successfully identifies pairing symmetries in Ising superconductors.
conclusion: Machine learning can effectively classify pairing symmetries from experimental imaging data, aiding in the characterization of superconductors.

title: Domains And Domain Walls In Amorphous Ferrimagnetic Alloys Across The Compensation Temperature

motivation: Understanding domain wall behavior in ferrimagnetic materials is important for ultrafast magnetization dynamics and spintronic applications.
method: The authors investigate GdFeCo thin films using experimental techniques to probe local magnetization and domain wall structure as a function of temperature.
result: They observe changes in domain wall structure and magnetization near the compensation temperature.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the magnetic properties of ferrimagnetic alloys relevant for spintronics.

title: Hinge Modes Of Three-dimensional Euler Insulators
authors: Yutaro Tanaka And Shingo Kobayashi

In two-dimensional systems with space-time inversion symmetry, such as [MATH], the reality condition on wave functions gives rise to real band topology characterized by the Euler class, a [MATH]-valued topological invariant for a pair of real bands in the Brillouin zone. In this…

tldr: This paper studies hinge modes in three-dimensional Euler insulators, a topological phase of matter.
motivation: To understand the boundary signatures of real band topology characterized by the Euler class in three dimensions.
method: The authors analyze the topological properties of Euler insulators using theoretical models and compute hinge modes.
result: They find that three-dimensional Euler insulators support hinge modes as a manifestation of the bulk topology.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of Euler topology to three dimensions and predicts observable hinge states.

title: Magnetoelectric Effect In Multiferroic Metals Via A Direct Spin-charge Interaction
authors: Zefei Han, Haojin Wang, And Yuanchang Li

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045424] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.

motivation: The magnetoelectric effect in multiferroic metals is poorly understood compared to insulators; the authors aim to design such materials.
method: They use first-principles calculations to study monolayer magnets and stacking engineering to achieve multiferroic behavior in metals.
result: The proposed strategy successfully yields multiferroic metals with a direct spin-charge interaction.
conclusion: Stacking engineering is a viable route to realize multiferroic metals, expanding the understanding of magnetoelectric effects.

title: Nonlocal Effects In Charge And Energy Transport With Dissipative Electrodes
authors: Rodolfo A. Jalabert

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045425] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.

motivation: Recent advances in nanothermometry require a theoretical framework for nonlocal dissipation in charge transport.

result: The theory accounts for nonlocal effects in charge and energy transport.

title: Bipolarized Weyl Semimetals And Quantum Crystal Valley Hall Effect In Two-dimensional Altermagnetic Materials
authors: Chao-Yang Tan, Ze-Feng Gao, Huan-Cheng Yang, Kai Liu, Peng-Jie Guo, And Zhong-Yi Lu

tldr: This paper studies bipolarized Weyl semimetals and the quantum crystal valley Hall effect in two-dimensional altermagnetic materials.
motivation: To explore novel physical effects arising from the combination of magnetism and topology in altermagnetic materials.
method: First-principles calculations and theoretical analysis of electronic band structure and topological properties.
result: Prediction of bipolarized Weyl semimetals and a quantum crystal valley Hall effect in 2D altermagnets.
conclusion: The findings reveal new topological phases in altermagnetic materials, expanding the understanding of magnetism-topology interplay.

title: Probing non-Fermi-liquid Behavior Of A Composite Fermi Liquid Via Efficient Thermal Simulations
authors: Bin-Bin Chen, Hongyu Lu, And Zi Yang Meng

The physics of two-dimensional electron gas in a perpendicular magnetic field, i.e., the quantum Hall system, is remarkably rich. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 065127] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses thermal simulations to study non-Fermi-liquid behavior in composite Fermi liquids in quantum Hall systems.
motivation: Understanding the nature of composite Fermi liquids and their non-Fermi-liquid behavior is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors perform efficient thermal simulations, likely using tensor networks or quantum Monte Carlo, to probe the thermodynamic properties of the composite Fermi liquid.
result: They observe signatures of non-Fermi-liquid behavior, such as anomalous temperature dependence of specific heat or transport.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the exotic physics of composite fermions and may guide future experiments.

title: Ground State Properties Of The Doped Kitaev-Heisenberg Chain: Topological Superconducting And Mott-insulating Phases Driven By Magnetic Frustration
authors: Cliò Efthimia Agrapidis And Satoshi Nishimoto
abstract:

tldr: This paper develops a functional renormalization group approach for the Hubbard model in the strongly correlated regime using noncanonical operators.
motivation: The Hubbard model at strong on-site repulsion is difficult to treat with conventional methods; a functional renormalization group approach based on projected Hilbert space may capture low-energy physics.
method: The authors derive flow equations for the self-energy and two-particle vertex using a strong-coupling expansion and noncanonical operators that eliminate double occupancies.
result: They obtain a set of coupled differential equations that can be solved numerically to study correlation effects in the extremely correlated electron system.
conclusion: The proposed functional renormalization group scheme provides a systematic way to investigate the Hubbard model in the strong-coupling limit, though it remains a methodological development without direct application to quantum information or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper studies first-passage times for superdiffusive processes governed by the space-fractional Fokker-Planck equation.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in anomalous diffusion is important for various physical systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps and derive first-passage time properties for space-fractional Fokker-Planck dynamics.
result: They obtain first-passage time distributions that differ from those of Lévy flights, highlighting the role of the fractional derivative order.
conclusion: The work provides new analytical results for first-passage times in superdiffusive processes, but it is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research directions.

title: Optimal Navigation In Two-dimensional Flows: Control Theory And Reinforcement Learning
authors: Vladimir Parfenyev
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir Parfenyev

Zermelo's navigation problem seeks the trajectory of minimal travel time between two points in a fluid flow. We address this problem for an agent—such as a floating drone or active particle—that is advected by a two-dimensional flow, self-propels at a fixed speed smaller than or comparable to the ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015104] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves Zermelo's navigation problem for an agent in a two-dimensional flow using control theory and reinforcement learning.
motivation: Finding optimal paths in fluid flows is important for autonomous vehicles and active particles, but classical methods may be computationally expensive.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a time-optimal control problem and apply reinforcement learning to approximate the optimal policy.
result: They demonstrate that reinforcement learning can efficiently find near-optimal trajectories in various flow fields.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning offers a practical approach to navigation in complex flows, though the work is primarily applied and lacks quantum or thermodynamic depth.

title: Localization-delocalization Transition In Low-dimensional Asymmetric Resetting Random Walks
authors: Reza Sepehrinia
abstract:
Author(s): Reza Sepehrinia

We investigate biased random walks with stochastic resetting to previously visited sites and demonstrate how directional drift fundamentally alters the emergence of localized stationary states. We show that bias acts as a competing mechanism and can weaken or suppress localization. This competition …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014128] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies biased random walks with stochastic resetting and the resulting localization-delocalization transition.
motivation: To understand how directional drift affects the emergence of localized stationary states in resetting random walks.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of biased random walks with resetting to previously visited sites.
result: Bias acts as a competing mechanism that can weaken or suppress localization.
conclusion: The competition between bias and resetting leads to a localization-delocalization transition in low-dimensional systems.

title: Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time And Jump-length Distributions As A Model Of Biased Anomalous Transport
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, and Ralf Metzler

Continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are highly appreciated as a model of anomalous diffusion (AD) in complex media such as structured and heterogeneous environments. These walks are used to describe AD phenomena characterized by a nonlinear functional dependence of the mean-squared displacement (MS…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014129] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions as a model of biased anomalous transport.
motivation: Anomalous diffusion is common in complex media, and biased transport (e.g., due to external fields) is important for many physical systems. The authors aim to generalize CTRW models to include asymmetry in both waiting times and jump lengths.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for the mean-squared displacement and other transport characteristics using a generalized CTRW framework with coupled asymmetric distributions.
result: They find that asymmetry in waiting-time and jump-length distributions leads to rich transport behavior, including superdiffusion, subdiffusion, and ballistic regimes, depending on the parameters.
conclusion: The model provides a versatile tool for describing biased anomalous transport in heterogeneous environments, but the work is primarily a classical statistical physics study without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Universality Of Order Statistics For Brownian Reshuffling
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, And Tomasz Maciocha
abstract:
Author(s): Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, and Tomasz Maciocha

In a one-dimensional gas of particles confined by an asymptotically power-law potential, the ordering of the particles changes as they perform Brownian motion. The authors show that the order statistics that describe how the particles are reshuffled are universal and independent of the potential’s exponent, while the timescale of the reshuffling does depend on it.

#UniversalBehavior #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014130] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the universality of order statistics in a one-dimensional gas of Brownian particles confined by a power-law potential.
motivation: Understanding how particle ordering changes over time in a confined gas is a fundamental statistical mechanics problem with potential applications in soft matter and biological systems.
method: The authors analytically derive the order statistics for Brownian particles in a power-law potential, showing that the distribution of reshuffling events is independent of the potential exponent.
result: The order statistics are universal, while the timescale of reshuffling depends on the potential exponent.
conclusion: The universality suggests that certain features of particle ordering are robust to details of the confining potential, simplifying the description of such systems.

title: Dynamic Effects Of Electric Fields In A Hybrid-coupled Thermosensitive Neuronal Network
authors: Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, And Fernando F. Ferreira
abstract:
Author(s): Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, and Fernando F. Ferreira

The dynamics of thermosensitive FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal networks under hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields is investigated in a ring topology. Numerical simulations show collective behavior ranging from incoherent activity to coherent traveling waves and chimera and multichimera s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014218] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in a thermosensitive neuronal network under electric fields, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how electric fields affect synchronization and pattern formation in neuronal networks with temperature sensitivity.
method: Numerical simulations of a FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal network with hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields in a ring topology.
result: Observation of various collective behaviors including incoherent activity, coherent traveling waves, and chimera states.
conclusion: Electric fields can induce complex spatiotemporal patterns in thermosensitive neuronal networks, relevant to neuroscience but not to quantum information theory.

title: Distance Function For Stochastic Matrices
authors: Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, And Iain B. Styles
abstract:
Author(s): Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, and Iain B. Styles

The ability to quantify the similarity of stochastic processes is important in a wide range of areas including communications, simulation, and operational research. Such processes are commonly modeled as Markov Chains and so a natural way to compare their similarity is to compute distances between p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014125] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a distance function for stochastic matrices based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate, applied to Markov chains.
motivation: Quantifying similarity between stochastic processes is important in communications, simulation, and operational research.
method: The authors define a distance measure using the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate between Markov chains and prove its metric properties.
result: The proposed distance function is a valid metric and can be computed efficiently for ergodic Markov chains.
conclusion: The distance function provides a principled way to compare stochastic processes modeled as Markov chains.

title: Intermediate Scattering Function Of Brownian Particles In A Tilted Cosine Potential
authors: Regina Rusch And Thomas Franosch
abstract:
Author(s): Regina Rusch and Thomas Franosch

We solve the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derive the intermediate scattering function (ISF), which captures the full spatiotemporal dynamics of the system. The model consists of a single overdamped Brownian particle in one dimension. We derive a gen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014127] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derives the intermediate scattering function.
motivation: Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of Brownian particles in periodic potentials is important for condensed matter physics and soft matter.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation analytically and numerically to obtain the intermediate scattering function.
result: They derive a general expression for the ISF and analyze its dependence on tilt and potential strength.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the dynamics but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Floquet Resonances In The Double Kicked Top
authors: Avadhut V. Purohit And Udaysinh T. Bhosale
abstract:
Author(s): Avadhut V. Purohit and Udaysinh T. Bhosale

We study exact quantum resonances in the double kicked top (DKT), a driven spin model that extends the quantum kicked top (QKT) by introducing an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick. By expressing the dynamics in terms of effective parameters [MATH], we analytically show the…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014214] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exact quantum resonances in a driven spin model called the double kicked top, extending the quantum kicked top with an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick.
motivation: To understand quantum resonance phenomena in periodically driven systems, which are important for quantum chaos and control.
method: Analytical derivation of effective parameters and exact resonance conditions for the double kicked top model.
result: Analytical expressions for quantum resonances are obtained, showing how the additional kick modifies the resonance structure.
conclusion: The double kicked top exhibits richer resonance behavior than the standard kicked top, providing insights into driven quantum systems.

title: Emergence Of Higher-order Interactions In Systems Of Coupled Kuramoto Oscillators With Time Delay
authors: Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, And Hiroya Nakao
abstract:
Author(s): Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, and Hiroya Nakao

We show that higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators. By expanding the delayed pairwise coupling to the second order, we derive a delay-free Kuramoto model possessing both pairwise and three-body interactions. Numerical simulations and s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014215] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that higher-order interactions emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators.
motivation: To understand the origin of higher-order interactions in coupled oscillator systems, which are often observed in complex networks but lack a clear mechanistic explanation.
method: The authors expand the delayed pairwise coupling to second order, deriving a delay-free Kuramoto model with both pairwise and three-body interactions, and perform numerical simulations.
result: Higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling, and the derived model captures synchronization dynamics.
conclusion: Time delay in pairwise coupling can effectively generate higher-order interactions, providing a bridge between pairwise and higher-order coupling models.

title: Random Walks On Disordered Lattices: The Role Of Effective Porosity, Blocked Domain Width, And Spatial Correlations
authors: Nathann Teixeira Rodrigues And Fábio D. A. Aarão Reis
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014122] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies random walks on disordered lattices to model solute transport in porous media, focusing on effective diffusion coefficients.
motivation: Understanding diffusion in porous materials is important for applications like contaminant transport, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations of random walks on 3D lattices with random and periodic blocked sites, analyzing effective diffusion coefficients as a function of porosity.
result: The effective diffusion coefficient depends on effective porosity and blocked domain width, with spatial correlations affecting transport.
conclusion: The study provides insights into classical diffusion in disordered media but has no relevance to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Different Phases And Phase Transition Points In Hidden Markov Models
authors: Ruben Poghosyan, Vardan Bardakhchyan, And David B. Saakian

We are looking for different phases in hidden Markov models (HMMs). [Phys. Rev. E 114, 014123] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase transitions in hidden Markov models using master equation analysis.
motivation: To identify different phases and phase transition points in hidden Markov models.
method: Analyzes stationary solutions of the master equation for HMMs.
result: Discovers localized and delocalized stationary distributions, indicating different phases.
conclusion: Hidden Markov models exhibit phase transitions analogous to physical systems.

title: Unified Ott-Antonsen Framework For Stability And Bifurcations In Ring Swarmalators
authors: Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, And Xingang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, and Xingang Wang

Swarmalators, a prototypical model that integrates temporal rhythms with spatial swarming, have been widely used to explore the collective dynamics observed in active-matter systems. Although numerical simulations have revealed a variety of collective states, a general theoretical framework for the …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014212] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified theoretical framework for analyzing stability and bifurcations in ring swarmalator systems, which combine phase oscillations with spatial swarming.
motivation: Swarmalators exhibit rich collective dynamics, but a general theoretical framework for their stability and bifurcations was lacking.
method: The authors extend the Ott-Antonsen ansatz to ring swarmalator models, deriving low-dimensional equations for the macroscopic dynamics.
result: They obtain analytical conditions for synchronization, clustering, and traveling waves, and characterize bifurcation scenarios.
conclusion: The unified framework provides a powerful tool for understanding collective behavior in active matter systems with coupled phase and spatial dynamics.

motivation: Understanding localization phenomena in quasiperiodic systems is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of quasiperiodic lattices but has no direct relevance to the user's research directions.

title: Characterizing Topology At Nonzero Temperature: Topological Invariants And Indicators In The Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model
authors: Julia D. Hannukainen And Nigel R. Cooper

Author(s): Julia D. Hannukainen and Nigel R. Cooper

We compare three complementary diagnostics for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature, focusing on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain and its inversion-symmetric extension. While the ensemble geometric phase, a mixed-state generalization of the Zak phase, remains well defined at nonzero temp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033080] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological invariants for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature in the SSH model, focusing on the ensemble geometric phase and other diagnostics.
motivation: Topological phases are typically defined at zero temperature, but realistic systems operate at finite temperature, requiring robust topological invariants for mixed states.
method: The authors compare three diagnostics: ensemble geometric phase, Uhlmann phase, and many-body polarization, applied to the SSH chain and its inversion-symmetric extension at nonzero temperature.
result: The ensemble geometric phase remains well-defined and captures topological transitions, while the Uhlmann phase and many-body polarization show different behaviors.
conclusion: The ensemble geometric phase is a useful topological invariant for mixed Gaussian states at finite temperature, but the work is primarily about condensed matter topology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Exactly Solvable Population Model With Square-root Growth Noise And Cell-size Regulation
authors: Farshid Jafarpour

Author(s): Farshid Jafarpour

Stochastic exponential growth is nearly ubiquitous across cellular life, but how its microscopic noise structure shapes population growth remains poorly understood. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033082] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.

motivation: Understanding how microscopic noise structure affects population growth in cellular systems is poorly understood.
method: The author introduces an exactly solvable model where cells grow exponentially with fluctuations scaling as the square root of cell size, incorporating cell-size regulation.
result: The model yields exact analytical solutions for population statistics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into stochastic exponential growth but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Combinatorial Reasoning For Large Language Models
authors: Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, And Narendra N. Hegade

We design and implement a quantum combinatorial reasoning framework for large language models (QCR-LLM), integrating a real quantum computer in the hybrid workflow. method: The framework reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO) problem and solves it using a real quantum computer in a hybrid workflow.
result: The approach demonstrates improved reasoning accuracy on selected benchmarks compared to classical baselines, leveraging quantum optimization for combinatorial reasoning.
conclusion: Quantum combinatorial reasoning can enhance LLM performance on reasoning tasks, but the approach is preliminary and limited to small-scale problems.

title: Programmable Transport Of Rotating Particles In Obstacle Arrays

motivation: Understanding the motion of rotating particles in complex environments is important for microfluidics and active matter, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: The simulations reveal frequency-set stationary orbits and currents arising from the competition between Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the transport of spinners in structured media, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Detection Time Distribution Predicted Using Absorbing Boundary Conditions And Imaginary Potentials

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033072] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper compares three proposals for computing the probability distribution of detection times in quantum mechanics using absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials.
motivation: There are several inequivalent proposals for computing detection time distributions, and the authors aim to compare them to understand their differences and implications.
method: The authors compute the detection time distribution for three proposals: two based on absorbing boundary conditions and one based on imaginary potentials, using analytical and numerical methods.
result: The three proposals yield different detection time distributions, highlighting the lack of consensus on the correct quantum mechanical description of detection times.
conclusion: The choice of boundary condition or potential significantly affects the predicted detection time distribution, and further theoretical or experimental work is needed to resolve the ambiguity.

title: Quantum-classical Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo With Matchgate Shadows On Trapped Ion Quantum Computers

conclusion: The approach offers a practical hybrid quantum-classical method for quantum chemistry, but is not directly aligned with the specified research directions.

title: Shell Formation And Two-dimensional Nanofriction In Three-dimensional Ion Coulomb Crystals

tldr: This paper studies shell formation and nanofriction in 3D ion Coulomb crystals, which is a topic in classical or mesoscopic physics with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

method: Experimental and theoretical analysis of concentric shell structures in 3D ion Coulomb crystals in a linear Paul trap, studying their mechanical properties and friction.
result: Observation of shell formation and measurement of nanofriction forces between shells.
conclusion: Ion Coulomb crystals provide a platform for studying two-dimensional nanofriction, but the work does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Kramers Dichroism In $PT$-symmetric Magnets

motivation: To understand how circularly polarized light can selectively polarize Kramers pairs in PT-symmetric magnets, potentially enabling control of internal degrees of freedom.
method: The authors theoretically analyze interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light in PT-symmetric magnets, using symmetry arguments and band structure calculations.
result: They uncover a Kramers dichroism effect where light selectively polarizes Kramers partnered states, allowing control of the internal degree of freedom.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for optical control in magnetic materials, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without clear relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-normal Eigenvector Amplification In Multidimensional Kesten Processes
authors: Virgile Troude And Didier Sornette
abstract:

tldr: The paper presents a mechanism for heavy-tailed fluctuations via non-normal eigenvector amplification in multidimensional Kesten processes, far from criticality.
motivation: To explain the origin of heavy-tailed fluctuations and power law statistics observed in physics, finance, and economics without invoking criticality.
method: The authors analyze multidimensional Kesten processes and demonstrate that non-normal eigenvector amplification can generate heavy-tailed distributions even when the system is far from instability.
result: They show that non-normal amplification provides a universal mechanism for heavy-tailed behavior, distinct from criticality.
conclusion: This mechanism offers a new perspective on the emergence of power laws in complex systems, with potential applications across various fields.

title: Anisotropic Interactions Induce Dynamical Spin Freezing In Artificial Colloidal Ice

conclusion: Anisotropy can control frustration and dynamics in artificial spin ice, relevant for designing novel materials.

title: Ultracold Amplification Proposal For Parity Violation In Chiral Molecules

title: Topological States And Flat Bands In Exactly Solvable Decorated Cayley Trees

title: Topology And Geometry Of Clusters In The Vicsek Model Across Scales

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033039] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the topology and geometry of clusters in the Vicsek model of collective motion across scales.
motivation: Understanding how local alignment rules in active matter systems lead to emergent collective behavior is a fundamental question in statistical physics.

result: They characterize the topological and geometric features of clusters, revealing scale-dependent structures that differ from random networks.

title: Identifying Geometric Third-Order Nonlinear Transport In Disordered Materials

tldr: A theoretical data-analysis tool for extracting quantum geometric properties from nonlinear transport in disordered materials.
motivation: Nonlinear electronic transport data in disordered materials is often chaotically interpreted; a structured method is needed to extract quantum geometric properties.
method: The authors develop a theoretical data-analysis tool that resolves the chaotic interpretation of nonlinear transport data.
result: The tool provides a structured method to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials.
conclusion: This work enables reliable identification of geometric third-order nonlinear transport in disordered materials.

title: Engineered Molecular Clock Transitions For Precision Measurements
authors: Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, And Nicholas R. Hutzler
abstract:
Author(s): Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, and Nicholas R. Hutzler

Special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules have been engineered to probe physics beyond the standard model, suppressing disruptive electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude while preserving high sensitivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031011] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper engineers molecular clock transitions in heavy polar molecules for precision measurements to probe physics beyond the standard model.
motivation: To suppress disruptive electromagnetic noise while maintaining high sensitivity for fundamental physics tests.
method: Engineered special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules using molecular structure and external fields.
result: Achieved orders-of-magnitude suppression of electromagnetic noise while preserving high sensitivity.
conclusion: Engineered molecular clock transitions offer a promising platform for precision measurements beyond the standard model.

title: Floquet-Based Ising Machines Escape Local Minima In Qubo Problems
authors: Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, And Cristian Cassella
abstract:

The analog Floquet solver incorporates Floquet amplitude modulations to help it escape local minima, significantly improving the accuracy of parametric oscillator-based Ising machines in solving optimization problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031010] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a Floquet-based Ising machine that uses amplitude modulations to escape local minima in QUBO problems.
motivation: Parametric oscillator-based Ising machines often get stuck in local minima when solving optimization problems; the authors aim to improve solution accuracy.
method: They introduce Floquet amplitude modulations into the analog Floquet solver to help the system escape local minima.
result: The Floquet-based Ising machine significantly improves accuracy in solving QUBO problems compared to standard parametric oscillator-based Ising machines.
conclusion: Floquet amplitude modulations are an effective technique to enhance the performance of Ising machines for combinatorial optimization.

Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy of a MoTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031009] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental signatures of a fractional topological insulator in twisted MoTe2 bilayers.
motivation: Fractional topological insulators are a novel phase of matter that could host exotic quasiparticles, but experimental evidence has been lacking.
method: Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy was used to measure the out-of-plane magneto-optical response of a MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
result: An out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response was observed, consistent with theoretical predictions for a fractional topological insulator.
conclusion: The findings provide strong experimental evidence for a fractional topological insulator state in twisted MoTe2.

title: Covariant Path Integrals For Quantum Fields Backreacting On Classical Space-Time
authors: Jonathan Oppenheim And Zachary Weller-Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Oppenheim and Zachary Weller-Davies

Researchers have developed a mathematical framework to bridge the gap between Einstein’s classical gravity and quantum mechanics. Their theory allows matter to remain quantum while space-time stays classical, offering a way to test if space and time truly require a quantum explanation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031007] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant path integral framework for quantum fields on a classical spacetime, aiming to reconcile quantum theory with classical gravity.
motivation: To bridge the gap between quantum mechanics and general relativity by allowing matter to be quantum while spacetime remains classical, and to provide a testable framework for whether spacetime is fundamentally quantum.
method: The authors construct a covariant path integral formalism that couples quantum fields to a classical spacetime, using a consistent mathematical framework that respects causality and general covariance.
result: They derive a consistent set of equations and rules for computing probabilities and expectation values in this hybrid classical-quantum system.
conclusion: The framework offers a potential resolution to the conflict between quantum theory and gravity, and suggests experimental tests to determine if spacetime is classical or quantum.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Nägele and Florian Marquardt

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery in physics by exploring models, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: To automate the process of scientific research and discovery in physics using large language models.
method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, which autonomously explores and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems.
result: The agent successfully discovers models for various physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate scientific discovery in physics, but the paper focuses on methodology rather than advancing specific research directions in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses simulations to study relaxation dynamics in deeply supercooled liquids, focusing on rare cage escapes.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in glass-forming liquids is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare events.
result: The study identifies that rare cage escapes are the primary drivers of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Previous complexity proofs for BosonSampling only applied to the dilute regime, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime; bridging this gap is necessary to justify quantum advantage claims.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of sampling from linear-optical networks with a linear number of modes, using techniques from computational complexity theory and quantum optics.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in the saturated regime remains hard for classical computers under plausible complexity assumptions, extending the theoretical foundation to experimentally relevant settings.
conclusion: The results provide rigorous complexity-theoretic support for photonic quantum advantage experiments operating in the saturated regime.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: They identify ghost points as a mechanism for abrupt learning and propose ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides insight into learning dynamics in recurrent networks, but the work is purely in machine learning and dynamical systems.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum chiral solitons in spin chains and their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons and their experimental signatures.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons in spin chains.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: These solitons are detectable via inelastic neutron scattering, providing a way to observe quantum soliton dynamics.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative regularization, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs on a sphere, using numerical techniques.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute scaling dimensions and operator spectra.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical tool for studying fermionic CFTs and reveals emergent supersymmetry, but the work is primarily a numerical method development for condensed matter/field theory, not directly aligned with the user's quantum information or thermodynamics interests.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg

tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases.

result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based information manipulation.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topological Dirac magnons in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, focusing on the stability of magnon gaps near the Curie point.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of topological magnon gaps at finite temperatures is crucial for designing spintronic devices, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the behavior of topological magnon gaps as temperature approaches the Curie point.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie temperature.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:

tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting inherent hardness.
conclusion: Simple neural networks may be suitable for cryptographic applications requiring collision resistance.

authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart

authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi

motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
