conclusion: The framework provides a high-level vision for the field but does not present new technical results or deep analysis.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical studies on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are an actively evolving field with expanding theoretical and experimental understanding.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: Understanding how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic manipulation.
method: The authors present a unified theoretical framework based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities in both optical and acoustic waves.
result: They show that the same physical principles govern forces and torques in optics and acoustics, enabling cross-disciplinary insights.
conclusion: The unified perspective can guide the design of advanced particle manipulation techniques using light and sound.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring strongly correlated and topological electronic states.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in complex systems like ecology and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across different fields.
method: Uses field-theoretic methods (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism) to derive and analyze stochastic reaction-diffusion equations.
result: Provides a unified framework for handling chemical systems and applications in ecology and epidemiology.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for studying stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond physics.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of experimental techniques, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their topological properties, but does not present new results.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising materials, but practical applications are still distant.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, including nonradiative decay mechanisms and their incorporation into studies of quantum systems.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical approaches and an outlook on future applications.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are well-developed and can be applied to photonics and energy harvesting, but the paper does not present new results or directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their formation and quantum features.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic applications, but their quantum aspects are less explored; this review aims to bridge that gap.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including interactions and quantum features.
result: It highlights quantum effects in skyrmion dynamics and potential for quantum information applications.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions may enable new functionalities, but the field is still nascent with many open questions.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand possible new physics beyond the standard model, particularly spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons that could explain dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper surveys theoretical models of spin-dependent exotic interactions and reviews experimental techniques used to search for them, including precision measurements and astrophysical observations.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic spin-dependent interactions and highlights the most promising experimental approaches.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for fundamental physics, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: To clarify why certain measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of circumstances where bounds are exceeded and identifies which assumptions are violated in each case.
result: It demonstrates that apparent violations arise from assumptions not being met, and that interesting material properties can be developed by violating these assumptions.
conclusion: Understanding the assumptions behind thermodynamic bounds enables the design of materials with properties that surpass conventional limits.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical implementations of quantum many-body systems in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Survey of atomic, photonic, and electronic platforms for realizing nonstandard geometries, including synthetic dimensions and curved spaces.
result: Summarizes recent progress in engineering fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional systems, highlighting key experimental demonstrations.
conclusion: These synthetic quantum matter platforms open new avenues for studying topological phases and quantum gravity analogs, but the paper is a review without novel technical contributions.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, including tests of quantum gravity and gravity-induced entanglement.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to study gravity at the quantum level.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks (e.g., decoherence models, entanglement mediation) and experimental approaches (matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics) for testing gravity with quantum systems.
result: The review summarizes current experimental progress and theoretical predictions regarding gravity-induced decoherence and entanglement between massive particles.
conclusion: Experiments are underway that will guide the theoretical description of gravity on laboratory scales, but the topic remains speculative and not directly aligned with the user's research directions.

title: Integrated Soliton Microcombs Beyond The Turnkey Limit
authors: Ze Wang, Tianyu Xu, Yuanlei Wang, Kaixuan Zhu, Xinrui Luo, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bo Ni, Yiwen Yang, Qihuang Gong, Yun-Feng Xiao, Bei-Bei Li, And Qi-Fan Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Ze Wang, Tianyu Xu, Yuanlei Wang, Kaixuan Zhu, Xinrui Luo, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bo Ni, Yiwen Yang, Qihuang Gong, Yun-Feng Xiao, Bei-Bei Li, and Qi-Fan Yang

Self-injection locking enables integrated soliton microcombs with turnkey initiation and improved coherence, but it also pins the pump close to resonance, limiting the access to large detuning for broader combs. Here, we use an auxiliary resonator to dynamically hybridize the pump mode, enabling adi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043802] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an integrated soliton microcomb platform that uses an auxiliary resonator to achieve broader frequency combs beyond the turnkey limit.
motivation: Integrated soliton microcombs are important for applications like optical communications and metrology, but conventional self-injection locking limits the achievable comb bandwidth. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors introduce an auxiliary resonator to dynamically hybridize the pump mode, enabling adiabatic pumping across a larger detuning range and thus generating broader soliton microcombs.
result: They experimentally demonstrate soliton microcombs with significantly broader bandwidth than achievable with standard turnkey self-injection locking.
conclusion: The auxiliary resonator technique provides a practical route to enhance the performance of integrated soliton microcombs, potentially benefiting various photonic applications.

title: Deep-Learning Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian In Real Space
authors: Zilong Yuan, Zechen Tang, Honggeng Tao, Xiaoxun Gong, Zezhou Chen, Yuxiang Wang, He Li, Yang Li, Zhiming Xu, Minghui Sun, Boheng Zhao, Chen Si, Chong Wang, Wenhui Duan, And Yong Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Zilong Yuan, Zechen Tang, Honggeng Tao, Xiaoxun Gong, Zezhou Chen, Yuxiang Wang, He Li, Yang Li, Zhiming Xu, Minghui Sun, Boheng Zhao, Chen Si, Chong Wang, Wenhui Duan, and Yong Xu

Integrating essential physical priors into deep-learning first-principles methods is a critical fundamental problem. Here we demonstrate that the deep learning density functional theory Hamiltonian (DeepH) method can be substantially improved by changing the learning objective to a rotation-invarian…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046401] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep learning to predict density functional theory Hamiltonians in real space, improving accuracy with rotation-invariant features.
motivation: Integrating essential physical priors into deep-learning first-principles methods is a critical fundamental problem.
method: The authors modify the learning objective to a rotation-invariant representation and apply it to real-space DFT Hamiltonians.
result: The improved DeepH method achieves higher accuracy in predicting Hamiltonians for various materials.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates that incorporating physical priors significantly enhances deep-learning-based first-principles calculations.

title: Nmr Evidence For Spontaneous Electronic Chiral Order In URhSn
authors: Y. Tokunaga, T. Ishitobi, H. Sakai, S. Kambe, H. Harima, A. Nakamura, A. Maurya, D. Li, Y. Homma, F. Honda, D. Aoki, And Y. Shimizu
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Tokunaga, T. Ishitobi, H. Sakai, S. Kambe, H. Harima, A. Nakamura, A. Maurya, D. Li, Y. Homma, F. Honda, D. Aoki, and Y. Shimizu

The first direct evidence of spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, a strongly correlated material without an inherently chiral lattice structure, fundamentally challenges the prevailing notion that electronic chirality requires a chiral crystal framework.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046501] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports NMR evidence for spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, a strongly correlated material without a chiral lattice.
motivation: To challenge the prevailing notion that electronic chirality requires a chiral crystal framework by finding direct evidence in a non-chiral lattice.
method: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements on URhSn single crystals.
result: Observation of spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, providing the first direct evidence of such order in a material without an inherently chiral lattice.
conclusion: Electronic chirality can emerge in non-chiral crystal structures, fundamentally altering the understanding of chiral order in strongly correlated materials.

title: Probing Dielectric Screening In Van Der Waals Heterostructures Via Pressure-Tuned Exciton Rydberg Series
authors: Shalini Badola, Adlen Smiri, Thomas Pelini, Aditi Moghe, Tristan Riccardi, Amit Pawbake, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Iann C. Gerber, And Clément Faugeras
abstract:
Author(s): Shalini Badola, Adlen Smiri, Thomas Pelini, Aditi Moghe, Tristan Riccardi, Amit Pawbake, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Iann C. Gerber, and Clément Faugeras

Excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors are directly exposed to the environment and are sensitive to the dielectric properties of their surrounding. Here, we show that the Rydberg series of excited states of excitons in a monolayer [MATH] encapsulated in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036903] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dielectric screening in van der Waals heterostructures by measuring pressure-tuned exciton Rydberg series in monolayer MoSe2 encapsulated in hBN.
motivation: Excitons in 2D semiconductors are sensitive to their dielectric environment, and understanding screening is crucial for optoelectronic applications.
method: The authors apply hydrostatic pressure to tune the dielectric environment and measure the exciton Rydberg series using optical spectroscopy.
result: They observe a pressure-dependent shift of exciton resonances and extract the dielectric screening effect.
conclusion: The work provides insights into dielectric screening in van der Waals heterostructures but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Isotope Shifts In Heliumlike Carbon: Probes Of Nuclear Structure And New Bosons
authors: Xiao-Qiu Qi, Fang-Fei Wu, Zong-Chao Yan, Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Li-Yan Tang, Ai-Xi Chen, And Ting-Yun Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao-Qiu Qi, Fang-Fei Wu, Zong-Chao Yan, Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Li-Yan Tang, Ai-Xi Chen, and Ting-Yun Shi

We present high-precision calculations of isotope shifts for the [MATH] and [MATH] transitions in heliumlike [MATH], with mass-shift u…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012817] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: High-precision calculations of isotope shifts in heliumlike carbon to probe nuclear structure and search for new bosons.
motivation: Isotope shifts provide a sensitive probe of nuclear properties and can constrain new physics beyond the Standard Model.
method: Variational calculations using explicitly correlated basis functions with relativistic and QED corrections.
result: Accurate isotope shift predictions for the 1s2p 1P1 and 1s2s 3S1 transitions in C4+.
conclusion: The results enable experimental tests of nuclear structure models and searches for new bosons via isotope shift measurements.

title: Wetting Of Quantum Fluids: A Route To Free-standing Shell-shaped Quantum Droplets
authors: Francesco Ancilotto
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Ancilotto

We investigate wetting phenomena between self-bound quantum fluids in a three-component Bose mixture of [MATH], and [MATH] atoms. Within a density-functional approach including mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum-fluctuation corrections, we cons…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013317] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wetting phenomena in quantum fluid droplets using density functional theory, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand wetting and self-bound droplet formation in three-component Bose mixtures, which is a topic in quantum fluids and ultracold atomic physics.
method: A density-functional approach including mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum-fluctuation corrections is used to model the system.
result: The study predicts conditions for wetting and the formation of free-standing shell-shaped quantum droplets.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum fluid wetting but does not address information-theoretic or thermodynamic aspects relevant to the user's interests.

title: Interelectronic Correlation: Neutral And Ionized Atoms In Conjugate Spaces
authors: M. M. Gutiérrez-Vílchez, I. López-García, And J. C. Angulo
abstract:
Author(s): M. M. Gutiérrez-Vílchez, I. López-García, and J. C. Angulo

The intercorrelation level among constituent electrons of a multielectronic system is quantified by comparing the electron-pair density and the product of its marginal one-particle densities. The resulting comparison is interpreted as a measure of the interelectronic correlation and/or mutual inform…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012812] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantifies interelectronic correlation in multielectronic systems using electron-pair densities and mutual information.
motivation: To develop a measure of interelectronic correlation based on comparing the electron-pair density with the product of one-particle densities.
method: The authors compare the electron-pair density and the product of marginal one-particle densities, interpreting the comparison as a measure of correlation and mutual information.
result: The approach provides a quantification of interelectronic correlation in neutral and ionized atoms.
conclusion: The method offers a new way to measure electron correlation in atomic systems.

title: Spin-angle-controlled Nonreciprocal Nonlinear Optical Response In Janus ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}{\mathrm{I}}_{3}{\mathrm{Br}}_{3}$
authors: Y. Q. Liu, Yong Peng, Junwei Zhang, M. S. Si, G. P. Zhang, And Z. M. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Q. Liu, Yong Peng, Junwei Zhang, M. S. Si, G. P. Zhang, and Z. M. Zhang

Noncollinear spin configurations can induce nonreciprocal nonlinear optical responses, but their microscopic mechanism remains unclear. Here, we start with an effective tight-binding model to investigate how the spin configuration affects the geometric Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) tensor which is at the …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034312] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-angle-controlled nonreciprocal nonlinear optical response in Janus Cr2I3Br3 using an effective tight-binding model.
motivation: The microscopic mechanism of noncollinear spin configurations inducing nonreciprocal nonlinear optical responses is unclear.
method: An effective tight-binding model is used to investigate how spin configuration affects the geometric Pancharatnam-Berry tensor.
result: The spin-angle-controlled nonreciprocal nonlinear optical response is demonstrated and analyzed.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the microscopic mechanism of nonreciprocal nonlinear optical responses in magnetic materials.

title: $H$-linear Magnetoresistance In The ${t}^{2}$ Resistivity Regime Of Overdoped Infinite-layer Nickelate ${\mathrm{La}}_{1x}{\mathrm{Sr}}_{x}{\mathrm{NiO}}_{2}$
authors: Yong-Cheng Pan, Tommy Kotte, Toni Helm, Motoki Osada, Atsushi Tsukazaki, And Yu-Te Hsu
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Cheng Pan, Tommy Kotte, Toni Helm, Motoki Osada, Atsushi Tsukazaki, and Yu-Te Hsu

We report a systematic magnetotransport study on high-crystallinity [MATH] (LSNO) thin films with [MATH]. By conducting pulsed-field transport experiment up to 62 T, we reveal two salient features of the normal-state transport in overdoped LSN…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020508] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magnetotransport measurements on overdoped infinite-layer nickelate thin films, revealing H-linear magnetoresistance in the T^2 resistivity regime.
motivation: To understand the normal-state transport properties of overdoped infinite-layer nickelates, which are relevant to high-temperature superconductivity.
method: Pulsed-field magnetotransport experiments up to 62 T on high-crystallinity La1-xSrxNiO2 thin films.
result: Observation of H-linear magnetoresistance in the T^2 resistivity regime, indicating a non-Fermi liquid behavior.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the electronic properties of overdoped nickelates, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Including Nanoparticle Shape Into Macrospin Models
authors: Iago López-Vázquez, Òscar Iglesias, And David Serantes
abstract:
Author(s): Iago López-Vázquez, Òscar Iglesias, and David Serantes

We investigate the feasibility of the macrospin approximation to account for the actual shape of soft magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) with realistic geometries. Specifically focusing on magnetite, we use the superellipsoidal parametrization to account for a variety of shapes, with a continuous interpo…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014421] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the macrospin approximation for soft magnetic nanoparticles with realistic shapes using superellipsoidal parametrization.
motivation: To account for the actual shape of magnetic nanoparticles in macrospin models, which is important for understanding their magnetic behavior.
method: The authors use superellipsoidal parametrization to model various nanoparticle shapes and compare macrospin predictions with micromagnetic simulations.
result: The macrospin approximation can capture shape effects for certain geometries but fails for others, indicating limitations.
conclusion: Shape must be carefully considered when using macrospin models for magnetic nanoparticles.

title: Muonium Reaction In ${\mathrm{La}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$: Investigation Of The Last Steps In Muon Implantation
authors: C. M. S. Santos, A. G. Marinopoulos, J. M. Gil, R. C. Vilão, A. Weidinger, And T. Prokscha
abstract:
Author(s): C. M. S. Santos, A. G. Marinopoulos, J. M. Gil, R. C. Vilão, A. Weidinger, and T. Prokscha

We report on a muon spin rotation study of the wide band-gap material [MATH]. The focus is on the implantation process and the configurations formed at the end of the implantation trajectory. The data are analyzed in the recently developed “doorway model.” First-principl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045205] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies muonium reactions in La2O3 using muon spin rotation, focusing on the implantation process and final configurations.
motivation: Understanding the last steps of muon implantation in wide band-gap materials is important for interpreting muon spin rotation experiments.
method: The authors analyze muon spin rotation data using the 'doorway model' and first-principles calculations.
result: They identify the configurations formed at the end of the implantation trajectory and characterize the reaction dynamics.
conclusion: The study provides insights into muonium behavior in La2O3, relevant for material science but not for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Twistoptics In Planar Heterostructures With An Arbitrary Number Of Rotated Three-dimensional Thin Layers And Two-dimensional Conductive Sheets
authors: Christian Lanza, José Álvarez-Cuervo, Kirill V. Voronin, Gonzalo Álvarez-Pérez, Aitana Tarazaga Martín-Luengo, Javier Martín-Sánchez, Alexey Y. Nikitin, And Pablo Alonso-González
abstract:
Author(s): Christian Lanza, José Álvarez-Cuervo, Kirill V. Voronin, Gonzalo Álvarez-Pérez, Aitana Tarazaga Martín-Luengo, Javier Martín-Sánchez, Alexey Y. Nikitin, and Pablo Alonso-González

Twistoptics has recently emerged as a branch of nano-optics that explores light propagation in stacks of thin anisotropic layers rotated relative to one another. The concept is particularly relevant for polaritons—hybrid light-matter quasiparticles—in van der Waals (vdW) materials, where strong in-p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045423] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies twistoptics in planar heterostructures with rotated layers and conductive sheets, focusing on polariton propagation.
motivation: To understand and control light-matter interactions in twisted van der Waals heterostructures for nano-optics applications.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using transfer matrix methods to model electromagnetic modes in stacks of anisotropic layers and 2D conductive sheets.
result: They derive general expressions for the dispersion and propagation of polaritons in such heterostructures, showing how twist angles and layer number affect the optical response.
conclusion: Twistoptics provides a versatile platform for engineering polariton propagation, with potential applications in nanophotonic devices.

title: Large Earthquakes Follow Highly Unequal Ones
authors: Sudip Sarkar And Soumyajyoti Biswas
abstract:
Author(s): Sudip Sarkar and Soumyajyoti Biswas

It was conjectured for a long time that the tectonic plates are in a self-organized state of criticality and that the Gutenberg-Richter law is a manifestation of that. It was recently shown that for a system near criticality, the inequality of their responses due to external driving would sharply ri…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014143] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies inequality of earthquake magnitudes as a signature of self-organized criticality, using a fiber bundle model.
motivation: To test the conjecture that tectonic plates are in a self-organized critical state and that the Gutenberg-Richter law is a manifestation of it.
method: Analyzes earthquake catalog data and uses a fiber bundle model to show that large earthquakes follow periods of high inequality in magnitude distribution.
result: Finds that large earthquakes are preceded by highly unequal magnitude distributions, supporting the self-organized criticality hypothesis.
conclusion: Inequality measures can serve as precursors to large earthquakes, providing insight into critical dynamics of tectonic systems.

title: Dynamical Origin Of Extreme Events In Mutually Coupled And Networked Brusselator
authors: S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, And I. Manimehan
abstract:
Author(s): S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, and I. Manimehan

This study investigates the dynamical origins and statistical properties of extreme events (EEs) in a diffusively coupled theoretical Brusselator system, extending from pairwise interactions to globally coupled networks. Statistically, the emergence of EEs is characterized by heavy-tailed probabilit…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014217] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies extreme events in coupled Brusselator systems, a topic in nonlinear dynamics and complex systems.
motivation: To understand the dynamical origins and statistical properties of extreme events in chemical oscillator networks.
method: Numerical simulations of diffusively coupled Brusselator models, from pairwise to globally coupled networks, analyzing heavy-tailed probability distributions.
result: Extreme events emerge with heavy-tailed statistics, and their occurrence is linked to specific dynamical regimes.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into extreme event generation in coupled nonlinear systems, with potential relevance to other fields.

title: Alternating Pattern Formation In Oscillatory Media With Spatially Uniform And Nonuniform Global Feedback
authors: Zhilin Qu, Chunli Huang, And Fengze Sui
abstract:
Author(s): Zhilin Qu, Chunli Huang, and Fengze Sui

Alternating (temporally period-2) stripes, clusters, and labyrinths have been observed in chemical and biochemical reactions, in Min-protein dynamics in E. coli and in vitro systems, and in calcium alternans in cardiac myocytes. However, the mechanisms underlying the formation of these spatiotempora…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014211] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies alternating pattern formation in oscillatory media with global feedback, applied to chemical and biological systems.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms behind alternating stripes, clusters, and labyrinths observed in chemical reactions and biological systems like Min-protein dynamics and cardiac alternans.
method: The authors analyze a generic model of oscillatory media with spatially uniform and nonuniform global feedback, using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.
result: They identify conditions and mechanisms leading to alternating patterns, showing how global feedback can induce period-2 spatiotemporal structures.
conclusion: The work provides insight into pattern formation in oscillatory media, relevant to biological and chemical systems, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Mie-tronics Supermodes And Symmetry Breaking In Nonlocal Metasurfaces
authors: Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Jie Ji, Daniel Leykam, Jaime Gómez Rivas, And Yuri Kivshar
abstract:
Author(s): Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Jie Ji, Daniel Leykam, Jaime Gómez Rivas, and Yuri Kivshar

It is usually believed that symmetry breaking in photonic systems leads to weaker confinement, such as in the case of metasurfaces when bound states in the continuum are replaced by quasibound states with lower quality [MATH] factors. Here, in contrast, we reveal that symmetry breaking can instead en…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033076] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies symmetry breaking in nonlocal metasurfaces, revealing that it can enhance confinement and Q-factors, contrary to conventional belief.
motivation: To understand the role of symmetry breaking in photonic systems, specifically in nonlocal metasurfaces, and to challenge the common assumption that symmetry breaking always reduces confinement.
method: The authors analyze Mie-tronics supermodes in nonlocal metasurfaces, using theoretical modeling and numerical simulations to study the effects of symmetry breaking on mode confinement and quality factors.
result: They find that symmetry breaking can lead to stronger confinement and higher Q-factors, enabled by the interplay of Mie resonances and nonlocal effects.
conclusion: Symmetry breaking in nonlocal metasurfaces can be exploited to achieve high-Q resonances, offering new design principles for photonic devices.

title: Inhibition Of Explosive Transitions In Spreading Dynamics By Nonlinear Higher-order Adaptation
authors: Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, And Shaoting Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, and Shaoting Tang

The coevolution of structure and dynamics, known as adaptation, is a fundamental property in various systems and drives diverse emergent behaviors. However, the adaptation in most works primarily stems from pairwise situations, which is insufficient to capture ubiquitous higher-order characteristics…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033068] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies explosive transitions in spreading dynamics on higher-order networks with nonlinear adaptation, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how higher-order interactions and nonlinear adaptation affect explosive transitions in spreading processes.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for spreading dynamics on simplicial complexes with nonlinear adaptation rules and analyze the conditions for explosive transitions.
result: Nonlinear higher-order adaptation can inhibit explosive transitions, leading to continuous phase transitions instead.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions and nonlinear adaptation play a crucial role in shaping spreading dynamics, with implications for controlling epidemic outbreaks or information cascades.

title: Moiré-resonant Surface State In Ultrathin ${\mathrm{RuO}}_{2}(110)$
authors: Philipp Keßler, Andreas Feuerpfeil, Armando Consiglio, Hendrik Hohmann, Ronny Thomale, Jonas Erhardt, Bing Liu, Vedran Jovic, Ralph Claessen, Patrick Härtl, Matteo Dürrnagel, And Simon Moser
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Keßler, Andreas Feuerpfeil, Armando Consiglio, Hendrik Hohmann, Ronny Thomale, Jonas Erhardt, Bing Liu, Vedran Jovic, Ralph Claessen, Patrick Härtl, Matteo Dürrnagel, and Simon Moser

[MATH] has emerged as a prototypical candidate for altermagnetism. In the face of daunting evidence for magnetic order in the bulk, the focus naturally shifted to surfaces and ultrathin films, where Coulomb interactions are dimensionally quenched and electron correlations strongly enha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033058] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of ultrathin RuO2(110) films, focusing on moiré-resonant surface states and altermagnetism.
motivation: To understand how dimensional confinement and Coulomb interactions affect magnetic order and surface states in RuO2, a candidate altermagnet.
method: Combines angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) with density functional theory (DFT) calculations to probe the electronic structure.
result: Identifies moiré-resonant surface states and provides evidence for altermagnetic ordering in ultrathin films.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of altermagnetism in reduced dimensions but have no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; this review surveys three complementary real-space techniques.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete picture of defects.
result: The paper summarizes capabilities and limitations of each technique and highlights cases where combining them yields more comprehensive disorder characterization.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy methods, especially when combined, provide valuable atomic-scale insight into disorder in semiconductors.

title: Emergent Trion Resonance Driven By Lattice Reconstruction In A Moiré Superlattice
authors: Zhida Liu, Haonan Wang, Xiaohui Liu, Yue Ni, Hongtao Yan, Frank Y. Gao, Saba Arash, Hyunsue Kim, Dong Seob Kim, Xiangcheng Liu, Xiaoxiao Yu, Yongxin Zeng, Jiamin Quan, Di Huang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Edoardo Baldini, Keji Lai, Allan H. Macdonald, Chih-Kang Shih, Jamie Warner, Li Yang, And Xiaoqin Li
abstract:
Author(s): Zhida Liu, Haonan Wang, Xiaohui Liu, Yue Ni, Hongtao Yan, Frank Y. Gao, Saba Arash, Hyunsue Kim, Dong Seob Kim, Xiangcheng Liu, Xiaoxiao Yu, Yongxin Zeng, Jiamin Quan, Di Huang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Edoardo Baldini, Keji Lai, Allan H. MacDonald, Chih-Kang Shih, Jamie Warner, Li Yang, and Xiaoqin Li

We investigate how many-electron excited states emerge in twisted [MATH] homobilayers when the lattice reconstructions evolve. Notably, we identify a new trion resonance that arises in the transition regime of lattice reconstruction, where gradual changes in atomic alignment between t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036902] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies emergent trion resonances in twisted MoSe2 homobilayers driven by lattice reconstruction, focusing on many-body excited states in moiré superlattices.
motivation: Understanding how lattice reconstruction affects many-electron excited states in moiré materials is crucial for tailoring their optical and electronic properties.
method: The authors combine optical spectroscopy with structural characterization to probe trion resonances as a function of twist angle, correlating atomic alignment changes with spectral features.
result: They identify a new trion resonance that appears in the transition regime of lattice reconstruction, indicating a strong coupling between lattice relaxation and many-body excitations.
conclusion: Lattice reconstruction in moiré superlattices can qualitatively alter many-body excited states, offering a new knob to control optical properties in these materials.

title: Crust Glass Formation Reveals The Neutron Star Birth Properties In Igr J17480-2446
authors: D. A. Baiko And A. I. Chugunov
abstract:
Author(s): D. A. Baiko and A. I. Chugunov

IGR J17480-2446 is a low-mass x-ray binary, harboring an exceptional accreting pulsar (a neutron star) with an unusual spin frequency of 11 Hz and a very slow postoutburst crust cooling. The former may imply that it is observed at an early stage of recycling, while the latter was shown to indicate t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 031402] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies crust glass formation in neutron star IGR J17480-2446 to infer its birth properties.
motivation: Understanding the early evolution and recycling of neutron stars is important for astrophysics, but the paper focuses on neutron star crust physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze the cooling curve of the neutron star crust and model glass formation to constrain the star's age and initial temperature.
result: They find that the crust glass formation time is consistent with a young neutron star that has undergone slow recycling.
conclusion: The study provides insights into neutron star birth properties but does not connect to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Atomic Parity Violation In Highly Charged $^{40,48}\mathrm{Ca}$ And $^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$ Ions
authors: A. V. Viatkina, Ch. G. Mertens, B. Ohayon, V. A. Yerokhin, And A. Surzhykov
abstract:
Author(s): A. V. Viatkina, Ch. G. Mertens, B. Ohayon, V. A. Yerokhin, and A. Surzhykov

We calculate parity-violation-induced [MATH] amplitudes for the [MATH] and [MATH] transitions in H- and Li-like ions of [MATH], and [MATH]. In our analysis, we account for neutron skin effects and nuclear uncertainties for each nucleus. We c…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012814] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates parity-violating transition amplitudes in highly charged calcium and lead ions, focusing on nuclear structure effects.
motivation: To study atomic parity violation as a probe of nuclear properties, such as neutron skin, in highly charged ions.
method: Relativistic many-body calculations of parity-violating E1 amplitudes for specific transitions in H- and Li-like ions, including nuclear uncertainties.
result: Provides theoretical predictions for parity-violation amplitudes in 40,48Ca and 208Pb ions, accounting for neutron skin effects.
conclusion: The results can be used to extract nuclear structure information from future experiments on atomic parity violation.

title: Parametric Mössbauer Radiation In The Grazing-diffraction Geometry: Specular Diffraction And Superradiant Amplification
authors: Ze-An Peng, Christoph H. Keitel, And Jörg Evers
abstract:
Author(s): Ze-an Peng, Christoph H. Keitel, and Jörg Evers

Parametric x-ray radiation (PXR) is a tunable and versatile x-ray production mechanism that relies on relativistic electrons traversing through a crystal. When the crystal contains Mössbauer nuclei, they may also contribute to the x-ray generation, giving rise to spectrally narrow parametric Mössbau…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013115] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies parametric Mössbauer radiation in grazing-diffraction geometry, focusing on specular diffraction and superradiant amplification.
motivation: To explore a new x-ray production mechanism that combines parametric x-ray radiation with Mössbauer nuclei for spectrally narrow emission.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the grazing-diffraction geometry and derive expressions for specular diffraction and superradiant amplification.
result: They find that superradiant amplification can enhance the radiation intensity and narrow the spectral linewidth.
conclusion: The proposed mechanism offers a tunable x-ray source with potential applications in nuclear resonance and quantum optics, but is not directly relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Raman Spectroscopy Of The Van Der Waals Topological Magnet GdGaI
authors: Nan Jiang, Yijin Zhang, Yujie Xia, Tomo Higashihara, Ryutaro Okuma, Jun-Ichi Yamaura, Yoshinori Okada, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Tiantian Zhang, Tomoki Machida, And Yasuhiro Niimi
abstract:
Author(s): Nan Jiang, Yijin Zhang, Yujie Xia, Tomo Higashihara, Ryutaro Okuma, Jun-ichi Yamaura, Yoshinori Okada, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Tiantian Zhang, Tomoki Machida, and Yasuhiro Niimi

We report polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy of a van der Waals compound [MATH] that is a candidate for excitonic insulators. By combining the symmetry analysis with density functional theory calculations, we identify six Raman-active phonons. The spectra exhibit only the expected an…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065128] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy of a van der Waals topological magnet GdGaI, identifying six Raman-active phonons via symmetry analysis and DFT calculations.
motivation: To characterize the phonon modes of GdGaI, a candidate excitonic insulator, using Raman spectroscopy.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy combined with symmetry analysis and density functional theory calculations.
result: Six Raman-active phonons were identified, and the spectra matched expectations from symmetry analysis.
conclusion: The study provides a detailed phonon characterization of GdGaI, relevant for understanding its excitonic insulator properties.

title: Mie Voids As Broadband Directional Light Sources
authors: Benjamin Reichel, Adrià Canós Valero, Mario Hentschel, Harald Giessen, And Thomas Weiss
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Reichel, Adrià Canós Valero, Mario Hentschel, Harald Giessen, and Thomas Weiss

The Kerker effect arises from the interference between electric and magnetic multipoles, enabling directional light scattering in nanophotonics. However, conventional dielectric and plasmonic nanoparticles can only act as Kerker sources in narrow spectral regions, limiting their applicability. Here,…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065421] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a nanophotonic design for broadband directional light sources using Mie voids, based on the Kerker effect.
motivation: Conventional Kerker sources are limited to narrow spectral regions; the authors aim to achieve broadband directional scattering.
method: They propose Mie voids (air holes in a dielectric) as a platform to engineer electric and magnetic dipole resonances over a wide wavelength range.
result: The Mie void design enables broadband directional light emission by balancing electric and magnetic multipole contributions.
conclusion: Mie voids offer a practical route to broadband directional light sources for nanophotonics applications.

title: Tunable Electron-plasmon Coupling In The Layered Transition Metal Dichalcogenide ${\mathrm{ZrSe}}_{2−x}{\mathrm{Te}}_{x}$
authors: Tongrui Li, Yuzhe Wang, Haoyuan Yan, Jiexiong Sun, Rui Xu, Jianghao Yao, Sen Liao, Shiwu Su, Yunbo Wu, Zhanfeng Liu, Yilin Wang, Zhe Sun, Donglai Feng, And Juan Jiang

Electron-plasmon coupling, in which carriers are dressed by collective electronic oscillations, represents an important many-body interaction in solids. Here, using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we report the tunable electron-plasmon coupling in the layered transition metal dichalcogeni…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045121] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports tunable electron-plasmon coupling in ZrSe2-xTex using ARPES, a condensed matter physics study.
motivation: To investigate electron-plasmon coupling in layered transition metal dichalcogenides and its tunability via composition.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on ZrSe2-xTex samples.
result: Observed tunable electron-plasmon coupling as a function of Te substitution.
conclusion: The study demonstrates control over many-body interactions in this material system.

title: Generating Consensus And Dissent On Massive Discussion Platforms With A Semantic-vector Model
authors: Alfredo Ferrer, David Muñoz-Jordán, Alejandro Rivero, Alfonso Tarancón, Carlos Tarancón, And David Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): Alfredo Ferrer, David Muñoz-Jordán, Alejandro Rivero, Alfonso Tarancón, Carlos Tarancón, and David Yllanes

Reaching consensus on massive discussion networks is critical for reducing noise and achieving optimal collective outcomes. However, the natural tendency of humans to preserve their initial ideas constrains the emergence of global solutions. To address this, collective intelligence (CI) platforms fa…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014311] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a semantic-vector model for generating consensus and dissent on massive discussion platforms, applied to collective intelligence.
motivation: To address the challenge of reaching consensus in large-scale online discussions where participants tend to preserve initial ideas, hindering global solutions.
method: The authors develop a semantic-vector model that represents opinions as vectors and simulates opinion dynamics to facilitate consensus or dissent.
result: The model demonstrates effectiveness in generating consensus or dissent on massive discussion platforms, as shown in simulations.
conclusion: The semantic-vector model offers a novel approach for collective intelligence platforms to manage opinion dynamics and improve decision-making.

title: Computer Simulations Of The Stark Effect In The Helium-$β$ Complex Of Krypton In Inertial Confinement Fusion Conditions
authors: G. Pérez-Callejo, E. Stambulchik, R. Florido, And M. A. Gigosos
abstract:
Author(s): G. Pérez-Callejo, E. Stambulchik, R. Florido, and M. A. Gigosos

There is an ongoing interest in using spectroscopy in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments, where dopants such as krypton can provide vital information about the temperature and density of the imploding plasma. While the most advanced tools for calculating Stark profiles are computer simula…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015212] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses computer simulations to study the Stark effect in krypton under inertial confinement fusion conditions, focusing on plasma spectroscopy.
motivation: To improve diagnostic capabilities in ICF experiments by modeling spectral line shapes of dopant krypton.
method: Computer simulations of Stark-broadened line profiles for the helium-β complex of krypton in dense plasmas.
result: Simulated profiles that can be compared with experimental spectra to infer plasma temperature and density.
conclusion: The simulations provide a tool for interpreting ICF spectroscopy data, but the work is applied plasma physics without quantum information or thermodynamics contribution.

title: Quantum Diffusion Of Molecular Hydrogen In Liquid $\mathrm{Ne}+{\mathrm{H}}_{2}$ Mixtures: A Quasielastic Neutron Scattering Study
authors: Daniele Colognesi, Ubaldo Bafile, Milva Celli, Leonardo Del Rosso, Franz Demmel, And Martin Neumann
abstract:
Author(s): Daniele Colognesi, Ubaldo Bafile, Milva Celli, Leonardo del Rosso, Franz Demmel, and Martin Neumann

This study presents an analysis of the diffusional dynamics of [MATH] impurities in liquid Ne using quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS) and quantum dynamical simulations. By applying a Lorentzian fitting procedure, we identify two key spectral features: peak width ([MATH]) and i…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015413] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the diffusion of molecular hydrogen in liquid neon using neutron scattering and simulations, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the diffusional dynamics of hydrogen impurities in cryogenic liquids is important for fundamental physics and potential applications, but the study is purely condensed matter physics.
method: Quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS) experiments and classical/quantum dynamical simulations were performed, with data analyzed via Lorentzian fitting to extract spectral features.
result: Two spectral features were identified, and the diffusion coefficient of H2 in liquid Ne was determined, showing quantum effects at low temperatures.
conclusion: The study provides insights into quantum diffusion in simple liquids, but does not address any topics in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Realizable Entropic Lattice Boltzmann Method For high-Péclet Scalar Transport
authors: Jingsen Feng, Yang Liu, And Xu Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Jingsen Feng, Yang Liu, and Xu Chu

We present a realizable entropic lattice Boltzmann method (RELBM) for scalar transport at high Péclet (Pe) number. The method combines an ADE-tailored entropic relaxation with a nonorthogonality correction to ghost-mode damping and a strictly conservative population-space realizability limiter activ…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L013301] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for scalar transport in fluid dynamics, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To improve the stability and accuracy of lattice Boltzmann simulations for high-Péclet number scalar transport.
method: Combines an ADE-tailored entropic relaxation with a nonorthogonality correction and a realizability limiter.
result: The method achieves stable and accurate simulations at high Péclet numbers.
conclusion: The proposed RELBM is effective for high-Péclet scalar transport problems.

title: Ring Solitons And Lump Waves Of The Elliptic Cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation In Physical Coordinates
authors: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang, And Xiangyu Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang, and Xiangyu Yang

The elliptic cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (ecKP) equation is derived from the incompressible Euler equations governing surface gravity waves with nearly elliptic fronts. Using Hirota's bilinear method, this paper systematically investigates ring solitons, lump chains, and lump waves of the ecK…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014216] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ring solitons and lump waves of the elliptic cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation, which is a classical nonlinear wave equation in fluid dynamics.
motivation: To understand nonlinear wave phenomena in elliptic cylindrical coordinates, which have applications in fluid dynamics and oceanography.
method: Uses Hirota's bilinear method to derive exact solutions for ring solitons, lump chains, and lump waves of the ecKP equation.
result: Obtains explicit analytical expressions for ring solitons and lump waves, and analyzes their properties.
conclusion: The ecKP equation admits rich soliton and lump wave structures, which may be useful for modeling wave patterns in elliptic cylindrical geometries.

title: THz Dynamics Of Hydrogen Sulfide: Search For Collective Modes Of A Non-hydrogen-bonded Analog Of Water
authors: Ferdinando Formisano, Alessio de Francesco, Francesco Sacchetti, Caterina Petrillo, And Eleonora Guarini
abstract:
Author(s): Ferdinando Formisano, Alessio De Francesco, Francesco Sacchetti, Caterina Petrillo, and Eleonora Guarini

Using neutron inelastic scattering, the authors investigate the dynamics of liquid hydrogen sulfide, which is similar to water but lacks the hydrogen-bond network. While fast sound is preserved, the secondary weakly dispersive mode typical of hydrogen-bonded liquids is not detected.

#WellStructured #ClearMotivation #SoftMatterSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015412] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the THz dynamics of liquid hydrogen sulfide using neutron scattering, focusing on collective modes in a non-hydrogen-bonded analog of water.
motivation: To understand the role of hydrogen bonding in the dynamics of liquids by comparing water with its non-hydrogen-bonded analog, hydrogen sulfide.
method: Neutron inelastic scattering experiments were performed on liquid hydrogen sulfide to measure its dynamic structure factor and identify collective modes.
result: Fast sound is preserved in hydrogen sulfide, but the secondary weakly dispersive mode characteristic of hydrogen-bonded liquids is absent.
conclusion: The absence of the secondary mode confirms its association with hydrogen-bond networks, highlighting the unique dynamics of water.

title: Constraints On The Thomson Optical Depth To The Cosmic Microwave Background From The Lyman-$α$ Forest
authors: Olga Garcia-Gallego, Vid Iršič, Martin G. Haehnelt, And James S. Bolton
abstract:
Author(s): Olga Garcia-Gallego, Vid Iršič, Martin G. Haehnelt, and James S. Bolton

The imprint of the thermal history of the intergalactic medium on the Lyman-alpha forest in the spectra of distant QSOs is used to constrain the Thomson optical depth to the cosmic microwave background (CMB). The analysis suggests a mild tension of high-resolution Lyman-alpha forest data with recently suggested large values of the optical depth to the CMB, in agreement with the direct measurements by the lanck satellite.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032009] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Lyman-alpha forest data to constrain the Thomson optical depth to the CMB, finding mild tension with large optical depth values.
motivation: The Thomson optical depth is a key cosmological parameter, and recent measurements have shown discrepancies. The Lyman-alpha forest provides an independent constraint.
method: The authors analyze high-resolution Lyman-alpha forest spectra from distant QSOs to infer the thermal history of the intergalactic medium and derive constraints on the optical depth.
result: The analysis shows a mild tension between Lyman-alpha forest data and large optical depth values, consistent with direct CMB measurements.
conclusion: The Lyman-alpha forest can serve as a useful probe of the Thomson optical depth, and the results support the lower values measured by Planck.

title: Multiphoton Ionization With Three-dimensional Light Fields
authors: D. Köhnke, H.-C. Ahlswede, T. Bayer, And M. Wollenhaupt
abstract:
Author(s): D. Köhnke, H.-C. Ahlswede, T. Bayer, and M. Wollenhaupt

We employ, for the first time, bichromatic three-dimensional (3D) polarization-shaped ultrashort laser fields in atomic multiphoton ionization to create previously inaccessible free-electron angular momentum wave packets. The 3D fields are created by the noncollinear superposition of two polarizatio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033048] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the use of bichromatic three-dimensional polarization-shaped laser fields to create free-electron angular momentum wave packets in atomic multiphoton ionization.
motivation: To explore the generation of previously inaccessible free-electron angular momentum wave packets using tailored light fields.
method: Bichromatic three-dimensional polarization-shaped ultrashort laser fields are created via noncollinear superposition of two polarization-shaped pulses and applied to atomic multiphoton ionization.
result: The technique enables the creation of free-electron angular momentum wave packets that were not accessible before.
conclusion: Three-dimensional light fields offer a new tool for controlling electron dynamics in multiphoton ionization.

title: Electronic Structure Of Compressively Strained Bilayer Nickelate Thin Film
authors: Bai Yang Wang, Sebastien N. Abadi, Yidi Liu, Yu Zhang, Yong Zhong, Yijun Yu, Berit H. Goodge, Xiaoliang Zhang, Yi-Ming Wu, Ruohan Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Eun Kyo Ko, Vivek Thampy, Chun Lin, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Young S. Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Chunjing Jia, Harold Y. Author(s): Bai Yang Wang, Sebastien N. Abadi, Yidi Liu, Yu Zhang, Yong Zhong, Yijun Yu, Berit H. Goodge, Xiaoliang Zhang, Yi-Ming Wu, Ruohan Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Eun Kyo Ko, Vivek Thampy, Chun Lin, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Young S. Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Chunjing Jia, Harold Y. Hwang, and Zhi-Xun Shen

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of bilayer nickelate thin films reveals that the out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031008] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the role of out-of-plane nickel orbital bands in superconductivity of bilayer nickelates.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on thin films under compressive strain and doping.
result: The out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.
conclusion: The out-of-plane orbital band is not essential for superconductivity in bilayer nickelates.

title: Topological Defect Propagation To Classify Knitted Fabrics
authors: Daisuke S. Shimamoto, Keiko Shimamoto, Sonia Mahmoudi, And Samuel Poincloux
abstract:
Author(s): Daisuke S. Shimamoto, Keiko Shimamoto, Sonia Mahmoudi, and Samuel Poincloux

The ability of a fabric to be knitted into a textile can be determined on the basis of the topology of its pattern.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031006] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses topological defect propagation to classify knitted fabrics, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The ability of a fabric to be knitted into a textile can be determined based on the topology of its pattern.
method: The authors analyze topological defects in knitted fabric patterns to classify them.
result: The paper demonstrates a method for classifying knitted fabrics using topological defect propagation.
conclusion: Topological properties can be used to classify knitted fabrics, but the work has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction at the nanoscale is important for applications in micro- and nano-electromechanical systems.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effect of external electric fields on interlayer binding and sliding resistance in h-BN.
result: They find that electric fields can significantly modulate interlayer binding and friction, offering a means to control sliding resistance.
conclusion: External electric fields provide a viable route to dynamically control friction in layered materials like h-BN.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding anisotropy in silica films can inform better coating design.
method: The authors use experimental techniques to characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films, including anisotropy and its response to heat treatment.
result: They discover hidden anisotropy in silica films that resists standard heat treatment, which has implications for coating performance.
conclusion: The findings guide strategies for coating deposition and postprocessing to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and study molecular electronic and vibronic properties at the atomic scale.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with a nanoscale optical antenna at the tip apex to confine the electromagnetic field.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling fluorescence imaging of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for studying molecular structures and reactions at the atomic level.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
